Systems and Control.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Extended version of a paper submitted to the 2027 European Control Conference (ECC 2027). Code and data: https://github.com/tihanyidani/vehicle-sharing

Systems and Control.title: Binary Decision Process in Pre-Evacuation Behavior
Systems and Control.summary: In crowd evacuation the time interval before decisive movement towards a safe place is defined as the pre-evacuation phase, and it has crucial impact on the total time required for safe egress. This process mainly refers to situation awareness and response to an external stressors, e.g., fire alarms. Due to the complexity of human cognitive process, simulation is used to study this important time interval. In this paper a binary decision process is formulated to simulate pre-evacuation time of many evacuees in a given social context. The model combines the classic opinion dynamics (the French-DeGroot model) with binary phase transition to describe how group pre-evacuation time emerges from individual interaction. The model parameters are quantitatively meaningful to human factors research within socio-psychological background, e.g., whether an individual is stubborn or open-minded, or what kind of the social topology exists among the individuals and how it matters in aggregating individuals into social groups. The modeling framework also describes collective motion of many evacuee agents in a planar space, and the resulting multi-agent system is partly similar to the Vicsek flocking model, and it is meaningful to explore complex social behavior during phase transition of a non-equilibrium process.
Systems and Control.comment: 7 pages

Systems and Control.title: Readiness Barrier Functions: Forward-Invariant Control Authority for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation
Systems and Control.summary: Allocators that greedily maximize a readiness metric over the actuator fiber bundle of an overactuated multirotor jump between disconnected optimal strata, demanding actuator rates no motor can deliver; effort-minimizing allocators are continuous but cannot keep wrench-rate authority above any certified level. We reconcile the two by treating authority as a forward-invariant quantity: a control barrier function on the log-determinant of the drag-aware authority co-metric, enforced at torque level by a quadratic program in the allocation null space. A single design inequality makes the certified set compact and strictly interior to the actuator box; the readiness cost of a rotor deactivation is $\ln(n/(n{-}m))$ for symmetric designs. An alignment ratio states when tracking stays exact, otherwise the wrench error is $\mathcal{O}(ρ^{-1/2})$, and a robust variant handles motor-parameter uncertainty with a closed-form floor shift independent of the airframe matrix. On a hexarotor and a fully-actuated octorotor the closed-form gap matches simulation to machine precision. Over $300$ randomized missions, greedy maximization violates the certified floor in up to $51\%$ of authority-scarce missions, while the proposed filter never leaves the certified set and, in the hardest moment reversal, commits a $79\times$ smaller wrench error. The robust variant holds the floor on all $150$ perturbed plants. A high-fidelity simulation with measured propeller and motor data shows where the floor holds under unmodeled aerodynamics, electrical limits, and delay, and where it stops applying.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters

Systems and Control.title: Beyond Scalar Inertia: Frequency-Response-Based Assessment of Finite-Duration Inertial Support in Grid-Forming Converters
Systems and Control.summary: Conventional scalar inertia characterizes only the low-frequency terminal behavior of grid-forming converters (GFMs) and cannot fully predict inertial energy delivery during short-duration frequency disturbances. This letter proposes a frequency-response-based method to assess finite-duration inertial support using complex terminal power--frequency responses, such as those provided by Network Frequency Perturbation (NFP) plots. For GFMs with nonzero steady-state droop, a duration-dependent energy-equivalent inertia is defined after subtracting the ideal static-droop contribution. An exact spectral relationship is established, expressing this metric as a duration-weighted integral of frequency-dependent inertia, without requiring knowledge of the internal controller structure and parameters. The duration dependence of the metric is further shown to encode observable oscillation frequencies and damping ratios. A coefficient-decoupling GFM control with identical scalar inertia and droop across different settings is used for verification.
Systems and Control.comment: This paper has 8 pages with 8 figures

Systems and Control.title: Learned Network Dynamics for Model Predictive Traffic Signal Control under Incidents
Systems and Control.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) of urban traffic signals relies on a model of how queues respond to signal decisions, which is hard to specify and calibrate in heterogeneous networks, particularly when incidents change capacities and turning shares. Measurements add a second limitation: the controlled lanes at the stop line are often short, so queues extending upstream of them fall outside lane-level measurements. We propose GNN-MPC, a receding-horizon controller that plans with action-conditioned network dynamics learned by graph neural networks. Phase sequences are coordinated across intersections by approximate best responses, with an acceptance test that keeps the predicted cost no higher than that of the initial plan. In microscopic simulation under non-recurrent incidents, GNN-MPC reduces travel time and increases completed trips relative to all tested controllers, on a homogeneous grid and a heterogeneous 21-intersection network. Controlled comparisons on the heterogeneous network distinguish the roles of observation and prediction. With nearly as many vehicles entering the network, GNN-MPC reduces travel time by 13% relative to MaxPressure with the same upstream measurement, and GNN-MPC without the upstream representation does not reproduce its performance. Under the same traffic measurements, planner and objective, replacing the learned dynamics with calibrated store-and-forward predictors increases travel time by 31-34%. Observing hidden demand and predicting its response to control are thus complementary requirements of network-level predictive control.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages main manuscript, 26 pages supplementary material (39 pages total)

Systems and Control.title: Linear Quadratic Control With Event-Based Control Actions: Performance Beyond Periodic Control
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates linear quadratic (LQ) control for discrete-time stochastic systems to balance control performance and actuation rate. In our framework, the control input is sparse in time, and the actuation timings are determined in an event-based manner. We examine two types of problems: A sparsity-promoting regularization problem and a hard-constraint problem with a prescribed average actuation rate. Due to the combinatorial nature of these problems, finding optimal solutions is generally hard. Inspired by rollout algorithms in the context of dynamic programming, we develop a rollout-based approach to obtain tractable suboptimal policies. We show closed-loop stability and establish theoretical performance guarantees with respect to classical periodic control. Moreover, under additional conditions, we quantify the performance improvement over periodic control and prove that this improvement is strictly positive. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in balancing control performance and actuation rate.
Systems and Control.comment: 16 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control

Systems and Control.title: Active Learning of Flows from Curve Observations using Gaussian Processes
Systems and Control.summary: The active learning of real control systems requires informative roll-outs of controls. In this paper, we present a local optimization algorithm that finds the trajectory that most reduces uncertainty about the flow of a control system modeled by a Gaussian process. Therefore, we derive an approximation scheme for the posterior kernel of the Gaussian process after observing it on an entire continuous-time trajectory and establish a Pontryagin-type necessary condition for the optimizer. As the flow is unknown, the actual trajectory can deviate from the planned trajectory. We propose a trajectory planner that searches for the most informative control within a maximal allowed deviation horizon instead of a fixed time horizon. We show by trajectory-wise time rescaling that the underlying optimal control problem is equivalent to a fixed end time optimal control problem. Finally, we study both the fixed end time planner and the fixed maximum deviation planner in a numerical example and compare them with benchmarks.

Systems and Control.title: Network Traffic Dynamics in Urban Low-Altitude Air Transport with Projected-Space Macroscopic Fundamental Diagrams
Systems and Control.summary: The growth of Low-Altitude Air Transport (LAAT) systems calls for effective macroscopic modeling tools to manage dense drone traffic. The Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD) offers a promising framework for this purpose, but its conventional formulations do not directly account for the three-dimensional interactions and path deviations that characterize drone operations. To address this challenge, we introduce a projected-space framework that represents drone motion using projected speed and shortest origin-destination (OD) distances, eliminating the dependence on realized trip lengths that are unknown at trip generation. Under suitable assumptions, we prove the steady-state exactness of the projected-space accumulation-based model and establish deterministic finite-window error bounds for the trip-based estimator. The projected-space accumulation-based formulation is further extended to heterogeneous multi-class systems to accommodate different drone characteristics and operational priorities. Microscopic simulations validate the projected-space formulations under stationary and transient traffic conditions, including hysteresis. Moreover, simulations involving heterogeneous priority classes demonstrate that mixed-priority operations can improve network outflow under the investigated scenarios. These findings establish a theoretical foundation for projected-space macroscopic modeling of LAAT systems and support its application to real-time traffic estimation and future airspace management and control.

Systems and Control.title: On the Existence of Koopman Linear Embeddings for Controlled Nonlinear Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Koopman linear representations have become a popular tool for control design of nonlinear systems, yet it remains unclear when such representations are exact. In this paper, we establish sufficient and necessary conditions under which a controlled nonlinear system admits an exact Koopman linear representation in both infinite-dimensional and finite-dimensional settings. We show that such a system must be transformable into a special control-affine preserved (CAP) structure, which enforces affine dependence of the state on the control input and isolates all nonlinearities into an autonomous subsystem. We further prove that a finite-dimensional representation additionally requires this autonomous subsystem must itself admit a finite-dimensional Koopman linear model with a sufficiently-rich Koopman invariant subspace. Finally, we introduce a symbolic procedure to determine whether a given controlled nonlinear system admits the CAP structure, thereby elucidating whether Koopman approximation errors arise from intrinsic system dynamics or from the choice of lifting functions.

Systems and Control.title: Strong Functional Observability and Strong Functional Detectability: Applications to Functional Observer Design for Systems with Unknown Inputs
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates strong functional observability, strong functional detectability, and strong$^*$ functional detectability for continuous-time linear systems with unknown inputs in both the state and measurement equations. Extending Kratz's finite algebraic approach \cite{26}, zero-output trajectories are characterized through the projected kernel of a finite matrix, without differentiating the unknown inputs. This characterization yields a necessary and sufficient rank condition for strong functional observability. For strong functional detectability, a frequency-dependent rank criterion involving only the original system matrices is derived, along with an equivalent finite test based on reduced zero-output dynamics. Strong$^*$ functional detectability is then characterized by an additional algebraic rank condition, and its relationship with the existence of stable functional observers is examined. A constructive observer design procedure based on constrained Sylvester equations is also developed. Particular cases and a numerical process example illustrate the theoretical results.

Systems and Control.title: Error-Corrected Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Optimal Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Uncertainty
Systems and Control.summary: We solve open-loop optimal control problems under parametric uncertainty using a physics-informed DeepONet that returns trajectories for all sampled scenarios in one evaluation. Trained only on the residual at generic controls, the operator is reused across targets and horizons. Because a gradient-based optimizer exploits surrogate errors, we correct the prediction by one Newton step on the dynamics, computed for all scenarios and times by one parallel scan. The corrected state has a second-order error bounded by the residual alone, and the corrected cost is honest for every control up to the sampling error. On a fixed-wing UAV benchmark, the corrected operator matches the accuracy of a batched Adam solver and an Ipopt solver at equal sample size and is 8 times faster than the Adam solver on the same GPU at a few hundred scenarios and 15 times faster than Ipopt on a CPU.
Systems and Control.comment: 26 pages including appendices, 2 figures, 10 tables

Systems and Control.title: Recursive Bayesian Monitoring of SLAM Failures for LiDAR-Based UAV Navigation
Systems and Control.summary: SLAM failures remain difficult to avoid in autonomous robotic systems, and undetected failures can propagate to unsafe planning, control, and mission-level decisions. Existing monitoring strategies often depend on prior maps, estimator-internal variables, or redundant sensing, which limits their applicability to deployed and resource-constrained robots. This paper presents a scene-geometry consistency monitor for detecting geometry-manifested SLAM failures using only the geometric output of the SLAM backend. The targeted failures include cumulative drift-induced failures, abrupt misregistration failures, and backend map corruption when they become observable as inconsistency in reconstructed scene geometry. The proposed method represents revisited local regions with recursive latent voxel geometry and evaluates each current observation against a trusted continuation explanation and a weak non-propagated reference explanation. The resulting voxel-wise evidence contrasts are aggregated into a fixed-boundary monitoring signal for online failure declaration and downstream safety response. Experiments on self-collected sequences, GEODE benchmark sequences, multiple robotic platforms, and different SLAM backends show that the monitor responds to failures when they are manifested in backend scene geometry. It achieves 4/4 valid post-onset declarations with no pre-onset alarms on four self-collected sequences, detects geometry-manifested failures in all five corrupted GEODE runs while remaining alarm-free in five geometrically consistent runs, adds only 0.1--0.2\% absolute CPU load, and supports a closed-loop UAV detect--isolate--recover workflow.

Systems and Control.title: Which Data-Center Load Models Can Be Trusted? An Evidence-Graded Review of Dynamic Modeling and Validation for Large Computational Loads
Systems and Control.summary: Grid operators now require dynamic models of data centers and other large computational loads, and new ride-through rules assume that these models predict how facilities respond to disturbances. This review asks what evidence supports that assumption. We coded 160 documents, screened from 1,424 de-duplicated database and seed records plus 65 added documents, by the strongest reference object each presents, from grid-side records to simulation only. Across 19 field-evidence entries, 15 requirement documents from three continents and nine model classes, we find two comparisons of a standard library model with measured data-center events: with default parameters the model failed both, and refitting it to each event separately reduced the error but was never tested on an unseen event. Among the sources reviewed, we found no successful held-out validation of a frozen, facility-specific data-center model against an independent measured disturbance, and 25 of the 33 model-phenomenon combinations with any evidence involve no electrical measurement. The features that distinguish the new rules (memory of repeated dips, recovery within 0.5-3 s, proportional power reduction during the sag, overvoltage response) are those current phasor models cannot represent or have never been tested against. In the operator procedures examined, simulations and model-to-model benchmarks are accepted as evidence of model fidelity, unlike the measured validation required of generators, and proposed mitigations have mostly been evaluated on unvalidated facility models. We propose context-of-use gates that separate calibration from validation, release labels for model claims, a minimum validation protocol with acceptance criteria, and a research agenda.
Systems and Control.comment: 21 pages, 10 figures, 10 tables. Companion dataset included as ancillary files

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Collective Decision-Making in Signed Networks
Systems and Control.summary: Collective decision-making often unfolds in networks where cooperation and antagonism coexist. Such signed interactions arise in social, biological, and robotic systems, and can lead to qualitatively different collective outcomes: consensus, polarization, or clustering. Existing signed network models typically explain these outcomes separately, leaving open how they can emerge within a single dynamical framework. Here, we introduce a generalized Laplacian flow for bi-partitioned signed networks, a class of networks that allows cooperative and antagonistic interactions both within and across two prescribed groups. The proposed model includes an adaptive social effort state, interpreted as a leaky memory of persistent signed network disagreement, which enables bounded and nontrivial steady-states beyond classical signed Laplacian flows. We derive conditions that determine whether the network reaches consensus, polarization, or clustering based on the spectral structure of the generalized Laplacian and effective resistance matrices. The framework applies beyond structurally balanced, weakly balanced, and quasi-structurally balanced networks, and reveals how changes in signed interaction strengths can shift a network between collective decision regimes. We validate the theory on stochastic block model networks, a judicial voting network, and a U.S. senate bill co-sponsorship network. Altogether, our results provide a structural and dynamical account of how mixed cooperative and antagonistic relationships shape emergent collective behaviors.

Systems and Control.title: Performance guarantees for optimization-based state estimation using turnpike properties
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper, we develop novel accuracy and performance guarantees for optimal state estimation of general nonlinear systems (in particular, moving horizon estimation, MHE). Our results rely on a turnpike property of the optimal state estimation problem, which essentially states that the omniscient infinite-horizon solution involving all past and future data serves as turnpike for the solutions of finite-horizon estimation problems involving a subset of the data. This leads to the surprising observation that MHE problems naturally exhibit a leaving arc, which may have a strong negative impact on the estimation accuracy. To address this, we propose a delayed MHE scheme, and we show that the resulting performance (both averaged and non-averaged) is approximately optimal and achieves bounded regret with respect to the infinite-horizon solution, with error terms that can be made arbitrarily small by an appropriate choice of the delay. In various simulation examples, we observe that already a very small delay in the MHE scheme is sufficient to significantly improve the overall estimation error by 20-25% compared to standard MHE (without delay). This finding is of great importance for practical applications (especially for monitoring, fault detection, and parameter estimation) where a small delay in the estimation is rather irrelevant but may significantly improve the estimation results.
Systems and Control.comment: replaced with accepted version

Systems and Control.title: Geometry-Preserving Neural Architectures on Manifolds with Boundary
Systems and Control.summary: A growing number of neural architectures have been developed to enforce geometric constraints, including projection-based networks, exponential-map updates, and manifold neural ODEs. In this paper, we study several such architectures, with the goal of understanding their approximation-theoretic properties and trade-offs. We distinguish between architectures that enforce constraints at intermediate layers and those that enforce constraints only at the output. For projected neural ODEs on uniformly prox-regular sets, we establish stability estimates and derive universal approximation results on compact smooth manifolds, including manifolds with boundary. In particular, we establish universal approximation of measurable manifold-valued maps in the $L^2$ topology. In contrast, architectures that enforce constraints only at the output can admit uniform approximation guarantees for continuous target maps under suitable geometric assumptions. We further investigate how the choice of constraint-enforcing map, namely metric projection or the Riemannian exponential map, affects these guarantees. While both constructions can be used to preserve constraints at intermediate layers, their use at the output leads to different approximation properties. In particular, exponential-map output architectures can encounter topological obstructions to uniform approximation, motivating approximation guarantees in $L^2$. On the other hand, metric projection-based output architectures can retain uniform approximation guarantees when the constraint set has positive reach. Our study raises the broader question of when the additional complexity of enforcing constraints at intermediate layers, as motivated by neural ODE approaches, and different choices of constraint-enforcing map are justified by the resulting benefits in approximation and learning performance.

Systems and Control.title: Ace! Motion Planning of Professional-Level Table Tennis Serves with a Robot Arm
Systems and Control.summary: Table tennis, a dynamic, compact, and popular sport, has for many years received significant attention as a robotics benchmark. Most of the research has focused on the rally aspect -returning an incoming ball-requiring high-speed vision, agile motion planning, and tight closed-loop control. On the other hand, getting robots to serve competitively remains a rather unexplored research problem, which in fact requires pushing physics modeling and control to the extremes. In this work, we present the first-ever approach capable of generating official rule-compliant serves that produce ball spins of up to 550 rad/s and speeds of up to 6.7 m/s, matching and even surpassing the capabilities of elite table tennis players. In official matches against these competitors, our serves score direct points in up to 21% of attempts and push the win rate of robot-initiated rallies above 50%. The motion plans for serving are generated in simulation by combining optimization-based control and Bayesian optimization, and are executed zero-shot in open-loop on our hardware.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures

Systems and Control.title: Mode Recommendation and Dynamic Routing Guidance for Improved Trip Quality in Mixed Traffic Networks
Systems and Control.summary: Urban mixed traffic networks provide diverse mobility options, yet conventional routing guidance with fixed travel modes leaves the benefits of coordinating travel modes and route planning largely unexploited. This paper proposes an integrated mode recommendation and dynamic routing guidance framework for urban mixed traffic networks comprising private vehicles, autonomous vehicles, and buses. We formulate a dynamic trip index (DTX) that incorporates mode-specific travel time, monetary cost, and convenience, enabling consistent evaluation of trip quality across travel modes. Using this measure, we develop a mode recommendation method that selects feasible autonomous vehicle or bus services based on predicted DTX for travelers without private vehicles, while preserving service capacity for travelers with known demand. We integrate this method with dynamic routing guidance for private and autonomous vehicles to improve the average trip quality of all travelers. Simulation studies involving $1{,}500$ travelers on a real-world road network in Shanghai, China, show that the proposed framework increases the mean realized DTX by $13.01\%$ compared with dynamic routing guidance alone and by $19.68\%$ compared with fixed travel modes with preplanned routes, highlighting the value of mode flexibility in improving trip quality beyond route adaptation.

Systems and Control.title: Seabird-Aware Multi-Objective Offshore Wind Capacity Allocation: A Gippsland Case Study
Systems and Control.summary: Offshore wind planning requires balancing capital cost, wind-resource potential, and seabird exposure. We formulate a spatial tri-objective mixed-integer linear program for offshore wind capacity allocation, minimizing capital cost and modeled seabird exposure while maximizing wind-weighted capacity. Applied to Australia's Gippsland offshore wind area, the model identifies exposure reductions of 23-44% at capital-cost premiums of 0.8-6.1% across 15 wind-weighted capacity requirements. We benchmark exposure-aware optimization against 19 percentile-based exclusion thresholds. At a fixed wind-weighted capacity requirement, the 5th-percentile threshold reduces exposure by 30.1% at a 37.6% cost premium, versus at least 30.1% at a 1.4% premium with optimization. Under a fixed capital budget, exclusion screening reduces exposure by 48.2% with a 26.9% capacity loss, compared with 48.5% and 7.6%, respectively, under optimization. These results highlight the value of explicitly optimizing graded seabird exposure.
Systems and Control.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE PES General Meeting 2027

Systems and Control.title: Loop-OPF: Solver-Informed Learning for Optimal Power Flow with Inference-Time Topology Adaptivity
Systems and Control.summary: Learning for optimal power flow (OPF) has recently been advocated to accelerate OPF solutions by using a pre-trained neural network (NN) to predict directly from given inputs such as the load demand. However, existing learning-for-OPF methods largely fall short of ensuring the optimality and feasibility of their predictions. They also struggle to adapt at inference time to unseen topology scenarios, such as those caused by line or generator outages. This work puts forth Loop-OPF, a solver-informed NN that builds its layers from the iterations of the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method. Under standard convexity and regularity conditions on DC-OPF, the resultant fixed-point output of Loop-OPF is thus optimal and feasible. To speed up PDHG across diverse OPF scenarios, Loop-OPF learns certain PDHG parameters in a self-supervised manner, without any OPF solution labels. We adopt the deep equilibrium (DEQ) framework for training so that the memory cost does not grow with the number of layers. As the grid topology enters every layer as an input, the same trained Loop-OPF directly adapts to unseen contingencies without retraining. Numerical tests on the IEEE 300-bus and PEGASE 1354-, 2869-, and 9241-bus networks have demonstrated the accuracy and topology adaptivity of the proposed Loop-OPF over competing learning-for-OPF methods.
Systems and Control.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. Code: https://github.com/MFHChehade/loop-opf

Systems and Control.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
Systems and Control.summary: Detecting maneuvers of non-cooperative satellites is essential for space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid the tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, the statistics already depend on the TPM through the interaction step, and the dependence forms a feedback loop. The loop itself can raise the maneuver probability in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is decoupled from the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geostationary target. In the simulation, the reference filter keeps its sensitivity after small maneuvers, whereas the NIS of the coast sub-filter of the IMM is reduced by the interaction step. RD-IMM detects 1-3 m/s maneuvers, which the fixed-TPM IMM rarely detects, with a false-declaration rate below the false-alarm probability of 0.05 set for the reference filter. In the first hour after the 1-3 m/s maneuvers, RD-IMM also has a lower position error than the compared filters.
Systems and Control.comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Code: https://github.com/hanes1207/RD-IMM

Systems and Control.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
Systems and Control.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet existing AI safety frameworks primarily define, categorize, or govern AI risk rather than proposing implementable models and methods for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk throughout an AI system's operational lifetime. This paper proposes CENTRY, a probabilistic framework that enables continual risk estimation, monitoring, and regulation of a deployed AI system from its interactions with its environment. The framework models AI risk as arising from three intrinsic sources: datasets, hardware resources, and models/algorithms. A structured latent-variable model is developed in which the latent representation is decomposed into a fast interaction subspace that captures the evolving AI--environment dynamics and three slow latent subspaces that encode the long-term risk states associated with the dataset, hardware, and model components. Rather than requiring a ground-truth risk label at every time step, the component-risk states are treated as latent variables and are learned by maximizing a variational evidence lower bound, optionally informed during training and continual refinement by evidence-supported behavior--cause records. The resulting framework unifies continual probabilistic inference, online risk estimation, and adaptive risk regulation in an implementable architecture. Under the explicit assumptions stated for the corresponding results, we establish formal guarantees spanning safety, learning, inference, and operations, including finite-horizon and asymptotic risk-budget compliance, regret and convergence bounds for adaptive regulation, consistency and identifiability of component-risk ratings, and detection-delay, false-alarm, containment, and computational-complexity characterizations.

Systems and Control.title: Real-Time 250-kHz Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Using a Jetson AGX Orin
Systems and Control.summary: High-performance optical coherence tomography (OCT) relies on desktop workstations for data acquisition, reconstruction, and visualization, limiting integration into compact imaging systems. We evaluated whether an embedded GPU platform could sustain real-time operation of a 250-kHz spectral-domain OCT instrument without a desktop computer. A custom C++/CUDA OCT engine running on a NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB was developed and integrated with a 2048-pixel spectrometer, Camera Link frame grabber, and galvanometer scanner, and compared against an RTX A4500 workstation under the same scan protocols. Both systems maintained mean B-scan processing latency well below the corresponding B-scan acquisition intervals. Although the RTX A4500 workstation achieved lower reconstruction latency, Jetson eliminated explicit host-to-device transfer and exhibited more consistent processing latency. Furthermore, the measured active wall power was 67 W for the Jetson and 155 W for the workstation, corresponding to approximately 2.3 times greater wall-energy efficiency for the Jetson. In a separate 62.6-min GUI-enabled measurement, the Jetson processed 800,000 B-scans without frame loss while maintaining real-time reconstruction and visualization. These results demonstrate that embedded computing can support high-speed OCT acquisition, processing, and control while reducing wall-power demand and computing-platform size.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables

Systems and Control.title: Belief-Driven Quantum Magnetometer Control for GPS-Denied Navigation
Systems and Control.summary: Autonomous vehicles increasingly need to navigate without satellite positioning. Magnetic anomaly navigation (Mag-Nav) with quantum magnetometers offers a passive, unjammable fix, but the low size-weight-and-power (SWaP) sensors that small drones can carry are weak, and they are operated open loop at a fixed setting. Interferometric (Ramsey) magnetometers face a trade-off: long interrogation times are more sensitive but become ambiguous when the expected field is uncertain. The navigator's own position belief, pushed through the anomaly map, predicts that field. We close this loop. The filter's predictive field distribution sets the Ramsey phase and interrogation time at every epoch, through a closed-form rule that moves between an ambiguity limit and a decoherence limit. We evaluate it on real U.S. Air Force flight data (real tracks, inertial drift, measured fields, and a survey map tested 18 months after it was flown), with only the Ramsey sensor modelled. Against fixed-setting baselines, 63 of 72 independent flight windows favour belief driven sensing ($p = 2 \times 10^{-11}$). Error falls by 20-27% for low-SNR sensors and 30-44% for mid-contrast sensors. An ablation separates the two ingredients. Phase alignment drives the gain in steady flight, and the rule matches the best fixed setting without the hindsight tuning that setting requires. After a lost start, interrogation time adaptation is essential, cutting median error by 37-42% even against hindsight-tuned phase-aligned settings. Gains are small for high-quality sensors with accurate maps. On an IBM superconducting qubit, the rule's interrogation time stays within $1.3\times$ of the empirical optimum. Coupled with information-aware routing, belief-driven sensing lowers mission error by 15-40%.
Systems and Control.comment: 9 pages

Systems and Control.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
Systems and Control.summary: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. We present ScaleEvals, a scalable reset-free protocol that evaluates policies through continuous physical play across a robot fleet. A VLM AutoPrompter generates scene-grounded tasks with difficulty estimates, language prompts, and skill tags, enabling performance analysis across diverse rollouts. A VLM AutoGrader assesses task progress, achieving 90.7% agreement with human graders. Scores are aggregated via a soft-win Bradley-Terry model, while tag-stratified ANOVA provides interpretable capability diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical autonomous rollouts on DROID and YAM, ScaleEvals achieves 23.0 net rollouts/hr per station while reducing active human labor by 98%. By ranking five SOTA generalist policies, ScaleEvals correlates with held-out manual evaluation ranking on DROID (r=0.94, rho=0.90, p=0.018), and remains internally consistent on a second embodiment, YAM (r=0.839, rho=0.80). Beyond aggregate rankings, we observe behavioral compositionality: recombining verb-, skill-, and object-conditioned evidence predicts policy order on unseen prompts. Across 10 tasks and 240 prospective physical rollouts, we recover three-policy orderings of 96% pairwise concordance, demonstrating ScaleEvals can predict not just which policy leads, but where rankings reverse.

Systems and Control.title: Frequency-Domain Identification of Passive Discrete-Time Systems via Sequential Convex Programming
Systems and Control.summary: This paper considers identification of passive discrete-time linear time-invariant systems from frequency-response data. A prescribed passivity margin and spectral-radius bound are enforced by a descriptor-form linear matrix inequality that is affine in the system realization matrices and storage certificate. A damped Gauss--Newton sequential convex programming method jointly refines the realization matrices through strongly convex semidefinite subproblems, with Armijo backtracking decreasing the fitting error while preserving both guarantees at every iterate. For unstructured identification, the number of decision variables is reduced without changing the attainable transfer matrices by normalizing the descriptor and certificate matrices and restricting the dynamics matrix to upper Hessenberg form. Numerical results on randomized passive plants show that the proposed method achieves the lowest mean frequency-response fitting error among several passivity-enforcing methods, at both full and reduced model orders.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Includes additional simulation results

Systems and Control.title: Loadability Assessment for Large-Load Integration: From Repeated Power Flow Tracing to Historical Trajectory Transfer
Systems and Control.summary: Integrating large data-center loads requires utilities to evaluate voltage-stability loading margins under different generation and demand conditions. Continuation power flow (CPF) traces P--V curves through successive prediction and correction steps, but related assessments can repeatedly reconstruct similar nonlinear behavior. Reusing an operating point as an initial guess does not capture the subsequent voltage response. This paper proposes a continuation method that transfers finite segments of historical power flow (PF) trajectories. Each segment is aligned with the present state and continuation direction, supplementing the CPF tangent predictor with previously computed nonlinear curve shape. Short Newton tests evaluate compatibility with the present PF equations, and an attention-based selector combines their results with network conditions, loading patterns, and recent continuation states. Numerical correction and fold refinement determine accepted solutions and the loading limit. The analysis bounds prediction error through differences in trajectory curvature and establishes sufficient conditions for local correction and branch preservation. Studies on modified IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems under renewable-generation and data-center load variations demonstrate reduced online computation and higher observed recovery of specified continuation solutions than Adaptive CPF. For loading-limit assessment, paired online speedups are 4.88--21.62$\times$ over Adaptive CPF and 1.53--4.77$\times$ over holomorphic embedding with arc-length parametrization (HEAP) across the tested scenarios.

Systems and Control.title: Scheduling of Variable-Speed Pumped Storage via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Variable-speed pumped storage hydropower (VSPSH) plants modulate power continuously in both generation and pumping, a match for the net-load ramps of rising wind and solar. Their flexibility is bounded by hydraulics rather than by a power rating, so the deliverable power range shifts with net head and excludes small outputs entirely. This paper addresses bidding and dispatch for such a plant across a two-settlement market with a hierarchical reinforcement-learning formulation. Its two layers are circularly dependent: a real-time (RT) bid is defined only against a cleared day-ahead (DA) commitment, and the DA reward only against an RT dispatch policy. Our proposed feasibility-constrained domain randomization breaks the cycle by training the RT layer on generated deliverable DA schedules before any bidding policy exists; the DA layer then optimizes against that frozen RT behavior, and the two alternate. Learning a policy at once profitable and deliverable is obstructed by the nonconvex operating region: penalizing infeasibility competes against the revenue the offer earns, discouraging an undeliverable offer without preventing one. We therefore pursue safety through action-space modification rather than through the reward, combining action masking of the bid space, projection of each commitment before settlement, and replacement by a fail-safe controller. Over 48 out-of-sample days it earns $3,313/day more than an equivalent penalty formulation while holding undeliverable commitment at a median of zero, which the penalty formulation does not, and no ablation improves on it without giving up deliverability or the storage target.

Systems and Control.title: Algebraic Observability for Power System Dynamic State Estimation
Systems and Control.summary: Existing observability methods for dynamic state estimation are developed for ordinary differential equation (ODE) models, whereas power systems are naturally described by differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Applying these methods generally requires a DAE-to-ODE transformation, usually Kron reduction, which may obscure the role of algebraic variables and network constraints. This paper presents an algebraic observability framework that operates directly on nonlinear power system DAEs and preserves their structure. A Jacobian rank test constructed from the model relations and their successive derivatives certifies the algebraic dependence of differential and algebraic variables on the known inputs and measurements. A reduced prolongation that differentiates only the stator relations keeps the number of latent indeterminates fixed as the prolongation order grows, which makes the test scalable. We establish the relationship between this rank test and hyper-regularity, an alternative framework for algebraic observability, and show that algebraic observability relates to local observability. We demonstrate algebraic observability on a single-machine decentralized setup, the WSCC 9-bus 3-machine system, and the IEEE 39-bus 10-machine system. The 39-bus test, with 257 latent indeterminates, completes in about 30 s.

Systems and Control.title: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters
Systems and Control.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential for learning complex robotic behaviors from demonstrations. However, learning safe behavior directly from data requires extensive coverage of safety-critical situations, which is often impractical in real-world settings. Test-time safety filters provide an alternative by correcting unsafe actions during deployment, but these interventions can drive the robot into states poorly covered by the training data, thereby degrading task performance. We introduce InteR-VLA, an intervention-robust framework for VLAs that leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden task-relevant state coverage and maintain competence under safety interventions. By better aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment under the same data budget, our approach mitigates intervention-induced distribution shift while preserving task performance. Real-world experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show that InteR-VLA maintains safety, increases Safe Success Rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal policies, and consistently outperforms nominal-data training on both evaluated VLAs.

Systems and Control.title: Control and Cryptosystem Co-Design for Encrypted Nonlinear Multi-Agent Coordination
Systems and Control.summary: A cloud that must not see the agents' states can steer them on data encrypted under CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic. Its stored estimate admits only so many multiplications before a refresh that costs time and error, and every decrypted command is flooded with noise of a mandated size, constraints no controller designed in exact arithmetic meets. For networked agents with polynomial dynamics, we prove one closed-loop bound tying the controller and the cryptosystem in both directions. If the exact loop contracts on a region, the encrypted loop stays within a certified radius of it, set by the per-cycle and refresh errors, the refresh interval, the flooding and the delay. The errors and the bound's probability are derived from the library's circuits, not measured. Inverted, the bound turns the tolerance and a failure-probability target into the refresh interval, and with it the precision, security parameters and period. Conversely, costs shape the realization: a tracing backend tallies any pipeline's operations before a ciphertext exists, and evaluating the prediction about each agent's reference holds the released error below its sixteen-agent level. A full satellite-train mission encrypted at 128-bit security ran inside its certified radius, and the certificate holds across six graphs and at 32, 64 and 128 agents. Security enters the design twice, in time and precision. The cryptosystem is therefore part of the control design, derived from the same specification and certified by the same guarantee as the controller.

Systems and Control.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration for Informative Sim-to-Real Adaptation
Systems and Control.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) can transfer agile robot skills from simulation to the real world, but closing the sim-to-real gap by domain randomization requires expert physics knowledge, and simulator calibration from real data typically targets a few hand-picked parameters. Even then, simulators miss real-world effects, and environments reconstructed from onboard perception inherit sensing errors that limit policy improvement. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), which uses conditional flow matching to calibrate simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity domains online during deployment. Residual fidelity captures sim-to-real dynamics discrepancies and perception-induced environment uncertainty. NFC operates in a latent space so that realistic environments can be sampled from the inferred posterior for real-to-sim policy fine-tuning. The framework is informative: the pretrained policy is fine-tuned only when an anomaly is detected, sequential NFC seeds its proposal from the simulation-pretrained estimator, and a hallucination policy modulates posterior uncertainty following optimism in the face of uncertainty. NFC attains the most accurate posteriors among established simulation-based inference methods on five robots with up to 39 physical parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain. On a wheeled robot with a broken wheel axle deployed on snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC raises success on rough terrain from 26% to 70% and reduces orientation jerk by 88%. Code and videos will be released upon publication.
Systems and Control.comment: The code and demonstration videos are available at https://www.youwei-yu.com/nfc/

Systems and Control.title: Neural Fidelity Calibration: Turning Field Anomalies into Simulation Fine-Tuning
Systems and Control.summary: A policy that transfers from simulation to a lab robot often fails in the field. Calibrating a simulator from real-world data typically targets only a few hand-picked parameters, and even calibrated simulators fail to capture unmodeled dynamics, while environments reconstructed via onboard perception inherit sensing noise and artifacts. We propose Neural Fidelity Calibration (NFC), a framework based on conditional flow matching that infers online, directly from a robot's execution data, both simulator physical parameters and residual fidelity - the remaining dynamics discrepancy and the gap between perceived and true environment geometry. A simulation-trained anomaly detector determines when recalibration or fine-tuning is required using onboard sensory signals alone, while an exploration policy actively modulates posterior uncertainty using optimism in the face of uncertainty. Across five robot platforms with up to 39 calibrated parameters and a 128x128 residual terrain map, NFC achieves the most accurate posterior distributions compared to established simulation-based inference baselines. In physical outdoor experiments with a wheeled robot suffering an axle failure across snow, mud, and wet grass, NFC increases rough-terrain navigation success from 26% to 70% while reducing orientation jerk by 88%.
Systems and Control.comment: The code and demonstration videos are available at https://www.youwei-yu.com/nfc/

Systems and Control.title: Control Barrier Functions in Motion Control
Systems and Control.summary: Projection-based controllers (PBCs) have significant engineering success in industrial high-precision motion systems by restricting their input-output behavior to performance-enhancing sector-sets thereby overcoming fundamental limitations of linear control. The projection results in continuous control signals, but their vector fields are discontinuous, potentially causing unwanted excitation of higher-order dynamics in the plant. Inspired by these projected controllers and the recent interest in control barrier functions (CBFs), we propose a new class of CBF-based motion controllers that (i) can mimic and exceed the performance benefits demonstrated by PBCs and (ii) have continuous dynamics thereby resulting in smooth control signals. We specialize our novel CBF-based control design to integrator dynamics, essentially connecting to a projected integrator, called Hybrid Integrator-Gain System (HIGS), thereby introducing CBF-HIGS. We analyze the CBF-HIGS's behavior using a describing function analysis, which reveals improved phase characteristics and a favorable trade-off in higher-order harmonic distortion compared to HIGS. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that CBF-HIGS enhances disturbance attenuation and reduces the excitation of higher-order harmonics compared to HIGS due to its continuous vector field, without compromising robustness properties. The paper provides the first use of CBFs for performance improvement of mechatronic motion systems.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology (TCST)

Information Theory.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
Information Theory.summary:
We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ
  \lesssim_α
  ν^{1/α}
  \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

Information Theory.title: SC-LDPC Codes Over $\mathbb{F}_q$: Minimum Distance, Decoding Analysis and Threshold Saturation
Information Theory.summary: We investigate random spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) code ensembles over finite fields. Under different variable-node edge-spreading rules, the random Tanner graphs of several coupled ensembles are defined by multiple independent, uniformly random monomial maps. The two main coupled ensembles considered are referred to as the standard coupled ensemble and the improved coupled ensemble. We prove that both coupled ensembles exhibit asymptotically good minimum distance and minimum stopping set size. Theoretical and numerical results show that the improved coupled ensemble can achieve better distance performance than the standard coupled ensemble. We introduce the essential preliminaries and analytical tools needed to analyze the iterative decoding threshold of coupled ensembles over any finite field. We consider a class of memoryless channels with special symmetry, termed q-ary input memoryless symmetric channels (QMSCs), and show that, for these channels, the distribution of channel messages (in form of probability vectors) likewise exhibits this symmetry. Consequently, we define symmetric probability measures and their reference measures on a finite-dimensional probability simplex, analyze their foundational properties and those of their linear functionals, endow their respective spaces with metric topologies, and conduct an in-depth study of their degradation theory. Based on our analytical framework, we establish a universal threshold saturation result for both of the coupled ensembles over a q-ary finite field on QMSCs. Specifically, as the coupling parameters increase, the belief-propagation threshold of a coupled system saturates to a well-defined threshold that depends only on the underlying ensemble and the channel family.

Information Theory.title: Revisiting Unicity Distance: A Channel Transmission Perspective and Its Limits
Information Theory.summary: This paper revisits the classical notion of unicity distance for substitution ciphers from an information-theoretic perspective. We frame simple-substitution encryption as a noisy transmission channel, in which the plaintext is the message, the unknown key is the noise, and the attacker is the receiver. Using typical sets to motivate the notion of meaningful plaintexts, we apply the channel coding theorem to blocks encrypted with independent fresh keys. We show that a block length exceeding $H(K)/D$ permits reliable communication at the language's entropy rate using suitably chosen codebooks across many blocks. This provides a channel transmission interpretation of the classical unicity-distance formula. We then test how well this formula describes plaintext recovery when the message is a passage from six known novels. More than $99\%$ of the passages are uniquely identifiable at 18 letters, well before the classical estimate of about 28. N-gram language models, based on the frequencies of short letter sequences, predict the recovery probabilities much more closely. In this experiment, the classical formula misses the recovery transition, while a more detailed model of the language captures it.

Information Theory.title: The many faces of multivariate information
Information Theory.summary: Total correlation, dual total correlation, S-information, and O-information are usually presented as a family of related but distinct measures of higher-order dependency in complex systems. Here we show that three of them (S-information, dual total correlation, and negative O-information) are in fact collinear samples of a single affine function of an integer parameter $k$, which we call $Δ^{k}$. This form provides a well-defined notion of interaction order: fragility under single-variable deletion. We then show that $Δ^{k}$ has a conjugate partner, $Γ^{k}$, which arranges S-information, total correlation, and O-information into a dual spectrum of redundancy rather than synergy. Finally, we relax the implicit maximum-entropy reference distribution built into all of these measures, defining a Kullback-Leibler generalization $Λ^{k}(P\|Q)$ that measures higher-order information gain when updating from an arbitrary prior to an arbitrary posterior.

Information Theory.title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
Information Theory.summary: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

Information Theory.title: Adaptive Entanglement Distillation
Information Theory.summary: Quantum network applications impose a variety of requirements on entanglement resources in terms of rate, fidelity, latency, and more. The repeaters in the quantum network must combine good methods for entanglement generation, effective entanglement distillation, and smart routing protocols to satisfy these application requirements. In this work, we focus on entanglement distillation in a linear chain of quantum repeaters. While conventional approaches reuse the same distillation scheme over multiple hop lengths after entanglement swaps, we propose a novel adaptive quantum error correction (QEC) scheme that boosts end-to-end metrics. Specifically, depending on the network operating point, we adapt the code used in distillation over successive rounds to monotonically increase the rate while also improving fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy using three codes, with parameters [[9,1,3]], [[9,2,3]], [[9,3,3]], and a new performance metric, efficiency, that incorporates both overall rate and fidelity. Since the minimum input fidelity for QEC-based distillation is high, we then extend our study to include non-QEC-based purification protocols, specifically DEJMPS since it outperforms others. We compare the performance of end-to-end DEJMPS against adapting from DEJMPS to QEC once DEJMPS improves the initial fidelity to the threshold for QEC. Through a refined efficiency metric, we illuminate the regime where QEC is beneficial. These results provide a detailed outlook for entanglement purification and distillation in first and second generation quantum repeaters.
Information Theory.comment: v3 reflects the manuscript accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Quantum Engineering (IEEE TQE)

Information Theory.title: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading
Information Theory.summary: A codeword spans a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks. The receiver knows the gains and the transmitter knows only their law. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, we require the decoding error probability to decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. When does outage predict the achievable rate? If block length grows faster than the number of antennas, outage gives the limiting optimal rate. If both grow to infinity at a fixed positive ratio of block length to array size, outage strictly overestimates the limiting rate. We determine the critical ratio above which positive rates are possible. For sufficiently large finite ratios, we find the exact limiting rate over all codes satisfying a total energy constraint on each codeword. The leading rate loss is inversely proportional to the ratio. Its coefficient depends on Gaussian channel dispersion at the most likely fade causing outage and on how quickly the outage rate decreases as the required error exponent increases. In the long-block limit, equal power loses rate on every window of three or more blocks under stationary first-order autoregressive fading with positive lag-one correlation. In a different three-block channel with identical marginal gains, tightening the reliability requirement first makes it optimal to leave the middle block unused and later to use it again.

Information Theory.title: The Sample Complexity of Distributed Simple Binary Hypothesis Testing under Information Constraints
Information Theory.summary: This paper resolves two open problems from a recent paper, arXiv:2403.16981, concerning the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing under information constraints. The first open problem asks whether interaction reduces the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing. In this paper, we show that sequential interaction does not help. The second problem suggests tightening existing sample complexity bounds for communication-constrained simple binary hypothesis testing. We derive optimally tight bounds for this setting and resolve this problem. Our main technical contributions are: (i) a one-shot lower bound on the Bayes error in simple binary hypothesis testing that satisfies a crucial tensorisation property; (ii) a streamlined proof of the formula for the sample complexity of simple binary hypothesis testing without constraints, first established in arXiv:2403.16981; and (iii) a reverse data-processing inequality for Hellinger-$λ$ divergences, generalising the results from arXiv:1812.03031 and arXiv:2206.02765.
Information Theory.comment: The proof of Theorem 7 is revised. This version is accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions of Information Theory

Information Theory.title: On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we study the group randomness of 0-1 real sequences derived from a binary linear code through the spectral anlysis of a suitable normalization of the Gram matrix of a $p \times n$ random matrix whose rows are uniformly and independently drawn from those 0-1 real sequences, where $p/n \to y \in (0,1)$. We show that as $n \to \infty$, its empirical spectral distribution converges to the Marchenko-Pastur law at a rate at least of the order $n^{-1/4}$ with high probability as a consequence of eigenvalue interlacing with the $\pm 1$ sequence model studied in 2021 [14], and that its largest eigenvalue, after centering by $p+1+y$, converges to a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance $4y$, provided that the dual distance of the code is at least 5. Furthermore, we show that when this is the only control parameter, the lower bound 5 is optimal in general by demonstrating that the binary Simplex codes and first-order Reed-Muller codes of dual distance 3 and 4 respectively do not possess either property.

Information Theory.title: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications
Information Theory.summary: We study balanced Boolean functions parameterized by two-to-one mappings of the forms $P(x+x^2)$ and $P(x+x^{-1})$, where $P$ is a sparse permutation polynomial with generalized Niho-type exponents. First, for $q=2^m$ with $m$ even, we determine the complete four-valued Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function parameterized by $Q(x+x^2)$, where $Q(x)=x(1+x^{q-1}+x^{2(q-1)})$. We then generalize a permutation polynomial studied by Gupta and Sharma to the parameterized family $P_λ(x)=x^{3q-1}+λx^{2q}+λx^2$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. We prove that $P_λ$ is a permutation polynomial if and only if either $λ=0$, or $λ\ne0$ and $X^3+X+λ^{-1}$ has no root in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, the number of admissible parameters is $(q+2)/3$ when $m$ is even and $(q+4)/3$ when $m$ is odd. Thus, admissible parameters exist for every $m\geq2$, and approximately one-third of the elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$ yield permutation polynomials. For every admissible parameter $λ$, we determine the complete Walsh distribution of the balanced Boolean function $f_λ$ parameterized by $P_λ(x+x^2)$ and prove that this distribution is independent of $λ$. For $m\geq3$, these functions have the five-valued Walsh spectrum ${q,0,-q,-2q,-3q}$, while for $m=2$ the spectrum degenerates to four values. As applications, their supports yield projective minimal binary five-weight codes, sets with five hyperplane intersection numbers, and regular cubelike Cayley graphs with six distinct eigenvalues. Finally, for mappings of the form $P(x+x^{-1})$, we construct an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions with simple explicit trace representations.

Information Theory.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
Information Theory.summary: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.
Information Theory.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures, accepted by IEEE Internet of Things Journal

Information Theory.title: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions
Information Theory.summary: Let $q=2^m$ with $m\geq 2$. We develop a geometric approach to the classification of locally-APN Niho-type power functions over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. Our approach begins with a characterization of $\mathbb{F}_q$-homogeneous functions: the conditions $D_F(a,F(a))=q$ and $D_F(a,b)\leq 2$ for every $a\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^*$ and $b\neq F(a)$ hold if and only if the projective graph of $F$ is a $(q+1)$-arc in $\mathrm{PG}(3,q)$. For Niho-type power functions, this differential condition is equivalent to the locally-APN property. Applying the classification of $(q+1)$-arcs and the description of their stabilizers, we prove, for $m\geq 3$, that $F_s(x)=x^{s(q-1)+1}$ is locally-APN if and only if $s\equiv(2^k+1)^{-1}\pmod{q+1}$ for some $1\leq k\leq 2m-1$ satisfying $\gcd(k,m)=\gcd(2^k+1,q+1)=1$. Together with the known case $m=2$ and the sufficient condition of Xie et al., this gives the complete classification and confirms the conjecture of Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

Information Theory.title: New Nonbinary Quantum Codes from Quasi-Twisted Codes with Scalar and Matrix Twists
Information Theory.summary: We construct quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields from one-generator index-$2$ quasi-twisted codes and from codes invariant under a $2\times2$ matrix twist, via the symplectic construction. For one-generator quasi-twisted codes, we give direct proofs of the dimension formulas and of matrix and polynomial tests for symplectic self-orthogonality. When the same scalar twist $λ$ acts on both blocks, we show that $λ^2\ne1$ gives only quantum distance $1$. Thus, in this construction, distance greater than $1$ requires $λ=\pm1$, corresponding to quasi-cyclic and quasi-negacyclic codes. We also study determinant-one $2\times2$ matrix twists. For twists given by companion matrices, we describe the resulting codes and their symplectic duals by polynomials over the base field. When the associated quadratic is irreducible over $\mathbb F_q$, these codes correspond to Hermitian constacyclic codes over the quadratic extension. With a rank criterion for the minimum distance and standard propagation rules, our explicit constructions present quantum codes that improve the recorded minimum-distance lower bounds for $164$ distinct entries in Grassl's tables of quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields.

Information Theory.title: User-Irrepressible Sequences for Multiple-Packet Reception
Information Theory.summary: This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes based on protocol sequences for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception (MPR) channels without feedback or synchronization of sequence phases. Each user schedules its transmissions according to a preassigned periodic binary sequence. A sequence set has the user-irrepressible property with MPR capability $γ$ ($γ$-UI) if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of the relative cyclic shifts. We propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) for arbitrary MPR capability $γ\geq 2$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified CRT-based construction framework for $γ$-UI sequences over this full range, without requiring conflict-avoiding codes with prescribed parameters. We establish the $γ$-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations and show that suitably selected subsets support one additional active user without increasing the sequence length. We also derive exact average individual delay expressions over all possible cyclic shifts and extend the delay analysis to $γ$-UI sequence sets obtained from conflict-avoiding codes.

Information Theory.title: Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing
Information Theory.summary: We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size $d$ is to be identified among $N$ items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling $T=Θ(d\log N)$ for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime $d=Ω(\log^2 N)$. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with $T\le (1/\ln 2+\varepsilon)d\log N$ tests for any $\varepsilon>0$, in the admissible regime $N=q^k$ for some prime power $q = Θ(d)$ and integer $k \ge 2$. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap remains except in the sparse regime $d = N^{o(1)}$.

Information Theory.title: Secure Distributed Matrix Multiplication with Precomputation
Information Theory.summary:
We consider secure distributed matrix multiplication, in which a user computes the product of two matrices with the help of honest-but-curious servers, any $T$ of which may collude. Using the outer-product partition, the matrices are split into $K$ and $L$ blocks and hidden by random masks. Assuming the user has precomputed the products of the random matrices, we develop methods that use this precomputation to reduce the number of servers required.
  Polynomial codes are designed through degree tables, whose distinct entries count the servers. We show that precomputation can reduce the minimum number of servers by designing degree tables specifically for this setting. For Gap Additive Secure Polynomial (GASPr) codes, we give a precise formula and show that it is monotone in the chain length $r$, so only the extremes GASP_small and GASP_big matter. We also prove lower bounds attained by GASP_small in several regimes. Consequently, any fraction of colluding servers below one can be tolerated, compared to the threshold of one half without precomputation, and the order of the total computational complexity decreases when the colluders are a fixed fraction of the servers. We show that no existing construction uses fewer servers than the better of GASP_small and GASP_big once the mask products are precomputed.
  We introduce Gap-Reduced Additive Secure Polynomial (GRASP) codes, which retain a single interval for the mask degrees while selecting the information degrees carefully. For $K = T = 4$ and every $L \geq 3$, we give an explicit GRASP code that uses one fewer server than every GASPr code and is within two servers of optimal. For large $T$, the configuration becomes an integer packing problem independent of $T$, and the number of servers saved by GRASP over GASPr grows quadratically in $K$ and $L$.

Information Theory.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
Information Theory.summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

Information Theory.title: UNILocPro: Unified Localization Integrating Model-Based Geometry and Channel Charting
Information Theory.summary: In this paper, we propose a unified framework (called UNILocPro) that integrates model-based geometry and channel charting (CC) for localization via a single massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) base station (BS) in mixed line-of-sight (LoS)/non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scenarios. Specifically, based on LoS/NLoS identification, an adaptive activation between the model-based and CC-based methods is conducted. Aiming for unsupervised learning, information obtained from the model-based method is utilized to train the CC model, where a pairwise distance loss (involving a new dissimilarity metric design), a triplet loss (if timestamps are available), a LoS-based loss, and an optimal transport (OT)-based loss are jointly employed such that the global geometry can be well preserved. To reduce the training complexity, we propose a low-complexity implementation (called UNILoc), where the CC model is trained with self-generated labels produced by a single pre-training OT transformation, which avoids iterative Sinkhorn updates involved in the OT-based loss computation. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed unified frameworks achieve significantly improved positioning accuracy compared to both model-based and CC-based methods. Notably, UNILocPro with timestamps attains performance on par with fully-supervised fingerprinting despite operating without labelled training data. It is also shown that the low-complexity UNILoc can substantially reduce training complexity with marginal performance degradation.
Information Theory.comment: To appear in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Information Theory.title: From description to design: Automated engineering of complex systems with desirable emergent properties
Information Theory.summary: Across the sciences, researchers have developed hundreds of statistics that describe the collective behavior of complex systems.
