These statistics are typically used passively, to describe a system after the fact, so it is rarely learned whether the patterns captured actually matter. The problem of engineering systems that display desirable emergent properties is a less developed area, as the very nature of emergent phenomena challenges the typical bottom-up approach to engineering. Here we propose a top-down approach, re-purposing the large number of descriptive statistics as objective functions in an optimization pipeline. Since this method lets a collective property instantiated directly, it makes long-standing correlational questions amenable to experimentation. We demonstrate this concept on four models taken from four different areas of science: a Kuramoto coupled-oscillator model (physics), a Wilson-Cowan network of excitatory and inhibitory processes (neuroscience), an SIRS pandemic spread model (epidemiology), and an echo-state network (machine learning). In each case, we take measures commonly used to describe behavior and feed those descriptive statistics back into the system to sculpt desirable macro-scale properties into the fundamental generative dynamics. We find that this approach is successful across domains and systems, and the inclusion of ``emergent" measures can actually improve the ability of some systems to perform tasks. We argue these threads can be unified into a general practice of emergent engineering that combines traditional task-oriented, bottom-up approaches to engineering with top-down guidance of collective, emergent properties to build resilient, capable, complex systems.

Probability.title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
Probability.summary: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

Probability.title: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
Probability.summary: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

Probability.title: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
Probability.summary: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $\varphi$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.

Probability.title: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
Probability.summary: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $Σ=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $Σ_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|Σ_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $Σ$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-Σ$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.

Probability.title: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

Probability.title: Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion: Definition and Fundamental Properties
Probability.summary: We introduce the $n$-th order multifractional stable motion ($n$-MFSM), a symmetric $\al$-stable process ($\al\in(1,2]$) whose Hurst parameter is a function $H(t)\in(n-1,n)$, obtained by a Taylor regularization of order $n\ge1$ of the kernel of the linear multifractional stable motion. It contains the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of Kawai as the special case of constant $H$, and, up to explicit deterministic factors, the linear multifractional stable motion ($n=1$) and the moving-average $n$-th order multifractional Brownian motion ($\al=2$). We prove existence, give the harmonizable representation in the Gaussian case, and show that, if $H$ is of class $\mathcal C^n$ near $t_0$, the rescaled $n$-th order increments at $t_0$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to the $n$-th order increments of the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of index $H(t_0)$. We then study the dependence structure through the codifference. For $s>0$ fixed and $H(t)\to H_+$ with $(H(t)-H_+)\log t\to0$, we obtain the exact power rate of $τ(X(s),X(t))-c_0(s)$ as $t\to\infty$ away from the boundaries of three explicit parameter regimes, where $c_0(s)=\|X(s)\|_\al^\al$ if $\al<2$ and $c_0=0$ if $\al=2$; the constants are explicit and of known sign when $n\ge2$ or $\al=2$, while for $n=1$ and $\al<2$ part of one regime yields only convergence or a modified constant. In particular this codifference does not tend to zero when $n\ge2$. For the $n$-th order increments with constant $H$, whose codifference asymptotics were obtained by Kawai, we give a self-contained proof with the sign of the leading constants and treat the boundary cases of the long-range dependence criterion $H\ge n-1/\al$; for a non-constant Hurst function this criterion is extended only to functions that are eventually constant.

Probability.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
Probability.summary: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.
Probability.comment: V2: The OU-K model now uses the full cosine schedule, without time truncation

Probability.title: The $H^{2|2}$-model and the Anderson model with Cauchy potential: similarities and a conjectured relation
Probability.summary: We highlight strange similarities between the Anderson model with Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$ and the $H^{2|2}$ supersymmetric sigma field with initial non local conductances proportional to $W_{x,y}=λ^2\left \vert \left (-Δ-E+ iλ)\right)_{x,y}^{-1}\right\vert^2$ where $Δ$ is the discrete Laplace operator. More precisely, looking at the Brownian interpolation of both, we show that they follow very similar equations. Motivated by that we investigate the different phases of the $H^{2|2}$-model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with conductances $rW$ for some $r>0$ and show that whatever $r>0$ the $H^{2|2}$-model displays localized and delocalized phases which are coherent with what is expected or proved for the Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$. Finally, we propose a conjecture that compares key quantities of the two models and would imply existence of delocalized regime for the Anderson model with Cauchy potential in dimension $d\ge 3$.

Probability.title: Exit-Pair Rigidity, Neutral Restart Laws, and Inverse Reconstruction in One Dimension
Probability.summary: For an absorbed one-dimensional diffusion, we characterize two-point restart laws preserving the exit-side probability for every independent renewal clock. Spectral identities establish rigidity under spatial accumulation, while explicit nonsymmetric potentials admit neutral pairs. We distinguish midpoint Dirichlet isospectrality from Weyl reflection rigidity and prove a second-order high-energy asymptotic under local continuity, giving two necessary asymmetry conditions for neutral pairs. Two complete exit profiles at distinct reset rates identify diffusivity and drift; a finite birth-death analogue admits exact Jacobi criteria and reconstruction from four channel functions.
Probability.comment: 18 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Code (C++ and Lean 4): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24402657

Probability.title: How communities help epidemics persist
Probability.summary:
Empirical studies show that communities such as households and workplaces strongly influence how an infection spreads and how long it persists in a population. To understand this effect, we study the contact process (SIS epidemic model) on random intersection graphs and their local weak limit. In the contact process, infected vertices recover with rate $1$ and transmit the infection to each of their neighbours with rate $λ$. The random intersection graph is defined on a finite population; each individual belongs to a random number of communities (captured by a membership distribution), and each community has a random size (captured by a community size distribution). Communities are all taken to be complete graphs. The local weak limit of the random intersection graph, called the branching community tree, has complete graphs arranged in a tree structure.
  Letting $M$ have the membership distribution and $K$ have the community size distribution, we prove that if either $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]=\infty$ for all $c > 0$ or $\mathbb E[e^{cK\log K}] = \infty$ for all $c > 0$, then for all $λ> 0$, the infection on the finite graph survives for exponentially long with high probability, and on the local limit graph, it survives forever with positive probability. On the other hand, if for some $c > 0$ both $\mathbb E[e^{cM}]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[e^{K\log(cK)}]<\infty$ hold, then the process with small $λ$ dies out in the local limit graph. We compare these findings with known results on the behaviour of the contact process on a "community-free" random graph with similar degree distributions, to highlight the impact of communities.

Probability.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
Probability.summary: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.

Probability.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
Probability.summary: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/β$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $β=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

Probability.title: No roughening transition for the Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 4$
Probability.summary: Consider the Ising measure $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}$ on $Λ_n:=([-n,n]^{d-1}\times[-n,n-1]) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ at inverse temperature $β$ with all plus boundary condition at heights $z \geq 0$ and all minus boundary condition at heights $z<0$. Let $β_c(d)$ be the critical inverse temperature. For every $d \geq 4$ and $β>β_c(d)$, we prove that $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}(σ_0)$ has a positive lower bound independent of $n$. As a consequence, any Dobrushin state (i.e., a subsequential limit of $μ_{Λ_n,β}^{\text{Dob}}$) is not translation invariant for those $(d,β)$, and thus there is no roughening transition when $d \geq 4$.

Probability.title: Brownian Twins of Fractional Diffusion Models
Probability.summary: We study generative diffusion models in which the Brownian motion driving the noising dynamics is replaced by fractional Brownian motion or by a Markovian approximation of it. In the standard linear-Gaussian setting, we show that the memory of the noise acts only through the noise schedule. To every such model we associate a Brownian twin, a classical diffusion model with the same drift and an explicit variance schedule, and prove that everything the reverse-time process knows about the data is contained in one linear statistic which follows the reverse-time equation of the twin. Consequently, the denoising score matching losses of the two models coincide for every network, and access to the full path or to the augmented state does not reduce the loss. Moreover, we characterize when the reduction degenerates and describe where the reduction ends.

Probability.title: $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
Probability.summary: We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

Probability.title: A sharp dimension barrier for uniform Gaussian approximations
Probability.summary:
We establish a universal dimension barrier for Gaussian approximations based on $n$ i.i.d. random vectors $X_1,...,X_n$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Fix $m\in(2,\infty)$ and consider mean-zero distributions with coordinate variances bounded from below by a fixed positive constant and coordinatewise $m$th absolute moments bounded from above by a fixed constant. We show that \begin{equation*}
  \log d=o\left(n^{(m-2)/(3m-2)}\right) \end{equation*} is necessary for any sequence of statistics to admit a Gaussian approximation to its distribution uniformly over this distribution class and all hyperrectangles. Here, the centered Gaussian target is required to have the covariance or correlation matrix of the observations. The obstruction includes randomized procedures and already holds for coordinate maxima. Conversely, for $m\in(2,4]$, we establish that this growth condition on $d$ is sufficient for the distribution of a vector of centered and scaled quantile-winsorized means to obey a Gaussian approximation with covariance target without further restrictions on the covariances of the observations or knowledge of $m$. Thus, the dimension barrier is sharp in this moment range. For $m\in(4,\infty)$, the same statistic attains the barrier up to a power of $\log n$.

Probability.title: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
Probability.summary: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\toτ$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(τ/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.
Probability.comment: This version updates the funding acknowledgements and includes minor edits in wording

Probability.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
Probability.summary: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.
Probability.comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. This paper is aimed at theoretical physicists. In particular, not all arguments are mathematically rigorous

Probability.title: Solvers for a Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
Probability.summary: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. Under our assumptions we derive two solvers: a martingale solver (inspired by the deep FBSDE solver studied in recent literature), and a min-max solver leveraging a Hilbert space orthogonality condition to enforce the martingale property. We obtain a posteriori error bounds for both solvers. The min-max solver avoids the need to approximate the class of square integrable martingales directly (which in practice is usually done by parameterizing a stochastic integral representation), at the expense of weakening the topology with respect to which one should expect convergence of an approximate solution.

Probability.title: Stopping models closed under pgf composition, and the stability of randomly stopped model extensions
Probability.summary: Statistical model transformations based on randomly stopped sums, maxima, and minima are widely used to extend statistical models by introducing an additional parameter. We characterize the finite-dimensional positive stopping models for which these randomly stopped sum and extreme transformations act as statistically stable (idempotent) model extensions. Stability requires the underlying stopping model to be closed under pgf composition. We prove that any finite-dimensional, connected, positive stopping model closed under pgf composition necessarily forms a family of random variables whose pgfs commute. Using the associated Koenigs function, we establish that these models form a statistical manifold admitting a global, one-dimensional parametrization $θ= \Pr(N=1) \in (0, θ_*]$, in which the probability mass at $i$ is a polynomial in $θ$ of degree at most $i$. Within this class, we further establish a duality between those models containing the identity variable (the ones yielding statistically stable extensions) and the set of all probability distributions supported on the positive integers. By providing numerous examples of stopping models closed under pgf composition, we clarify the assertion that, under certain conditions, the only stopping model that is so is geometric.

Probability.title: Asymptotic formulas for products of Poisson distributions
Probability.summary:
In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour of the product tail probability $
  \mathbb{P}(ξ_1\cdotsξ_N \geqslant n), $ where $\{ξ_1,\ldots,ξ_N\}$ is a finite collection of independent Poisson random variables with positive parameters $λ_1,\ldots,λ_N$. We derive a refined Laplace-type asymptotic formula for the tail probability, based on Stirling's logarithmic approximation, a constrained saddle-point method, the Lambert function, and a careful evaluation of the constrained Gaussian prefactor. This yields an explicit approximation with an $O(\log n)$ remainder term in the exponent.

Probability.title: Numerical Analysis of 2D Stochastic Navier--Stokes Equations with Transport Noise: Regularity and Spatial Semidiscretization
Probability.summary: This paper establishes a strong convergence rate for the spatial finite element discretization of a two-dimensional stochastic Navier--Stokes system with transport noise and no-slip boundary conditions on a convex polygonal domain. The main challenge arises from the lack of spatial $D(A)$-regularity of the solutio (where $A$ is the Stokes operator), which prevents the direct applicability of standard error analysis techniques. Under a smallness assumption on the transport noise, for a MINI-element spatial semidiscretization, we establish a strong convergence rate of order $h^{\varrho} \log\big(1 + \frac{1}{h}\big)$, where $\varrho \in (0,1/2)$.

Probability.title: Random pullback attractors for evolution equations with nonlocal perturbations and fractional Brownian motion
Probability.summary: We study semilinear evolution equations with time-nonlocal perturbations of \(μ\ge0\) and additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter \(H\in(1/2,1)\). Under the regularity assumptions and a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity, we establish global existence and uniqueness in the concept of pathwise mild solutions. We overcome the difficult in which the solution family lacks the cocycle property, by shifting the corresponding stochastic Volterra equation on a weighted space, and then the continuous random dynamical system follows. Based on a dissipativity condition, we establish the pullback random asymptotic compactness and the compact random pullback attractor \(\mathcal A_μ\). Finally, we prove that the family of random pullback attractors \(\mathcal A_μ\) is upper semicontinuous at \(μ=0\) almost surely.

Probability.title: Large deviations and conditional laws for a time-integrated logarithm of averaged Gaussian squares
Probability.summary: Systems with identical instantaneous power distributions can have very different probabilities of insufficient service over a fixed interval. We study the lower tail of the time-integrated logarithm of a weighted mean of $d$ independent squared Gaussian paths as $d\to\infty$. A global entropy inequality resolves the nonconvex service constraint, identifies the unique Gaussian minimizer and controls the nonlinear likelihood weight far from that minimizer. Combined with a joint local limit, it yields sharp probabilities at fixed internal thresholds and conditional path laws: a Fredholm determinant enters the leading factor, and tangential Gaussian fluctuations are independent of the exponential service deficit. The approximations extend through moderate deviations to the central scale. For stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck paths, cancellation in the radial likelihood expansion yields relative error $O(d^{-1})$ on compact positive parameter families with proportions and saddles separated from zero. Genuine temporal covariance attenuation by correlation kernels for a type of positive limiting proportion increases the lower-tail rate, yet the finite-sample outage distributions cross near typical service. Thus one-time power distributions alone do not determine reliability.

Probability.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
Probability.summary: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.
Probability.comment: 37 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. v2: terminology unified (kinetic Fokker-Planck), no change in the results

Probability.title: A Class of Coupled Forward-Backward Systems Under General Filtrations
Probability.summary: We consider a class of coupled-forward backward systems defined on a general probability space assumed only to satisfy the usual conditions. We obtain existence and uniqueness results for arbitrary finite time horizons.

Probability.title: Contractive kinetic Langevin samplers beyond global Lipschitz continuity
Probability.summary: In this paper, we examine the problem of sampling from log-concave distributions with (possibly) superlinear gradient growth under kinetic (underdamped) Langevin algorithms. Using a carefully tailored taming scheme, we propose two novel discretizations of the kinetic Langevin SDE, the tamed exponential euler scheme and tamed OBABO and we show that they are both contractive and satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality. Building on this, we establish a series of non-asymptotic bounds in $2$-Wasserstein and total variation distance between the law reached by each algorithm and the underlying target measure. In particular, we show that both algorithms can reach almost optimal $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-1})$ convergence rate in Wasserstein and Total Variation distances, and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-\frac{1}{2}})$ under increased Hessian local regularity for the tamed OBABO scheme.
Probability.comment: Improved convergence rates from previous version, fixed some gaps in proofs, included TV rates

Probability.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
Probability.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.
Probability.comment: Updated on November 20, 2026. Revisions that do not affect the results, such as corrections to the eDNA analysis methodology, were made

Probability.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
Probability.summary: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.
Probability.comment: 21 pages, 8 pedagogical figures (hopefully). The first two versions of this arXiv submission (uploaded in May and August 2025) contained the material of two papers. It has now been split into this version and arXiv:2611.25081

Probability.title: Energy-constrained Brownian motion
Probability.summary: For reflected Brownian motion in an interval of length $N$, we consider the first time at which the length of time since the most recent visit to the boundary reaches $M$; this random `lifetime' comes from the interpretation in which the Brownian motion has a finite energy capacity $M$, uses energy at unit rate in the interior, and gets its energy replenished up to $M$ on every visit to the boundary. We prove distributional asymptotics for the lifetime in three different regimes depending on the relative growth of $N$ and $M$; these one-dimensional results parallel results in the random walk case by Wade and Grinfeld. We also present some initial results on the multidimensional version of the problem, for one scaling regime in the case of a ball, and conjectures on the behaviour in general domains.

Probability.title: Asymptotic expansions for normal deviations of random walks conditioned to stay positive
Probability.summary: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ having i.i.d. increments with zero mean and finite variance. We continue our study of asymptotic expansions for local probabilities $\mathbf P(S_n=x,τ_0>n)$, which has been started in \cite{DTW23}. Obtained there expansions make sense in the zone $x=o(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log^{1/2} n})$ only. In the present paper we derive an alternative expansion, which deals with $x$ of order $\sqrt{n}$.
Probability.comment: 40 pages, updeted version after accepting in journal

Probability.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
Probability.summary: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_σ$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(Ω, \mathcal F_0; L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.

Probability.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
Probability.summary: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.
Probability.comment: 37 pages. V3 features an improved constant in the isoperimetric inequality Proposition 5.1

Probability.title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
Probability.summary:
How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $ρ$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses.
  For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(ρ-2)/ρ$; at $ρ=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $ρ>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs.
  At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.
Probability.comment: 48 pages, 9 figures. Ancillary files contain exact certificates for 381 polygon-rate instances and verification scripts

Probability.title: Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
Probability.summary: We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota (2024), our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.
Probability.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures. Fixed typos in abstract

Probability.title: A Dynamical Theory of LoRA in Continual Learning
Probability.summary: Despite the widespread use of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), little is known about its dynamics in continual learning and the mechanisms by which low-rank updates affect catastrophic forgetting. We provide an asymptotically exact dynamical characterization of LoRA in a solvable two-task teacher-student model. In the high-dimensional online-learning limit, we derive a closed system of ordinary differential equations for a finite set of macroscopic order parameters, yielding exact expressions for the generalization errors throughout both the initial Task 1 learning phase and the subsequent LoRA fine-tuning on Task 2. The theory quantitatively matches finite-dimensional simulations and exposes two characteristic effects of LoRA: when the first-task representation is not yet specialized, low-rank adaptation reduces interference with features learned on the first task, but its initialization slows adaptation to the second task. Building on this mechanistic picture, we analyze a state-dependent masking strategy that freezes hidden units carrying the strongest first-task representations and restricts adaptation to the complementary subspace. This structural partitioning markedly reduces forgetting, while preserving plasticity on the new task. Our framework further clarifies the role of adapter rank: transfer improves only up to the intrinsic dimensionality of the target task and saturates beyond it, while forgetting continues to grow with rank. These results provide a dynamical and geometric account of how low-rank adaptation organizes information across sequential tasks, and are qualitatively reproduced on sequential MNIST and CIFAR-100 using a shallow network and ResNet-18, respectively.
Probability.comment: v2: added a deep multi-task benchmark (ResNet-18, Split CIFAR-100), random-selection controls, a rank sweep at a fixed number of frozen units, and a deeper analysis of the specialized regime

Probability.title: On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study the group randomness of 0-1 real sequences derived from a binary linear code through the spectral anlysis of a suitable normalization of the Gram matrix of a $p \times n$ random matrix whose rows are uniformly and independently drawn from those 0-1 real sequences, where $p/n \to y \in (0,1)$. We show that as $n \to \infty$, its empirical spectral distribution converges to the Marchenko-Pastur law at a rate at least of the order $n^{-1/4}$ with high probability as a consequence of eigenvalue interlacing with the $\pm 1$ sequence model studied in 2021 [14], and that its largest eigenvalue, after centering by $p+1+y$, converges to a Gaussian random variable with mean 0 and variance $4y$, provided that the dual distance of the code is at least 5. Furthermore, we show that when this is the only control parameter, the lower bound 5 is optimal in general by demonstrating that the binary Simplex codes and first-order Reed-Muller codes of dual distance 3 and 4 respectively do not possess either property.

Probability.title: Vanishing bond-percolation threshold implies vanishing contact-process threshold
Probability.summary: We show that for any infinite, locally finite and connected graph $G$ and $p\in(0,1/2]$ the survival probability of the contact process with infection rate $λ\ge20p$ is at least $3/4$ times the bond percolation probability with retention probability $p$. In particular, $λ_c(G)\le20\,p_c(G)$ whenever $p_c(G)<1/2$, and $p_c(G)=0$ implies $λ_c(G)=0$. The proof uses a submartingale built from percolation clusters on finite balls. We contrast this with the SIR epidemic, in which every vertex is infected at most once, and for which there are graphs with $p_c(G)=0$ on which the SIR epidemic dies out almost surely for every infection rate.
Probability.comment: This note is not intended for journal publication and was produced with substantial assistance from the AI systems Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT/Codex (OpenAI). The authors have checked all statements and proofs and take full responsibility for the contents

Probability.title: Stochastic Differential Equations on the Simplex
Probability.summary: We propose a framework for simplex-valued diffusion processes, formulated as solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by antisymmetric Brownian motion. Our edge-wise representation includes the multivariate Jacobi processes and the general class of continuous simplex-valued polynomial diffusions. Also, it allows bounded, locally Lipschitz state-dependent drift rates and edge weights. We establish weak solutions, as well as global strong existence and pathwise uniqueness for strictly positive initial states under a sufficient boundary non-attainment condition.

Probability.title: The Number of Real Eigenvalues of a Random Sign Matrix
Probability.summary: Let $R_n$ count the real eigenvalues of an $n\times n$ matrix with independent uniform $\pm1$ entries. We prove that $R_n/\sqrt n$ converges in $L^1$ to $\sqrt{2/π}$. In particular, $R_n=Θ(\sqrt n)$ with probability tending to one, as conjectured by Vu.

Probability.title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
Probability.summary: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+2e$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

Probability.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
Probability.summary: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(Ω,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(Ω), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(ξ) Z_Y(dξ), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For α>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(Ω, B_α^2(C^-)), where B_α^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(ω,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_α= B_α^2(C^+) \oplus B_α^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(Ω, B_α). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. In L^2(Ω, B_α), we apply stochastic pre-orthogonal adaptive Fourier decomposition (SPOAFD) to U_+ and U_- separately, using normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman spaces as dictionaries. The adaptive selection is determined by the spectral density. Finally, using the Poisson kernel and SPOAFD expansions, we establish weak mean-square convergence of the original process against test functions in C_c^\infty(R).

Probability.title: Rapid Mixing of Glauber Dynamics for Monotone Systems via Entropic Independence
Probability.summary:
We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics on monotone systems. For monotone systems satisfying the entropic independence condition, we prove a new mixing time comparison result for Glauber dynamics. For concrete applications, we obtain mixing time bounds from specified extremal configurations: $\tilde{O}(n)$ for the random cluster model induced by the ferromagnetic Ising model with consistently biased external fields, and $\tilde{O}(n^2)$ for the bipartite hardcore model under the one-sided uniqueness condition, where $n$ is the number of variables in the corresponding models, improving the best known results in [Chen and Zhang, SODA'23] and [Chen, Liu, and Yin, FOCS'23], respectively.
  Our proof combines ideas from the stochastic dominance argument in the classical censoring inequality and the recently developed high-dimensional expanders. The key step in the proof is a novel comparison result between the Glauber dynamics and the field dynamics for monotone systems.
Probability.comment: v2: fixed a gap in the random cluster model proof (dependence on mu_min) and an incorrect reversibility assumption; main results unchanged

Probability.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
Probability.summary: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

Probability.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
Probability.summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

Probability.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
Probability.summary: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

Probability.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
Probability.summary: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

Probability.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
Probability.summary:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

Probability.title: Boolean threshold functions, neuron capacity, and memory retrieval
Probability.summary: How much information can a single neuron remember? How many memories can neural networks retrieve without creating false memories? These questions are related to a basic question: how many Boolean threshold functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_0+\langle a,x\rangle)$, $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, are there? In this paper, we show that the number $T_n$ of distinct Boolean threshold functions is \[ T_n=2\binom{2^n-1}{n}\bigl(1+O(n^{-99})\bigr). \] Equivalently, the capacity of a single threshold neuron is $n^2-\log_2(n!)+1+O(n^{-99})$ bits, improving the $O(n)$ error term in the result of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi to $O(n^{-99})$. To prove this, we show that, for $1\le r\le n-1$, and $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ are chosen at random from $\{-1,1\}^n$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left\{ \langle v_1,\ldots,v_r\rangle\cap\{-1,1\}^n =\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_r\} \right\} =1-O(n^{-99}). \] In the context of the Kanter--Sompolinsky Hamiltonian for memory retrieval, this identifies $r=n-1$ as a sharp threshold, at which, for almost every collection of $r$ memories, the only ground states are these memories and their negatives, confirming a weaker form of the Kalai--Linial--Odlyzko conjecture. It also settles a recent open problem posed by M. Anthony on the specification number of Boolean threshold functions. In addition, we show that, for every $1\le r\le n-1$, \[ \mathbb P\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\text{ are linearly dependent}\} =2\binom r2\,2^{-n}+O\!\left(2^{-n}e^{-cn}\right), \] confirming a conjecture of Kahn--Komlós--Szemerédi.
Probability.comment: Lean verification is available at https://github.com/XinyuanXie-hub/BooleanThreshold and in the Palomar entry at https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000020&version=1

Probability.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
Probability.summary:
We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process.
  In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms.
  Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

Probability.title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
Probability.summary: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

Probability.title: Skew-Symmetric Factor Models
Probability.summary: The paper introduces and analyzes a factor model for (real) skew-symmetric data, which arise naturally in directed flows and in pairwise comparisons used for rankings. Working within a signal-plus-noise framework, we analyze spectral inference and establish a BBP-type phase transition in signal strength. Under Gaussian noise, we derive joint eigenvalue fluctuation limits. Above the separation threshold, the estimated signal strength is asymptotically normal whenever the population strength has multiplicity one. For a general multiplicity $k$, the joint limiting fluctuations of the corresponding sample eigenvalues above the threshold are given by the eigenvalues of a scaled $k\times k$ Gaussian unitary ensemble matrix. The skew-symmetric structure induces paired eigenspaces, and we characterize the canonical angles between the population and sample eigenspaces. Below the threshold, the corresponding largest sample eigenvalue converges to the edge of the semicircle law, with fluctuations governed by the Tracy--Widom $F_2$ distribution, in contrast to the $F_1$ law familiar from real symmetric models. The approach is illustrated through financial and demographic applications.

Probability.title: Differential Equations for Macdonald's Hypergeometric Series
Probability.summary:
We study differential equations for certain multivariable hypergeometric series, introduced by Macdonald in the 1980s, which generalize hypergeometric functions of matrix argument due to Bochner and Herz. Such equations are well studied in the one-variable case, where they serve to characterize the classical hypergeometric functions $_p F_q(z)$ and provide a route to many of their key properties. Accordingly, Macdonald asked for a similar characterization for the multivariate series. This problem, however, has remained open. Differential equations are known only for a handful of cases with $p\leq 3$ and $q\leq 2$.
  In this paper we give a complete solution to Macdonald's problem. In the multivariable case there are \emph{two} series $_p F_q(x)$ and $_p F_q(x,y)$, depending on $p+q+1$ parameters and one or two sets of variables, $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $y=(y_1,\dots,y_n)$. We give differential equations characterizing both series, for all values of $p$ and $q$. The proof involves several new ideas in the theory of symmetric functions, especially Jack polynomials and interpolation polynomials.
Probability.comment: v2: Revised the title and abstract and expanded the introduction. Clarified the proof of Theorem B, corrected several formulas, and updated the references. 38 pages

Probability.title: Fermat costs and path-dependent first-passage percolation
Probability.summary: We introduce a path-dependent and space-inhomogeneous first-passage percolation (FPP) model in the continuum. Inspired by Euclidean FPP, it is defined through a sample of points drawn from a common density function on a Riemannian manifold. In Euclidean FPP, the cost of each step in a discrete path is given by its length raised to the power $α>1$. In our model, the power $α$ increases as the path progresses, governed by a control mechanism. Consequently, the resulting percolation cost is not a distance. However, we prove a shape theorem showing that, as the number of points goes to infinity, the percolation costs converge to deterministic space-time integrals along curves in the manifold. This limit defines a quasi-distance with the property that traversing a curve from a high-density region towards a low-density one is generally cheaper than in the reverse direction; thus highlighting its potential use in machine learning applications.

Probability.title: Epidemic random model under vaccination regime and non-permanent immunity driven by time-changed Levy noise
Probability.summary: A random version of the Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Vaccinated (SIRV) epidemic model with non-permanent immunity and a population of non-constant size is studied. The compartments satisfy a system of differential equations in which the contact rate is a random coefficient, and the contact rate itself is driven by a stochastic differential equation with time-changed Levy noise. This noise is constructed from a conditional Brownian motion and a doubly stochastic Poisson random field, both governed by a stochastic clock. When the clock is independent of the Brownian and Poisson components, the two parts of the noise are a time-changed Brownian motion and a time-changed Poisson random measure. The equation for the contact rate decouples from the compartment equations and enters them as a random parameter, which allows the compartments to be treated pathwise. The existence, uniqueness, and positivity of the global solution are proven, and the basic reproduction number of the model is shown to be random. Furthermore, sufficient conditions for extinction and persistence in mean of the disease are derived. The conditions are expressed in terms of the parameters of the model and two long-run characteristics.

Probability.title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
Probability.summary: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. For two contacts we obtain a closed-form criterion for when response feedback strictly improves on every static design. An unequal-cost example with a computer-certified exact saddle shows that the same conclusion can hold without symmetry, even though no product prior is least favourable there. A correlated prior shows that outcome feedback can still reduce Bayes risk, so the equivalence is genuinely minimax. In this idealized setting, the results support responsive survey designs that adapt to paradata but not to outcomes.
Probability.comment: 16 pages. Ancillary files contain an exact rational certificate and a standard-library Python checker for the computer-assisted part of Section 6

Probability.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
Probability.summary: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler--Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball and a Lipschitz test function, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + Σ^2 h^2 + h^4 \log^2\frac1h)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $Σ$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4 \log^2\frac1h$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $Σ^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error.

Differential Geometry.title: Taut and Dupin Submanifolds (Updated Version)
Differential Geometry.summary: This is an updated version of a paper by the author which originally appeared in 1997. The original paper was a survey of the closely related fields of taut and Dupin submanifolds of Euclidean space, and this updated version includes many results in the field that have appeared since the publication of the original version. The emphasis is on stating results in their proper context and noting areas for future research, and relatively few proofs are given. The important class of isoparametric hypersurfaces is surveyed in detail, as is the relationship between the two concepts of taut and Dupin. Also included is a brief introduction to submanifold theory in Lie sphere geometry which is needed to state many known results on Dupin submanifolds accurately. The paper concludes with detailed descriptions of the main known classification results for both Dupin and taut submanifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
Differential Geometry.summary: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

Differential Geometry.title: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenböck curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient of complex projective space with its Fubini-Study metric. This also holds using the second intermediate Ricci curvature in place of sectional curvature. More generally, a nonzero Betti number in the range controlled by an intermediate Ricci bound forces local symmetry. We also derive sharp Hodge eigenvalue estimates and a scalar spectral vanishing criterion.

Differential Geometry.title: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
Differential Geometry.summary: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

Differential Geometry.title: On Gromov's Volume Growth Theorem
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M^n$, $n\ge3$, be complete and noncompact, with nonnegative Ricci curvature. We derive the estimate \[ Vol (B(p,R))\le \frac{C_n}{c}(1+R)^αR^{n-2} \] from the radial lower bound $Scal(x)\ge c(1+d(p,x))^{-α}$, where $c>0$ and $0<α<2$. The proof extends Ge's heat-covariance argument by retaining the heat occupation of the set where a chosen scalar threshold fails. Varying that threshold with the source time makes all entropy errors integrable and yields the exact exponent $n-2+α$, without a logarithmic loss. We give explicit examples showing that this exponent is optimal and also allow failure of the curvature lower bound on a set of finite volume.

Differential Geometry.title: Disjoint Divisors and Splitting Rigidity under Nonnegative Orthogonal Ricci Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $X^n$ be a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal Ricci curvature. We prove that if $X$ admits two nonzero effective divisors with disjoint supports, then its universal cover splits. As applications, we study the MRC fibration of $X$, and show that when the dimension of a general fiber is $n-1$, the universal cover of $X$ splits as a product of a simply connected Riemann surface and a compact rationally connected manifold. When $X$ is rationally connected, it splits off a $\Pj^1$-factor if and only if it contains two disjoint nonzero effective divisors. Together with the results of Zhang and Zhang, these conclusions give a unified description of the universal cover for all possible dimensions of the general MRC fiber. We also establish metric existence criteria for certain projective bundles.

Differential Geometry.title: Elliptic regularization for anisotropic mean curvature flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We develop an elliptic regularization scheme for anisotropic mean curvature flow in arbitrary dimension, with general norms serving as surface tension and mobility. Starting from a non-fattening set of finite perimeter, we prove that the vertically rescaled minimizers and translating solitons converge in the Kuratowski sense to the unique generalized level-set motion, and locally in BV to the flat flow. Furthermore, by implementing a restarting and matching procedure prior to curvature identification, we establish for the limit flat flow a coupled phase-transport and surface-energy dissipation balance valid for arbitrary, possibly crystalline, anisotropies. When the surface tension is continuously differentiable (away from the origin) and strictly convex, we further prove that the flat flow is a BV flow and that its reduced boundary defines a unit-density anisotropic Brakke flow. To our knowledge, this is the first construction of unit-density anisotropic Brakke flows valid for every strictly convex differentiable surface tension, in arbitrary dimension and for prescribed non-fattening initial data, without assuming perimeter convergence.

Differential Geometry.title: Riemannian Curvature Functionals for de Rham Spectral Triples
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute mixed Clifford residue functionals for the Hodge-de Rham operator in even dimensions. A symbol-composition calculation recovers the Riemann and Einstein tensors and yields two ordered curvature functionals with the same classical limit. For specified truncation products on warped collars, we evaluate all five boundary cases and prove that the curvature-recovering antisymmetrizations have no boundary correction. We extend the constructions to spectral data equipped with two one-form actions. Explicit noncommutative torus and finite-direction examples distinguish the functionals and exhibit failures of module balancing and Riemann symmetries. A conformal example shows that a naive exterior lift need not recover classical curvature. The additional structures and limitations of each extension are stated explicitly.

Differential Geometry.title: Geometric Dissipation Structures and the Koszul Form
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper investigates the canonical Koszul one-form at the interface of Jean Marie Souriau's Lie group thermodynamics and Paulette Libermann's symplectically complete foliations to describe geometric dissipation. On the Poincaré half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ under $SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, the equivariant momentum map level sets form a regular Libermann foliation framing the conservative boundaries. The Koszul-derived dissipative vector field acts strictly transverse to these leaves, driving a metriplectic flow that breaks Noether conservation laws and generates entropy.
