Quantum wise, we develop Berezin quantization on para-Kähler symmetric spaces, where the Koszul potential acts as a weight determining state density via the Fisher Souriau metric, and formalize Kostant's geometric quantization using the real dual polarizations of a bi-Lagrangian web.

Differential Geometry.title: Banchoff Curvature and Realisation Moduli of Piecewise-Affine Arrangement Immersions
Differential Geometry.summary: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-Müller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.
Differential Geometry.comment: 46 pages, 3 figures. Companion paper to "Antipodal parity and second-chaos Regge curvature on random hyperplane arrangements" v2: added arXiv identifier for the companion paper (arXiv:2611.25129)

Differential Geometry.title: Projectively Flat Spherically Symmetric Sprays of Constant Curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study projectively flat spherically symmetric sprays of constant curvature. We derive a system of equations that is equivalent to the constant-curvature condition for such sprays and solve it to obtain a complete classification of the projective factor \(p(r,s)\) into four explicit families. We further show that the sprays induced by projectively flat spherically symmetric Finsler metrics of constant flag curvature \(K=0\), \(K=-1\), and \(K=1\) are all special cases of our classification, thereby confirming that the sprays induced by these constant-flag-curvature Finsler metrics are fully contained in our framework.

Differential Geometry.title: The Kähler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for Kähler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete Kähler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is Kähler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman Kähler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is Kähler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.
Differential Geometry.comment: 15 pages. Final version. To appear in Bull. Sci. Math

Differential Geometry.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space. In particular, our results disprove Atiyah's conjecture on configurations of points and its hyperbolic analogue.
Differential Geometry.comment: 20 pages, 1 figure. Earlier version on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22663662

Differential Geometry.title: Uniqueness of $L_{p}$ Minkowski Problem in the supercritical range near the affine exponent
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the isotropic $ L_{p} $-Minkowski problem. The equation is affine invariant at the exponent $ p = -n-1 $, where all origin-centered ellipsoids with the volume of the unit ball are solutions, and it is known that the unit sphere is the only solution for $ p \in (-n-1, 1) $. We prove uniform $ C^{0} $ estimates for all solutions in the supercritical range $ p < -n-1 $. This allows us to prove a key spectral estimate of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator on solutions. We then utilize the Rayleigh quotient method with position vectors as test functions for the operator adapted from Ivaki-Milman to prove uniqueness in the range $ p \in (-n-1- δ_{n}, -n-1) $ for some $ δ_{n} > 0 $.

Differential Geometry.title: Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
Differential Geometry.summary: We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact Kähler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.

Differential Geometry.title: Diameter Growth of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ under Cliff Metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: Cliff metrics are right invariant Riemannian metrics on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ introduced by Nielsen and his collaborators in the geometric approach for gate complexity in quantum computations. In this paper, we compute the exponential growth rate for the diameter of $\mathrm{U}(2^N)$ equipped with cliff metrics as $N \rightarrow \infty$. We prove that if the norm of most generalized Pauli matrices are sufficiently large, this growth rate coincides with the growth rate of maximal gate complexity obtained by Knill.

Differential Geometry.title: Torsional Rigidity and Spherical Deficit for a Dirichlet Problem on Riemannian Manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this work, we study several inequalities related to a Dirichlet problem on Riemannian manifolds whose Ricci curvature is bounded from below. First, we establish sharp inequalities involving the torsional rigidity and show that equality forces the domain to be isometric to a geodesic ball in a space form, with no symmetry assumption on the ambient manifold. Next, we derive an integral identity associated with the same Dirichlet problem, which measures the spherical deficit arising in this context. In particular, we apply this identity to Einstein manifolds, where it yields a rigidity result and a bound for the weighted spherical deficit in terms of the deviation of the normal derivative from a constant.
Differential Geometry.comment: 22 pages. v2: The model-manifold assumption in Theorem A is removed: equality in the torsional rigidity estimates now characterizes geodesic balls in space forms on any manifold with Ricci curvature bounded below, via an Obata-type lemma. Several statements corrected and typos fixed. Comments welcome

Differential Geometry.title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

Differential Geometry.title: A local symmetry forces positivity for projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that a projectively induced Kahler-Einstein metric has positive Einstein constant as soon as it admits one nonzero local real-holomorphic Killing field. Neither completeness nor a prescribed global group action is assumed. This gives a partial answer, under a local symmetry hypothesis, to the general positivity problem for Kahler-Einstein submanifolds of (finite-dimensional) projective space. The key observation is that, by Calabi rigidity, a local real-holomorphic Killing field is induced by a projective unitary vector field whose tangency propagates along any connected global Kahler immersion, without a simple-connectivity assumption. Applied to Hulin's complete continuation, this produces a global Killing field with a bounded Hamiltonian potential given by the ambient projective moment map. The resulting Laplace equation, the Omori--Yau maximum principle and Yau's Liouville theorem exclude both negative and zero Einstein curvature. We also prove a non-Einstein obstruction under uniformly negative Ricci curvature and obtain compact equivariant continuations.

Differential Geometry.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
Differential Geometry.summary: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

Differential Geometry.title: Noncompactifiable Kähler threefolds with positive Ricci curvature
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a complete Kähler threefold $(M,ω)$ with positive Ricci curvature and infinite-dimensional third rational homology. It admits no analytic compactification, answering Yau's compactification question negatively (see \cite{Yau1992}, Problem~71, p.~304). The metric is obtained by solving a complex Monge--Ampère equation on an affine threefold and lifting the solution to an infinite cyclic cover. Its Ricci form $ρ_ω$ satisfies $\int_Mρ_ω^3=\infty$, disproving the top Yang--Yau conjecture.

Differential Geometry.title: SVarM: Linear Support Varifold Machines for Classification and Regression on Geometric Data
Differential Geometry.summary: Despite progress in the rapidly developing field of geometric deep learning, performing statistical analysis on geometric data--where each observation is a shape such as a curve, graph, or surface--remains challenging due to the non-Euclidean nature of shape spaces, which are defined as equivalence classes under invariance groups. Building machine learning frameworks that incorporate such invariances, notably to shape parametrization, is often crucial to ensure generalizability of the trained models to new observations. This work proposes \textit{SVarM} to exploit varifold representations of shapes as measures and their duality with test functions $h:\mathbb{R}^n \times S^{n-1} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$. This method provides a general framework akin to linear support vector machines but operating instead over the infinite-dimensional space of varifolds. We develop classification and regression models on shape datasets by introducing a neural network-based representation of the trainable test function $h$. This approach demonstrates strong performance and robustness across various shape graph and surface datasets, achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

Differential Geometry.title: The parallel postulate characterizes the Euclidean plane
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every complete Riemannian plane satisfying the parallel axiom is isometric to the Euclidean plane. More generally, we characterize the Euclidean plane among complete Riemannian planes without conjugate points by an asymptotic condition on geodesic intersection probabilities. This also answers affirmatively a question of Croke asking whether a complete Riemannian plane must be Euclidean if almost every pair of geodesics intersects exactly once.

Differential Geometry.title: Conformally flat Mercator equation and conserved quantities of conformal circles
Differential Geometry.summary: We study properties of solutions of the conformal Mercator equation on the conformal sphere. We focus on conformal circles and give two different approaches of finding their conserved quantities from conformal Killing vector fields - variational and tractorial. We find a direct relation between the two sets of quantities.

Differential Geometry.title: Affine Boosted Gauss Curvature Flow
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove convexity in the affine orbit of entropies associated to Gauss curvature flow for sub-affine powers. This allows the construction of an affine boosted Gauss curvature flow, which keeps the evolving hypersurface at the affine minimizer of the Gaussian entropy. The modified flow has bounded isoperimetric ratio, and after rescaling it converges along a sequence of times to self-similar solutions of the Gauss curvature flow. The construction also proves existence of new self-similar solutions to Gauss curvature flow in the sub-affine regime.

Differential Geometry.title: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

Differential Geometry.title: An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.

Differential Geometry.title: The upward conformal limit
Differential Geometry.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, both the Higgs bundle moduli space and the de Rham moduli space have stratifications by holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations over the space of complex variations of Hodge structure. The $\hbar$-conformal limit gives a biholomorphic identification of the fibers of the two strata over a stable complex variation of Hodge structure. We introduce here the $\hbar$-upward conformal limit, which is the limit at infinity rather than at zero. The main results of this paper relate the irreducible components of the nilpotent cone on $X$, which are Lagrangian submanifolds, with Lagrangians in the Morse strata on $\bar{X}$, called zero velocity Lagrangians, via the $\hbar$-upward conformal limit. In particular, Higgs bundles that flow up to the zero of the Hitchin section on $X$ are identified with opers on $\bar{X}$.

Differential Geometry.title: On pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian metrics
Differential Geometry.summary: In our previous work, we studied the squared $L^2$-norm functionals $\mathcal G$ of Gauduchon's torsion $1$-form and $\mathcal F$ of the Chern torsion over the space of all Hermitian metrics with unit volume on a compact complex manifold. We introduced torsion-critical metrics as critical points of $\mathcal F$. In this paper, We prove that a pluriclosed and astheno-Kähler metric is torsion-critical if and only if it is Kähler. In particular, every compact pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian threefold is Kähler. We also give explicit examples and derive geometric consequences under additional curvature assumptions.

Differential Geometry.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian quotient equations on Riemannian manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we consider the Dirichlet problem for a class of sum Hessian quotient equations involving a gradient term on the right-hand side on Riemannian manifolds. Under the assumption of the existence of a subsolution, based on the a priori estimates for the solutions, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of $(k-1)$-admissible solutions for the Dirichlet problem on compact Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundary. Our existence results cover the case $0\le l<k<n$ with $k\ge 2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $(k-1)$-admissible, and the case $k=n$ with $0\le l\le n-2$, where the subsolution is assumed to be $n$-admissible.

Differential Geometry.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
Differential Geometry.summary: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to explicit gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

Differential Geometry.title: An Isoperimetric Comparison for a Variational Threshold Associated with the Riemannian \(p\)-Laplacian
Differential Geometry.summary: We study a variational threshold $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ associated with a one-phase free boundary functional involving the Riemannian $p$-Dirichlet energy and a volume penalization on a bounded domain $K$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$. In the Euclidean case, this threshold is the smallest parameter for which the interior Bernoulli problem has a solution minimizing the energy; it bounds the Bernoulli constant from above, and the inequality is strict for balls. We characterize $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ as the infimum of a capacity-to-volume quotient and prove that this infimum is always attained. We then prove an isoperimetric comparison theorem: domination of the isoperimetric profile of $M$ by that of a model space implies a lower bound for $Λ_{p,M}(K)$ in terms of the threshold of a model geodesic ball. This extends a theorem of Daners and Kawohl. For geodesic balls in space forms, we give an explicit one-dimensional formula for the threshold and prove its strict monotonicity in the curvature, at fixed radius and at fixed volume. As applications, we obtain comparison results on compact manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, through the normalized Lévy--Gromov inequality, and on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, where the factor $\mbox{AVR}^{1/N}$ appears; a product-cylinder example shows that nonnegative Ricci curvature alone is not sufficient. Finally, we characterize the equality cases: geodesic balls in space forms, round spheres and geodesic balls in the Lévy--Gromov setting, Euclidean space and balls in the setting of Euclidean volume growth.

Differential Geometry.title: Pinchoff by surface diffusion
Differential Geometry.summary: Since Nichols and Mullins analysed the instability of cylindrical wires in 1965, numerical and asymptotic studies have predicted a self-similar neck at pinchoff under surface diffusion. Yet even the existence of a finite-time singularity for the flow of a smooth closed surface has remained open. We construct the first such examples, and establish their stability, modulo a finite-dimensional space. The same shrinking neck closes the central hole of an embedded torus in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and separates the lobes of a genus-zero dumbbell. In both cases the surface remains embedded until the singular time $T$ and converges smoothly away from the pinching point. Writing $A(t)$ for the waist radius and $r(z,t)$ for the radius near the neck, we prove that $A(t)=\{4μ(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)), \quad A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)ζ,t) \longrightarrow U(ζ) \quad\text{in }C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}).$ The profile $U$ above is also for the first time rigorously constructed here. It was numerically computed by Wong-Miksis-Voorhees-Davis, and identified by Bernoff-Bertozzi-Witelski as the ground state of a family of conical shrinkers. Our proof also yields a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows that admit positive symmetric conical shrinkers.
Differential Geometry.comment: 127 pages, 3 figures. This revision extends the pinchoff construction to embedded dumbbells and proves a general compactification and stability criterion for fourth-order geometric flows. The computer-assisted proof certificate is included as ancillary material

Differential Geometry.title: Topology-Preserving Hodge--Laplacian Diffusion on Manifolds with Boundary
Differential Geometry.summary:
Overview: We study deterministic and stochastic Hodge--Laplacian diffusion of differential forms on a fixed smooth compact Riemannian manifold with boundary. Absolute and relative boundary conditions select harmonic spaces representing ordinary and relative cohomology. We investigate the preservation properties of these diffusion processes, their compatible cellular discretizations, and their implications for reverse diffusion models. Numerical experiments on an annulus and a solid torus illustrate the theoretical results.
  Mathematical Significance: Using the de Rham complex and its constant-sheaf interpretation, we distinguish preservation of harmonic coordinates from preservation of a cohomology class. We establish that deterministic heat flow preserves the harmonic projection and exponentially damps its orthogonal complement. For additive stochastic forcing, we prove that pathwise harmonic preservation is equivalent to the absence of harmonic noise. Exact forcing preserves closedness and the initial cohomology class for closed initial data, whereas harmonic-projected forcing need not preserve closedness. We further show that compatible cellular discretizations retain these properties, with an algebraic extension to fixed weighted cellular sheaves. Separating invariant preservation from time-step stability and covariance accuracy, we derive bounds on leakage arising from approximate harmonic projectors.
  AI Relevance: We develop a finite-dimensional conditional score formulation that confines reverse diffusion to a prescribed harmonic component or, for closed data, a fixed cohomology class. This provides a mathematically grounded framework for incorporating topological constraints into diffusion-based generative AI models on manifolds.

Differential Geometry.title: Hermitian connections and holonomy with parallel torsions
Differential Geometry.summary:
Let $(M^n,g,J)$ be a connected Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let $\nabla$ be a Hermitian connection with nonzero parallel torsion. Assuming that its restricted holonomy acts irreducibly on $T^{1,0}M$, the author proved that the first Ricci curvature must vanish. In this paper we derive a Berger like complete list of its holonomy representations: the complexified adjoint representation of a compact simple Lie algebra, and the standard seven-dimensional complex representation of compact $\Gtwo$. Curvature of such a connection is proven to be parallel.
  Secondly, without irreducibility assumption, we derive an explicit local normal form for the metric whose Chern connection has parallel trosion, which includes holomorphic warpings and nontrivial holomorphic extensions of hyperkähler manifolds. For complete metrics with bounded Chern curvature, the characters associated with nontrivial global restricted-holonomy blocks vanish. Compact metrics admit an unwarped local form, are balanced, and have a unimodular vertical Lie algebra. On their universal covers, suitable Kähler factors split off and the remaining factor has vanishing first Chern Ricci form. A compact simply connected elliptic bundle over a K3 surface explains why this local classification does not give a global product classification. This extends the classification result of Zheng and author on Hermitian manifolds whose Chern connection is Ambrose-Singer. In particular, the analysis shows that if the metric is not Kähler its Chern curvature must satisfies $\Rm_{(\cdot), (\cdot)}X=0$ for some parallel nonzero vector $X\in T'M$.
  In appendix we include a by-product: On a compact complex homogenous space $M$ with finite fundamental group, any Hermitian metric whose Chern connection has parallel torsion, must be Kähler.

Geometric Topology.title: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
Geometric Topology.summary: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.

Geometric Topology.title: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
Geometric Topology.summary: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.
Geometric Topology.comment: 28 pages, 5 Figures, 7 Tables. Last replacement: 4 figures are slightly modified, a few misprints are corrected

Geometric Topology.title: There are hard braids
Geometric Topology.summary:
Let us call a trivial braid hard if it cannot be untangled by Reidemeister moves without increasing the number of crossings. Are there hard trivial braids? Our paper answers this question.
  Hard braids exist. For every number of strands starting from 4, for every even length starting from 16, we present examples of hard trivial braids of that size.
  Our smallest example is minimal. We prove that there are no hard braids on three strands. On four strands our shortest example, of length 16, is a shortest hard braid.
  The hard braids in that family can be untangled without increasing their length if we use Reidemeister moves and an infinite family of moves $σ_i^{\varepsilon}σ_j^{m}σ_i^{-\varepsilon} \leftrightarrowσ_j^{-\varepsilon}σ_i^{m}σ_j^{\varepsilon}$, which involve only three strands.
  We also build a harder family of hard braids which no moves confined to a bounded number of strands can untangle. For every $m$ we construct a trivial braid on $4m$ strands, of length $16m^2$, which can be untangled without increasing its length by moves on $2m+1$ strands but not not on $2m$ strands.

Geometric Topology.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author. Finally, we use Luttinger twists along the Klein bottle to construct contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings, without the use of open books or Lefschetz fibrations.
Geometric Topology.comment: V2: added section 6 on Luttinger twists along the Klein bottle

Geometric Topology.title: Computing pro-$p$ Closures of Finitely Generated Subgroups of Closed Orientable Surface Groups
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $Γ_g$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g\geq2$, and let $p$ be a prime. For every finitely generated subgroup $H\leqΓ_g$ we give an algorithm which, given any finite generating set of $H$ by words in a standard generating set, outputs a finite set of words in the same alphabet that generates the pro-$p$ closure of $H$. This extends the computation of pro-$p$ closures in free groups by Ribes-Zalesskii and Margolis-Sapir-Weil.

Geometric Topology.title: Kleinian groups with tunnel number one
Geometric Topology.summary: We give a structural theory for the holonomy groups of hyperbolic links with tunnel number 1 in arbitrary 3-manifolds. This is a first step towards understanding the canonical triangulations of such links, as it generalises the combinatorial structure theory of two-bridge link groups that is an input to the Sakuma--Weeks triangulation.

Geometric Topology.title: A filtered basis for Haiman ideals
Geometric Topology.summary: Given the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n, y_1, \dots, y_n]$, we consider the Haiman ideal $J(d)$ of polynomials that vanish to order $d$ on the diagonals. We define a rotational order on monomials and use it to construct a filtration on $J(d)$ and a bigraded, homogeneous, free $\mathbb{C}[\mathbf{y}]$-basis compatible with this filtration. This gives a new independent proof that $J(d)$ is free over $y$'s. We also discuss the connections between this filtration and triply-graded link homology.

Geometric Topology.title: Low-slope Lefschetz fibrations with finitely presented fundamental groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that for any finitely presented group $G$, there exists a genus-$3k (k\in \Z)$ Lefschetz fibration over the two-sphere having slope as close as desired to $2$ and the fundamental group of the total space is isomorphic to given group $G$. These are the first examples not satisfying the slope inequality with total spaces being non-simply connected. As a corollary, by taking fiber sum of these Lefschetz fibrations with trivial genus-$3k$ Lefschetz fibration over any genus-$h(>0)$ (positive genus) surfaces, we obtain Lefschetz fibrations having slope arbitrarily close to $2$ with different fundamental groups over any genus-$h$ surface.

Optimization and Control.title: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
Optimization and Control.summary: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

Optimization and Control.title: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
Optimization and Control.summary: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

Optimization and Control.title: Rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration
Optimization and Control.summary: We apply proof mining methods developed by Kohlenbach and the second author to compute uniform rates of metastability for a generalization of the Halpern iteration studied by Kanzow and Shehu. As special cases, we obtain rates of metastability for the Halpern and modified Halpern iterations, as well as for the Tikhonov-Mann iteration. Furthermore, convergence results are obtained as immediate consequences of our quantitative results.

Optimization and Control.title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
Optimization and Control.summary: Embedding hard operational constraints into an unconstrained Hamiltonian via large penalty multipliers induces quadratic spectral aliasing during phase estimation and increases two-qubit gate depth. This paper proposes a penalty-free, closed-loop dynamic quantum circuit scheme, designated as Zeno-decoupled gauge-ratchet optimization (Z-GRO), for constrained binary optimization without outer-loop training. Reversible feasibility phase operators within symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes confine evolution to the feasible subspace, while an interaction-correlated commutator gauge operator resolves initial symmetry stall. Directional cooling couples the unpenalized objective Hamiltonian to a reusable ancilla with a zero-two-qubit-gate threshold offset, bypassing echoed tunneling gates on retained branches. A survival-filtered Ramsey controller advances the threshold from a linear-programming bound with automatic overshoot rollback. Exact density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles show a single-check discrimination gain above four orders of magnitude, improving ground-state probability by factors of 3.0 to 4.3 over quantum Zeno dynamics and 11.4 to 22.5 over penalized schemes. Z-GRO reduces the spin-glass time-to-solution scaling base to 1.529 (compared to 1.684 for quantum Zeno dynamics and 1.909 to 2.047 for penalized schemes) and lowers 14-qubit knapsack time-to-solution by factors of 2.4 to 14.5. For two-qubit gate error rates between $5 \times 10^{-4}$ and $5 \times 10^{-3}$, Z-GRO achieves 2.9 to 7.0 times the optimal probability of noisy penalized feedback, while majority shielding limits loss to 6.3% at a 5.0% readout bit-flip rate, recording 0/24, 0/25, 0/96, 3/25, and 2/80 overshoots.

Optimization and Control.title: KL-Guided Support Selection and Subspace Cubic Newton Methods for Sparse Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study sparse composite optimization with a smooth loss and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth regularizer. The objective is locally smooth on each fixed support. Our method combines full-space proximal-gradient steps with inexact cubic-regularized Newton steps on a subspace selected by thresholding. If the iterates are bounded and the objective satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property, the entire sequence converges to a first-order stationary point. A threshold based on the KL exponent ensures that the selected coordinate set coincides with the support of the limit after finitely many iterations, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption. We also provide a residual-based threshold when such an exponent exists and its value is unknown. Under an additional continuity assumption on the restricted Hessian, the line search eventually accepts full cubic steps. With bounded cubic regularization parameters and damping parameters chosen to meet the target tolerances, we bound the number of outer iterations needed to reach restricted approximate second-order stationarity after support identification and entry into the full-step regime. We conduct numerical experiments in two settings: when the KL exponent is known and when it is unknown. In the former case, we use a degenerate problem to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. In the latter case, we compare the proposed method and its adaptive variant with existing solvers on sparse recovery and logistic regression problems.

Optimization and Control.title: Stochastic Extragradient Methods Beyond Lipschitz Continuity
Optimization and Control.summary: Stochastic variational inequality problems have received significant attention due to their ability to model large-scale machine learning tasks. Typically, the operators involved are assumed to be globally Lipschitz, with only a handful of works extending beyond the standard setting to the so-called $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. In this work, we propose a novel stochastic past extragradient algorithm for variational inequality problems under a broad regularity assumption that is even less restrictive than $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz continuity and provide convergence guarantees under bounded variance of the stochastic oracle. More precisely, we show a.s. convergence with suitable stepsize schedules and obtain convergence rates in expectation and in probability for fixed horizons. Finally, in numerical simulations we compare our proposed algorithm against standard methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Pseudo-random Instance Generators in C++ for Deterministic and Stochastic Multi-commodity Network Design Problems
Optimization and Control.summary: Network design problems constitute an important family of combinatorial optimization problems for which many exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed over the last few decades. Two central problems in this family are the multi-commodity, capacitated, fixed charge network design problem (MCFNDP) and its stochastic counterpart, the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP with recourse. These are standard problems that often serve as workbenches for devising and testing models and algorithms in stylized but near-realistic settings. Progress on solution methods requires instances of varying size, structure and difficulty. We present two open-source C++ generators. The deterministic generator modernizes and extends the generator underlying the Canad instances, with new topologies and continuous control of capacity tightness and cost structure. The stochastic generator, which is to our knowledge the first publicly available one for the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP, builds scenarios that match user-specified moments and correlations. We also release libraries of configurations for 6,000 deterministic and 416 stochastic instances, as well as the base instances and configurations of 20 stochastic instances on hub-and-spoke benchmark networks. The generators aim to support systematic and reproducible experimentation, including the training and out-of-sample evaluation of learning-based and stochastic programming methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Distributed Optimization of $M$-Convex Functions Subject to Linear Constraints via Continuous Relaxation and Shapley-Folkman Decomposition
Optimization and Control.summary: $M$-convex functions from discrete convex analysis admit tractable minimization and convex extensions that agree with them at integer points. We study the minimization of a separable collection of $N$ $M$-convex functions subject to $m$ linear coupling constraints. Our two-stage algorithm first solves the convex relaxation and then reconstructs an integer solution through local Carathéodory decompositions and an LP purification step. The returned solution has no objective increase relative to the convex-relaxation value and a coupling residual that is $O(m)$ for bounded coupling coefficients, with no explicit dependence on $N$. We prove polynomial value-oracle evaluation of the $M$-convex extension and give both an exact value-oracle-polynomial implementation and a distributed consensus-ADMM implementation under a proximal oracle. We also establish proximity and additive envelope-gap guarantees when Stage~1 uses a strongly convex extension. On an inventory placement problem with up to about $10^6$ products, both guarantees hold on every run, and the method is faster than exact integer-programming benchmarks by a factor that grows with the number of regions.

Optimization and Control.title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization with Applications
Optimization and Control.summary: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

Optimization and Control.title: Applicability of the MPCC approach to Zeng reformulations of nonlinear pessimistic bilevel programming
Optimization and Control.summary: The vanilla method in bilevel programming is to reformulate it as a single-level mathematical programs with complementarity constraints (MPCC), via the KKT conditions of the lower-level. This method seemed to work only for optimistic formulations. However, in (Zeng, 2020), B. Zeng presented a general method to reduce pessimistic bilevel problems to optimistic ones. In this note, we study how to apply the MPCC approach to the pessimistic counterpart through Zeng's reformulation (Zeng, 2020). While we show that it cannot be applied directly since constraint qualification can be destroyed by the reformulation, it still can be used to solve natural relaxations, in the spirit of (Wiesemann,2013),(Loridan & Morgan,1989), (Loridan & Morgan,1996).

Optimization and Control.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
Optimization and Control.summary: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations generate dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a closed-loop primal-dual scheme, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This scheme requires no penalty couplers, slack qubits, or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN achieves 83.3% full-chip exact feasibility, reduces high-constraint error by 6.1-20.1-fold over $K$-scaled first-order updates (138.4-323.3-fold over fixed-gain curvature), outperforms time-matched mixed-integer programming at 256 spins, and attains 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the scheme is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.

Optimization and Control.title: Small noise limit for Entropic Variational Mean-Field Games
Optimization and Control.summary: We study second order variational mean-field games with quadratic Hamiltonian. In analogy with entropic optimal transport, Benamou, Carlier, Di Marino and the second author recently proposed an entropy-minimization formulation of the problem, which could be interpreted as the Lagrangian counterpart of the classical Eulerian approach. We investigate the small-noise $Γ$-limit for the Lagrangian entropy-minimization formulation and establish $Γ$-convergence of second order mean-field games towards their deterministic first order counterpart. This also translates into another (dynamical) proof of the convergence of the Schrödinger problem to optimal transport. Moreover, we study the original Eulerian problem and prove a first order energy expansion, which establishes a selection principle for minimizers of the deterministic problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Operator Learning for Backstepping Control of Parabolic Equations on Time-Varying Domains
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper develops a neural operator approach to boundary stabilization of a parabolic equation on a time-varying domain, reducing the cost of backstepping kernel computation. Specifically, we establish the continuity of the operator mapping moving boundaries to backstepping kernels and apply the universal approximation theorem to establish the existence of an approximate kernel. Due to the compactness requirement, the approximate kernel is derived only on a finite time interval, limiting the exponential decay estimate to a finite horizon. To extend the result to an infinite horizon, we must circumvent the compactness requirement. Taking periodic moving boundary as an example, we propose a modified DeepONet architecture that lifts the non-compact time domain into a compact, higher-dimensional space. This modification relaxes the constraint of approximation accuracy and extends finite-horizon exponential decay to uniform exponential stability over an infinite horizon. Numerical simulations demonstrate accelerated backstepping kernel computation and closed-loop stabilization.

Optimization and Control.title: On Robust Strictly Positive Real Synthesis for High-Order Interval Polynomials
Optimization and Control.summary: We establish two complementary results on common strictly positive real (SPR) numerators for Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial families. First, for every order $n \ge 10$, we construct a monic Hurwitz-stable interval polynomial family with rational endpoints and positive width in every nonleading coefficient such that every nonzero real numerator of degree at most $n$ produces a strictly negative real part at some member and some positive frequency. In particular, robust Hurwitz stability alone does not guarantee equal-degree SPR synthesis in high orders. Second, for every order $n \ge 1$, we prove that a common real SPR numerator of exact degree $n$ always exists whenever the lower endpoint of each interior coefficient interval is at most $10^{-5}$ times its upper endpoint, while the constant and leading coefficients vary over arbitrary compact positive intervals.

Optimization and Control.title: Delightful Policy Gradient under Distributed Friction
Optimization and Control.summary: Distributed reinforcement learning trains on data from stale, buggy, or mismatched actors, whose actions often have high surprisal (negative log-probability) under the learner's policy. Supervised fine-tuning learns stably from such logged data, while policy gradient often does not. We trace the difference to negative learning from surprising data: rare failures can dominate finite-batch updates, while rare successes carry information the current policy would otherwise miss. The Delightful Policy Gradient (DG) separates the two by gating each term with delight, the product of advantage and surprisal, and needs no behavior probabilities. In a contaminated bandit, DG suppresses the perpendicular noise of rare failures by a factor that vanishes as the learner improves; no gate based only on learner probability can do this without also suppressing rare successes. On MNIST with stale actors, DG beats importance-weighted policy gradient given the exact behavior probabilities. On a transformer sequence task, DG often reaches an order of magnitude lower error under staleness, actor--learner probability mismatch, actor bugs, reward corruption, and rare discovery. With four frictions combined, its sample-efficiency advantage grows with sequence length. All experiments are controlled diagnostics; we do not evaluate an end-to-end distributed system.

Optimization and Control.title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
Optimization and Control.summary: Generative models transform simple random inputs into samples that resemble observed data. For a finite training set, a central question is how its geometry shapes the terminal dynamics and the probabilities assigned to individual samples. We address this question for flow matching with linear interpolation between independent Gaussian and empirical samples. The squared distance to the training set generates explicit paths contracting exponentially toward the nearest sample. We prove that exact trajectories restarted at prescribed late-time states approximate these paths uniformly over all elapsed times and compact sets of starting states away from Voronoi interfaces, with an error exponentially small in the inverse squared restart noise scale. The initial mass near interfaces controls the quadratic Wasserstein error between the exact and reference laws. For Gaussian and fixed Gaussian-tube restart laws, this gives a square-root rate in the restart noise scale, uniform over time, which a two-site example shows to be sharp in general. At ties, the Clarke subdifferential characterizes the graphical limit of the rescaled velocity field. This geometry motivates two learning methods: fitting the distance potential with value and gradient supervision, and fitting velocities along explicit contraction paths. A transport estimate separates initialization mismatch, velocity error, incomplete contraction, and endpoint allocation. MNIST experiments illustrate the distinct roles of support proximity, nearest-site retention, and feature fidelity. These results connect flow matching and score-based diffusion through a common limiting geometry and show how asymptotic analysis can inform the design and evaluation of generative models.

Optimization and Control.title: Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient Methods for Stochastic Composite Nonconvex Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose {\sf ALFPG}, an Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient framework for stochastic composite nonconvex minimization. It adapts stepsizes from the optimization trajectory without requiring smoothness constants or line search. For finite-sum problems, {\sf ALFPG-FS} combines coordinate-wise stepsizes, Nesterov extrapolation, and a SPIDER estimator; {\sf ALFPG-D} is its full-batch specialization. Under component-wise smoothness, bounded sublevel sets, and separate lower bounds on $f$ and $h$, {\sf ALFPG-FS} achieves expected $ε$-stationarity with $\mathcal O(N+\sqrt N ε^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations. For expectation problems, we develop {\sf ALFPG-MVR1} and {\sf ALFPG-MVR2} (MVR: Momentum-based Variance Reduction). Both use one fresh sample per iteration. MVR1 uses one stochastic-gradient evaluation; MVR2 uses at most two evaluations at different points with the same sample. MVR1 requires smoothness of the expected loss; MVR2 additionally requires uniformly smooth sample losses. When the regularizer is convex or Lipschitz continuous on its effective domain and stochastic gradients are almost surely bounded, both methods achieve expected $ε$-stationarity using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(σ^2ε^{-4}+ε^{-2})$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(σε^{-3}+ε^{-2})$ stochastic-gradient evaluations, respectively. Here, $N$ is the number of component functions, $σ^2$ bounds the gradient noise variance, and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ hides polylogarithmic factors. Neither expectation variant requires prior knowledge of $σ$, and both recover $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(ε^{-2})$ complexity in the zero-noise regime. Numerical experiments on sparse phase retrieval, linear eigenvalue problems, and neural network regression show that all four ALFPG variants generally outperform state-of-the-art proximal-gradient baselines.

Optimization and Control.title: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization benchmark problems from mixed Hamming packings
Optimization and Control.summary: Benchmarking exact solvers and noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices for quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) requires small yet challenging instances, preferably coming from actual applications. We propose such a benchmark set derived from mixed Hamming packing, a hard problem in coding theory. Starting from its mixed-integer linear programming formulation, we provide a generator for the equivalent QUBO models and study 133 instances whose optima are certified by that formulation. In the feature space of the MQLib library, we position a broad range of existing quantum-oriented benchmarks relative to the classical ones: they lie along a narrow, sparse border of the region covered by MQLib, whereas our instances form a coherent family in a region that both collections leave almost empty. Classical heuristics and a simulated bifurcation machine find the optimum of most instances quickly, in several cases sooner than an exact mixed-integer solver first encounters it, suggesting heuristic warm starts for exact solvers; for an exact QUBO solver, in turn, it appears challenging to prove optimality. In Ising form, the instances are densely connected antiferromagnets whose large local fields are almost exactly balanced by the couplings, so that the decision on each variable rests on a small remainder. This makes them hard to embed and to represent accurately on current quantum annealers, in line with our D-Wave experiments.
Optimization and Control.comment: 36 pages, 4 figures, 'Online resource 1' included at the end of the paper

Optimization and Control.title: Linear and Quadratic Penalties for Cardinality Constraints in Unconstrained Binary Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study penalty strategies for converting constrained binary optimization problems to quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) form on the example of the sparsest $k$-subgraph problem. We adopt an augmented Lagrangian approach involving a linear penalty in addition to the commonly used quadratic one, and show the benefits of this approach. From the constraint structure, we derive sufficient bounds on the penalty coefficients. We conduct extensive experiments comparing combinations of our different penalty strategies with a wide range of classical and quantum QUBO solvers. Our experiments show that to obtain a good-quality solution, the right penalty strategy is almost as important as the quality of the QUBO solver, and iterative approaches appear to be the most efficient. We discuss the mechanisms that lead to a degradation of the solution quality due to large quadratic penalties.

Optimization and Control.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
Optimization and Control.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.
