For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.65^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.
Information Theory.comment: 33 pages, 9 figures. v2: added word "any" to title, improved a bound following comment from ZM26, added three small special cases, removed unicode from an anc file, and added a statement about deep sets. v3: no new results, but many small text edits for clarity, and also added appendix with four new figures to aid in indexation of results. v4 text edits for clarity

Information Theory.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
Information Theory.summary: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.

Information Theory.title: The Insertion List-Decoding Capacity and an Improved Bound on the Deletion List-Decoding Capacity
Information Theory.summary:
Informally, the capacity of list-decoding in a given adversarial error model is the largest rate at which we can list-decode with list size polynomial in the block length. The capacity of list-decoding from insertions and deletions is a basic, yet poorly understood, aspect of coding against synchronization errors. For example, when dealing with a $δ>1/2$ fraction of insertions, the best known lower bounds give little more than the fact that the capacity is positive. Beyond that regime we also only have loose bounds, with the lower bounds stemming from the analysis of uniformly random codes.
  We make progress in our understanding of the limits of list-decoding binary codes from insertions and deletions. We show that the capacity of list-decoding from a $δ$-fraction of insertions is exactly
  \begin{equation*}
  (1+δ)\left(1-h\left(\fracδ{1+δ}\right)\right)
  \end{equation*} for all $δ\in[0,1]$, where $h$ is the binary entropy function, achieved with high probability by a code sampled according to a symmetric $2$-state Markov chain. Curiously, we complement this by showing that such an approach does not beat uniformly random coding in list-decoding from deletions. We also give an improved upper bound on the capacity of list-decoding from a $δ$-fraction of deletions, showing in particular that it behaves like $1-h(δ)+o(δ)$ when $δ\to 0$. This matches the first-order asymptotic behavior of the capacity of the binary deletion channel for vanishing deletion probability, but differs in the second-order term.
Information Theory.comment: 25 pages. A preliminary version of this work appears in ITCS 2027

Information Theory.title: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams
Information Theory.summary: Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product $Nγ$ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size $a$ from $\{0,1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$ goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate $O((Nγ)^{-1/2})$ if $a\in \{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

Information Theory.title: The Complexity of Oracle-Efficient Realizable Transductive Learning
Information Theory.summary: In realizable transductive online learning, the learner knows the entire sequence of $T$ instances in advance, and the labels are consistent with one of $N$ hypotheses. With explicit access to the hypothesis class, the halving algorithm makes at most $\log_2 N$ mistakes. Can a comparable guarantee be achieved using only polynomially many empirical risk minimization (ERM) queries? We answer this question negatively, even for a weighted-ERM oracle that optimizes arbitrary real-valued linear objectives and returns a complete maximizing hypothesis. For every fixed $β\in(0,1)$ and every randomized learner making polynomially many oracle queries, there exists a fixed realizable instance with exactly $N=2^{\lfloor T^β\rfloor}$ hypotheses on which the learner makes $Ω_β(\sqrt{T\log N})$ mistakes in expectation. This matches the agnostic-rate upper bound achieved by random playout using $O(T)$ oracle calls. The separation persists for much smaller classes as well: along a sequence with $\log N=Θ((\log T)^2)$, we establish a mistake lower bound of $\exp(Ω(\log T/\log\log T))$. Our main technical contribution is a composition lemma that combines two realizable prediction problems such that their mistake lower bounds add, up to a small loss, while keeping the growth of the combined hypothesis class under control. Iterating this lemma yields a family of hard instances spanning the desired parameter regimes, establishing a sharp separation between information-theoretic and oracle-efficient mistake guarantees.
Information Theory.comment: 22 pages, 1 figure; fixed LaTeX \Cref issues in v1. No changes to the content

Information Theory.title: The Insertion-Deletion Distance of Linear Codes under Random Coordinate Permutations
Information Theory.summary: We study the maximum insertion-deletion (insdel) distance attainable by permuting the coordinates of a fixed $[n,k]_q$ linear code. Exploiting the connection between common subsequences of codewords and noncrossing matchings in the related bipartite graphs, we establish probabilistic lower bounds under random coordinate permutations over large alphabets. In particular, if the maximum symbol multiplicity among nonconstant codewords is $O(n/q)$, a uniformly random coordinate permutation yields insdel distance at least $2n-O(n/\sqrt q)$ with high probability for sufficiently large $q$. Furthermore, for projective linear codes satisfying the same symbol multiplicity condition, we show that the maximum attainable insdel distance is $2n-Θ(n/\sqrt q)$. As an application, for $[n,k]_q$ MDS codes containing the all-one vector, random coordinate permutations yield insdel distance at least $2n-O(\sqrt{kn})$ with high probability whenever $(k-1)(\log q)^2=o(n)$. In particular, for full-length Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, we obtain the lower bound $2q-O(\sqrt{kq})$ with high probability for $k=o(q/(\log q)^2)$, substantially improving previously known lower bounds while allowing a wider range of dimensions. Finally, we give explicit constructions of full-length RS codes over square fields, attaining the order-optimal insdel distance $2q-Θ(\sqrt q)$.

Information Theory.title: Parity-check matrices and their MDS or NMDS properties for several classes of non-GRS type linear codes
Information Theory.summary: Parity-check matrices and weight distributions are important for understanding the structure and performance of linear codes. However, obtaining explicit expressions for them is often challenging. In recent years, numerous families of non-GRS type linear codes have been constructed, motivated by applications in coding theory and cryptography. For many of these codes, explicit parity-check matrices remain unavailable, hindering further investigation of their duality properties, decoding methods, and weight distributions. In this paper, we first develop a method for constructing parity-check matrices using code extensions and Cramer's rule, and then apply this method or through direct constructions to obtain explicit parity-check matrices for column-twisted generalized Reed--Solomon codes (TGRS), modified GRS codes and so on. Second, we introduce the $(Ł,¶)$-twisted generalized Roth--Lempel (TGRL) code $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{m\times m},\B)$, obtain explicit parity-check matrices for three subclasses through direct constructions, and establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $\C_{k,\ell}(Ł,¶,\A_{2\times 2},\B)$ with the most general $Ł$, $¶$, and $\B$ to be maximum distance separable (MDS). For one-column TGRS codes, we prove that they are either MDS or near MDS (NMDS), furthermore, establish a necessary and sufficient condition for them to be NMDS, and determine the weight distribution of a family of these NMDS codes using subset sums in finite abelian groups. Finally, basing on known results for non-GRS properties of TGRS codes, we establish sufficient conditions for these codes considered in this paper to be non-GRS from the perspective of punctured codes.

Information Theory.title: Wyner's Common Information and the Common Entropy are NP-Hard to Compute
Information Theory.summary: Wyner's common information $J(P_{XY})$ and the common entropy $G(P_{XY})$ of a pair of finite random variables $(X,Y)$ with joint distribution $P_{XY}$ minimize, respectively, the mutual information $I(X,Y;W)$ and the entropy $H(W)$ over all auxiliary random variables $W$ that make $X$ and $Y$ conditionally independent. We prove that both quantities are NP-hard to compute, by polynomial-time reductions from the Maximum Edge Biclique problem. Moreover, unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm can approximate $J(P_{XY})$ within an additive error $1/(8N^2)$, or $G(P_{XY})$ within an additive error $1/(2N)$, where $N$ is the number of positive entries of $P_{XY}$.
Information Theory.comment: Updated version of the manuscript. Submitted for publication

Information Theory.title: Self-Orthogonal Minimal Codes from n-to-1 Mappings
Information Theory.summary: Self-orthogonal codes are central to the construction of quantum error-correcting codes, and minimal codes yield secret-sharing schemes whose access structures are read off from the supports of their codewords. A code that is both self-orthogonal and minimal therefore serves both purposes at once, so that a single family of codes can produce a quantum code and a secret-sharing scheme simultaneously. Linear codes arising from n-to-1 mappings over finite fields are a natural source of such codes and have attracted considerable attention recently, yet their parameters and weight distributions remain difficult to determine: for most high-degree functions the Walsh spectra cannot be computed directly, and it is precisely these weights on which the analysis of minimality and self-orthogonality rests. We address this difficulty through the algebraic theory of skew polynomial rings. Using the right greatest common divisor of skew polynomials, we determine the dimensions of the kernel spaces of the linearized polynomials associated with the n-to-1 mappings, which in turn yield the weight distributions of the corresponding codes. With this method we treat two newly constructed families of n-to-1 functions together with one known family, and obtain the exact weight distributions of the resulting codes; we further prove that all of these codes are minimal and self-orthogonal. Each family therefore simultaneously yields a quantum error-correcting code and a secret-sharing scheme, with explicitly determined parameters and access structures. This work offers a new perspective for determining the parameters of linear codes derived from n-to-1 mappings.

Information Theory.title: Explicit Constructions of MDS Cyclic Codes from Rational Function Fields
Information Theory.summary: We present a unified construction of maximum distance separable (MDS) cyclic codes over \(\mathbb F_q\) from rational function fields. The evaluation places form a single orbit under a cyclic automorphism group, and the defining divisor is invariant under that group. We recover the classical existence results for lengths \(n\) satisfying \(n\mid(q-1)\), \(n=p\), or \(n\mid(q+1)\), where \(p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F_q)\). For odd divisors \(n\) of \(q+1\), we construct codes in every even dimension \(2\leq k\leq n-1\) using a second orbit of rational places for \(n<q+1\) and duality for \(n=q+1\). Finally, we use the repeated-root factorization of \(x^n-1\) to give a direct proof of the classical result that no nontrivial MDS cyclic code of length \(n\) exists when \(p\mid n\) and \(n\ne p\).

Information Theory.title: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes
Information Theory.summary: A code is non-overlapping if no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is a suffix of a codeword. Let $S_n(q)$ be the largest size of a non-overlapping code of length $n$ over an alphabet of size $q$. Levenshtein proved that $S_n(q)\le c_nq^n$, where $c_n=(1/n)\bigl((n-1)/n\bigr)^{n-1}$. The codes $I^{n-1}J$, where $I$ and $J$ partition the alphabet, attain this bound when $n$ divides $q$, and Blackburn conjectured that for every $n$ and all sufficiently large $q$, the best such code is a maximum non-overlapping code. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. We also show that only the codes $I^{n-1}J$ with $|I|=(n-1)q/n$ and their reversals meet Levenshtein's bound.

Information Theory.title: Deterministic Polar Subcode Design via Exact Low-Weight Spectrum Characterization
Information Theory.summary: We develop a deterministic framework for improving polar-subcode minimum distance through information-set selection and dynamic frozen expression design. Expression design faces two difficulties. Changing an expression can introduce new low-weight codewords, and excluding different codewords can impose conflicting requirements on the same coefficients. To address both difficulties, we first fix the information set and release the editable frozen constraints to form a common supercode containing every candidate code. Its low-weight codewords give necessary and sufficient conditions for one coefficient assignment to exclude every codeword of the specified weights. To apply these conditions at longer lengths, we use the polar decomposition. At each split, a one in the left codeword gives two complementary output bits whose combined weight is always one. We can therefore eliminate the corresponding variables from the parity checks and count their compatible assignments to obtain the exact low-weight spectrum. With both constituent codes fixed, the same reduced checks also simplify the coefficient search. Assignments that give identical check values across all relevant messages share one representative, from which the entire group can be recovered. We give sufficient conditions for choosing the coefficients sequentially without backtracking. Finally, we use the outcome of expression design on one information set to guide exchanges of information positions for the next, linking the two design steps. In experiments spanning block lengths from 64 to 1024 and several code rates, the proposed design meets the target minimum distances in minutes and achieves competitive frame error rates under successive cancellation list decoding.

Information Theory.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
Information Theory.summary: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.

Information Theory.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
Information Theory.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.

Information Theory.title: List Estimation
Information Theory.summary:
Classical estimation outputs a single point estimate of an unknown $d$-dimensional vector from an observation.
  In this paper, we study \emph{$k$-list estimation}, in which a single observation is used to produce a list of $k$ candidate estimates and performance is measured by the expected squared distance from the true vector to the closest candidate. We compare this centralized setting with a symmetric decentralized MMSE benchmark in which $k$ agents observe conditionally i.i.d.\ measurements and each agent outputs its own MMSE estimate. On the centralized side, we show that optimal $k$-list estimation is equivalent to fixed-rate $k$-point vector quantization of the posterior distribution and, under standard regularity conditions, admits an exact high-rate asymptotic expansion with explicit constants and decay rate $k^{-2/d}$. On the decentralized side, we derive lower bounds in terms of the small-ball behavior of the single-agent MMSE error; in particular, when the conditional error density is bounded near the origin, the benchmark distortion cannot decay faster than order $k^{-2/d}$. We further show that if the error density vanishes at the origin in a power-law fashion, then the decentralized benchmark is provably unable to match the centralized $k^{-2/d}$ exponent, whereas the centralized estimator retains the $k^{-2/d}$ scaling. Gaussian specializations yield explicit formulas and numerical experiments corroborate the predicted asymptotic behavior. Overall, the results show that, in the scaling with $k$, one observation combined with $k$ carefully chosen candidates can be asymptotically as effective as---and in some regimes strictly better than---this MMSE-based decentralized benchmark with $k$ \rev{conditionally independent} observations.

Information Theory.title: ProFL: Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning
Information Theory.summary: Performative prediction is a framework that captures distribution shifts that occur during the training of machine learning models due to their deployment. As the trained model is used, the induced data distribution evolves, leading to deviations from the original data distribution. The impact of such model-induced distribution shifts in federated learning (FL) is increasingly likely to transpire in real-life use cases. A recently proposed approach extends performative prediction to FL with the resulting model converging to a performative stable point, which may be far from the performative optimal point. Earlier research in centralized settings has shown that the performative optimal point can be achieved under model-induced distribution shifts, but these approaches require the performative risk to be convex and the training data to be noiseless. These assumptions are often violated in realistic FL systems. This paper addresses these limitations and proposes Performative Robust Optimal Federated Learning (ProFL), an algorithm that targets the performative optimal point in FL while mitigating the effects of noisy and contaminated local data. We present a neighborhood-convergence analysis under the Polyak--Lojasiewicz condition, which applies to non-convex objectives. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the advantage of Robust Optimal Federated Learning over the state-of-the-art.
Information Theory.comment: 27 pages, including appendices. Updated the theoretical analysis and experimental results to reflect the version accepted by IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing

Information Theory.title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
Information Theory.summary: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.
Information Theory.comment: 6 pages + 7 pages appendix, 6 figures, 3 tables, 1 algorithm. Extended version of the manuscript submitted to IEEE WCNC 2027, including the detailed derivation of the SCA algorithm

Information Theory.title: Instance-optimal high-precision shadow tomography with few-copy measurements: A metrological approach
Information Theory.summary:
We study the sample complexity of shadow tomography in the high-precision regime under realistic measurement constraints. Given an unknown $d$-dimensional quantum state $ρ$ and a known set of observables $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$, the goal is to estimate expectation values $\{\mathrm{tr}(O_iρ)\}_{i=1}^m$ to accuracy $ε$ in $L_p$-norm, using possibly adaptive measurements that act on $O(\mathrm{polylog}(d))$ number of copies of $ρ$ at a time. We focus on the regime where $ε$ is below an instance-dependent threshold.
  Our main contribution is an instance-optimal characterization of the sample complexity as $\tildeΘ(Γ_p/ε^2)$, where $Γ_p$ is a function of $\{O_i\}_{i=1}^m$ defined via an optimization formula involving the inverse Fisher information matrix. Previously, tight bounds were known only in special cases, e.g. Pauli shadow tomography with $L_\infty$-norm error. Concretely, we first analyze a simpler oblivious variant where the goal is to estimate an observable of the form $\sum_{i=1}^m α_i O_i$ with $\|α\|_q = 1$ (where $q$ is dual to $p$) revealed after the measurement. For single-copy measurements, we obtain a sample complexity of $Θ(Γ^{\mathrm{ob}}_p/ε^2)$. We then show $\tildeΘ(Γ_p/ε^2)$ is necessary and sufficient for the original problem, with the lower bound applying to unbiased, kurtosis-bounded estimators when $p \geq 1$. Our upper bounds rely on a two-step algorithm combining coarse tomography with local estimation. Notably, $Γ^{\mathrm{ob}}_\infty = Γ_\infty$. In both cases, allowing $c$-copy measurements improves the sample complexity by at most $Ω(1/c)$.
  Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between quantum learning and metrology, unifying asymptotic metrological limits with finite-sample learning guarantees.
Information Theory.comment: 69 pages; several technical errors from the earlier version fixed including the wrong order of optimization over measurements and references states; key messages remain unchanged

Information Theory.title: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission
Information Theory.summary: This paper investigates joint trajectory and power optimization for movable antenna (MA)-aided secure transmission, where the MA can transmit during its movement. Specifically, the average secrecy rate is maximized subject to movement and power constraints, which couple the MA positions and transmit powers over time, respectively. To tackle this nonconvex problem, we first decouple the transmit powers via Lagrangian duality, where the optimal power for a given trajectory is derived in semi-closed form and shown to depend only on the current MA position. Accordingly, we decouple the MA positions by equivalently reformulating the problem on a discretized linear rail in terms of the farthest grid point and the number of time slots spent at each grid point. Then, from strong duality of the convex relaxation for each farthest point, we construct an asymptotically optimal solution in which the MA dwells at no more than two positions. Finally, a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to select the farthest grid point and certify the optimality gap. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the benchmark schemes.

Information Theory.title: Shared Sky, Shared Spectrum: Coordinated Satellite-5G Networks for Low-Altitude Economy
Information Theory.summary: Driven by both technological development and practical demands, the low-altitude economy relying on low-altitude aircrafts (LAAs) is booming. However, neither satellites nor terrestrial fifth-generation (5G) networks alone can effectively satisfy the communication requirements for ubiquitous lowaltitude coverage. While full integration of satellites and 5G networks offers theoretical benefits, the associated overhead and complexity pose significant challenges for rapid deployment. As a more economical and immediately viable alternative, this paper investigates partially-integrated networks where satellites and 5G systems operate with coarse synchronization yet achieve coordinated spectrum sharing, pooling their capabilities to jointly serve LAAs. Leveraging the inherent position-awareness of LAAs, we propose a framework for joint time-frequency spectrum sharing with an adaptive synchronization time scale, where only large-scale channel state information (CSI) is required. To avoid solving the NP-hard optimization problem directly, link-feature-aided clustering is employed following a divide-andconquer strategy. The proposed framework achieves substantial performance gains with low overhead and complexity, enabling swift advancement of low-altitude applications while paving the way for future integrated satellite-terrestrial network evolution.

Information Theory.title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
Information Theory.summary: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, $q$ being a prime power. For an entanglement-assisted or unassisted stabilizer code defined by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear space $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, a set of erasures and an associated repair group, we propose a procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures, within the stabilizer measurement model. The repair group is reduced by eliminating qudits that need not be measured. In classical local recovery, such symbols can be found by Gaussian elimination, although the resulting repair group need not be a smallest one. In the quantum case we eliminate an admissible set of qudits. Finding a largest admissible set is a linear matroid parity problem, and for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes defined by two linear codes it is a linear matroid intersection problem. Both problems are solvable in deterministic polynomial time. We give closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for general codes and for codes from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and, for two-code CSS codes, a sharper bound with a min--max formula. Based on these bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the concept of dimension locality of classical local recovery.
Information Theory.comment: The new authors extended and improved the results from v1 by using matroid theory. This is a continuation of arXiv:2608.04403

Information Theory.title: Vector Quantized Information Bottleneck Mitigation of Adversarial Attacks on Modulation Classifiers
Information Theory.summary: Radio-frequency (RF) signal processing based on machine learning, including Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), plays a critical role in Next Generation (NextG) intelligent communications but remains highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Prior work explored Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) as a means to improve robustness, but only in continuous spaces and never for RF classifiers. We investigate the impact of discrete-space information bottlenecks on the adversarial robustness of AMC models. Classification accuracy of attacked modulated RF waveforms is evaluated in two frameworks designed to leverage VIB for adversarial robustness: (i) a two-stage framework where VIB is applied in the preprocessing step using a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQVAE) to suppress adversarial perturbations in the process of input signal reconstruction and (ii) a Vector Quantized Classifier (VQC) that leverages VIB inside the classifier proper. The architectures of VQVAE and VQC are identical up to the bottleneck where the VQVAE adds a decoder while VQC utilizes a classification head. We train both VQVAE and VQC with loss functions that we derive from the VIB information-theoretic model. Both frameworks incorporate vector quantization and KL regularization to enforce discrete bottlenecks that filter out adversarial noise. Evaluations under white-box attacks demonstrate that discrete bottlenecks significantly enhance robustness: VQVAE outperforms its continuous VAE (Variational Autoencoder) counterpart, while VQC achieves strong robustness without requiring signal reconstruction.
Information Theory.comment: Presented at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Machine Learning for Communication and Networking (ICMLCN). To appear in IEEE Xplore. \c{opyright} 2026 IEEE

Information Theory.title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Sharp Bounds and Extremizers
Information Theory.summary: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $χ^2(P\|Q)$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $χ^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $χ^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $χ^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained. As an application to lossless source coding, we consider the product measures $P^n$ and $Q^n$ induced by $P$ and $Q$, respectively, on blocks of length $n$. We bound the expected saving in ideal codelength under $P^n$ when the encoder replaces $Q^n$ with the mixture $λP^n+(1-λ)Q^n$. The lower bound depends on the sources only through $D(P\|Q)$, and the upper bound depends on them only through the two ordered chi-squared divergences between $P$ and $Q$. For every fixed $n$, the upper bound agrees with the expected saving to first order as $λ\to 0^+$.
Information Theory.comment: Section 4 is new, together with revisions

Information Theory.title: What Must LLM Agents Communicate? From Information Loss to Communication Failures
Information Theory.summary: When evidence is distributed across LLM agents, a team may collectively possess all the information needed for a decision yet fail to use it effectively. What must agents communicate for accurate joint predictions, and when does interaction help? We study three requirements for effective communication: sufficiency of the information conveyed, selection of relevant evidence, and utilization of received information. Drawing on information theory and communication complexity, we develop a framework that combines theoretical benchmarks with controlled experiments and message-level analyses. We find that local probability reports can discard essential information, with theoretical information loss closely matching observed performance penalties. Query-first interaction improves predictions when relevant evidence depends on a private query, but compact one-shot representations can eliminate this advantage. Even when sufficient information is communicated, agents may fail to select or use it correctly. Together, these findings distinguish fundamental communication limits from failures in how LLM agents communicate and use information.

Information Theory.title: Sharp one-shot bounds and optimal exponents of universal randomness extraction
Information Theory.summary: We introduce techniques for the study of randomness extraction against quantum side information (privacy amplification) by relating this problem to variants of hypothesis testing tasks with quadratic constraints. Building also on the recently introduced measured smooth entropy approach of [Regula and Tomamichel, arXiv:2603.04493], we precisely determine the optimal scaling of the error of quantum privacy amplification in several regimes. Our results apply to the standard operational security criterion based on trace distance and focus in particular on universal classes of hash functions. On the technical side, our investigation reveals connections with operator space theory methods used in non-commutative Khintchine inequalities. As one application, we give a one-shot converse bound that shows the leftover hash lemma of [arXiv:2603.04493] to be tight up to a constant factor for all strongly 4-universal hash functions. This allows us to evaluate the asymptotic i.i.d. error exponent of universal randomness extraction for all rates, matching the bound of [Dupuis, arXiv:2105.05342] and improving also earlier classical asymptotic results of [Hayashi, arXiv:1010.1358]. We furthermore give new one-shot achievability and converse bounds on the error in the strong converse regime, which we show to match up to a constant factor. This establishes the exact strong converse exponent of quantum privacy amplification under 2-universal hash functions, complementing the converse bound of [Shen, Gao, and Cheng, arXiv:2202.10263].

Probability.title: Regenerative range for planar random walks
Probability.summary: We consider a centred random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which consumes resources originally present at every site. After consumption, each resource regenerates independently with probability $p$ at each step. We study the number of resources consumed up to time $n$, which is denoted $C_n$. Letting $p=p_n$ depend on $n$ and supposing that the walk moves faster than the resources regenerate, $i.e.$ $p_n=o(1)$, we establish a Law of Large Numbers and a Central Limit Theorem for $C_n$. In particular, we identify a phase transition between a so-called fast regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrow\infty$, where the fluctuations of $C_n$ are Gaussian, and a slow regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrowλ\in[0,\infty)$, where the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and described by a weighted renormalized self-intersection local time of planar Brownian motion depending on the parameter $λ$.

Probability.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
Probability.summary: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\toρ\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-ρ)/(2-ρ)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $ρ=1$.

Probability.title: Universal existence and generic uniqueness for quadratic BSDE systems in a two-player stochastic differential game
Probability.summary: We study two-dimensional quadratic backward stochastic differential equations in the augmented natural filtration of a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The generator has components $q_{θ,i}(z)=z_i(z_1+z_2)-α_i z_i^2/2$, $i=1,2$, where $θ=(α_1,α_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. In the associated stochastic differential game, two players choose efforts $u_1,u_2$, the common state has drift $u_1+u_2$, and player $i$ pays $u_i^2/2$ per unit time and has risk sensitivity $α_i-1$. For every bounded terminal payoff vector $ξ$, which may depend on the entire state path, $(Y,Z)\mapsto Z$ is a bijection from solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ to Nash equilibria in BMO controls. Whether the risk-neutral system ($α_1=α_2=1$) is well posed for every such $ξ$ was left open in [Jackson (2023), Section 6.4]. For $α_1α_2\ne0$ with $α_1^{-1}+α_2^{-1}=1$, existence and uniqueness in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every bounded $ξ$ were established in [Fan, Hu and Tang (2025), Corollary 2.25]. We prove that every bounded $ξ$ admits a solution in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$. The solution is unique for every bounded $ξ$ if $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)=1$, but for every $θ$ with $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)\ne1$, we construct a bounded $ξ$ admitting at least two distinct solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$. Nevertheless, for each $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $M>0$, uniqueness holds on a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of $[-M,M]^2$-valued terminal conditions equipped with the topology of convergence in probability. Moreover, if $ξ_n$ in this space converges in probability to a point $ξ$ of this subset, every choice of solutions for $ξ_n$ converges to the unique solution for $ξ$ in $\mathcal{S}^p\times\mathcal{H}^p$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.
Probability.comment: 60 pages. This version proves existence for every bounded terminal condition, characterizes universal uniqueness for all real parameter pairs, and gives the corresponding results for Nash equilibria

Probability.title: Sharp estimates for incremental moments of inverse subordinators and approximation errors for time-changed stochastic differential equations
Probability.summary: This paper establishes precise upper and lower bounds for the incremental moments of general inverse subordinators. Such processes are used as random time changes to model subdiffusive phenomena. The upper and lower bounds provide the foundation for a general framework for analyzing numerical approximation of time-changed stochastic differential equations on deterministic time grids. We derive an upper bound for the approximation error and further prove that the resulting order of convergence cannot be improved in general.

Probability.title: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
Probability.summary:
We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process.
  In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms.
  Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

Probability.title: Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry
Probability.summary: We develop series representations for solutions to general nonlinear controlled and stochastic Volterra equations in terms of two new types of signature, called geometric and Itô Volterra signature. These signatures collect the necessary iterated kernel integrals and satisfy (quasi) shuffle identities, which allow us to prove universal approximation results for Volterra path functionals. We then derive finite order expansions with precise remainder terms for both controlled and stochastic Volterra equations with possibly singular kernels, as well as expansions of their expectations. For the latter, we provide sufficient conditions for absolute convergence of the resulting series representation and verify them for polynomial Volterra processes. As an application, we propose a weak approximation principle for stochastic Volterra equations based on matching low-order expected signature coordinates of the kernel. Numerical experiments for Volterra-Jacobi processes demonstrate promising performance.

Probability.title: Stochastic Operator Algebras: Intrinsic Cumulant Geometry
Probability.summary: If an orthogonal projection splits a random vector into independent parts, every mixed cumulant across the cut vanishes. For a family of cuts we identify the subspaces on which higher cumulants can survive. A distance bound on vectors characterizes when square-integrable defects at the individual cuts admit a simultaneous correction by a Hilbert tensor. The criterion is the same in every integer degree $r\ge3$ and can be tested on Hilbert-space-valued random variables. For laws fixed by random recombination, uniform cutting supplies the moment asked for by Courtade. The minimum dimension of a nonzero finite-dimensional common reducing subspace determines the optimal fourth-moment ratio. A separate application to polynomial optimization characterizes the $r^{-2}$ push-forward rate on a convex body by the boundary area of sublevel sets at regular minima.

Probability.title: The Poissonian limit of a model inspired by the one-dimensional ERAP, and its application to satellite data
Probability.summary: We consider a model of particle tracking in one dimension studied by Quarck in which $n$ independent random points of the interval $[0,1]$ are shifted by i.i.d. noise at a common scale $\varepsilon_n>0$. We prove that, if $\varepsilon_n=αn^{-2}+\mathbf{o}(n^{-2})$ for some $α>0$ when $n\to \infty$, then in the latter limit the total number of consecutive swaps in the shifted sample w.r.t. its order statistics converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with a parameter depending explicitly on the product of $α$, the mean absolute difference of the shifts and the $L^2$-norm of the density of points. We compare the statistical criterion implied by this theorem to numerical simulations based on real terrain maps, and discuss both its usefulness and limitations.

Probability.title: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration
Probability.summary: We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.

Probability.title: Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests
Probability.summary: Let $F_q$ be the rooted forest sampled by Wilson's algorithm for a finite reversible Markov chain killed at rate $q$. We express the probability that $k$ prescribed vertices are roots as a product. For the $i$th factor, start an evolving set from the singleton consisting of the $i$th vertex, in the domain obtained by removing the preceding $i-1$ vertices. The factor is the probability that the set contains its starting vertex at an independent exponential time of rate $q$. These factors are the successive Schur-complement pivots of the determinantal root kernel. The construction couples the walk up to its exit from a domain with the evolving set biased by its mass. For the ordinary evolving set, the expected mass at that time divided by the initial mass is the probability that the walk has not yet left the domain. We use the probability that a second walk hits the first Wilson branch to bound the probability that two vertices belong to the same component. For a symmetric transition kernel, the expected size of the component of any vertex is at most $(1+1/q)^2$. Under a Gaussian heat-kernel upper bound with exponent $ν>4$, we also obtain spatial decay on the scale $q^{-1/2}$, up to a finite-volume correction.

Probability.title: A lower bound on the Nusselt number in stochastically forced Rayleigh--Bénard convection
Probability.summary:
We establish a lower bound on the expected long-time averaged Nusselt number for two-dimensional Rayleigh--Bénard convection at infinite Prandtl number, with free-slip boundaries and a suitable additive noise of amplitude $0<σ\leq1$ in the temperature equation. For every deterministic initial temperature, we prove that \[
  \underline{Nu}-1
  \geq c(σ^3 Ra)^{7/192}, \] provided that \[
  σ^3 Ra
  \geq C(1+\log(1/σ))^{192/7}, \] where $c,C>0$ depend only on the domain parameter $L$. Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number.
  The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional Itô process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.

Probability.title: Inhomogeneous long-range percolation in the weak decay regime
Probability.summary: We study a general class of percolation models in Euclidean space including long-range percolation, scale-free percolation, the weight-dependent random connection model and several other previously investigated models. Our focus is on the weak decay regime, in which inter-cluster long-range connection probabilities fall off polynomially with small exponent, and for which we establish several structural properties. Chief among them are the continuity of the bond percolation function and the transience of infinite clusters.
Probability.comment: 32 pages. v3 incorporates journal revisions and corrects the introductory integrability assumption to require integrability only at infinity; fixes minor typos. Main results unchanged

Probability.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
Probability.summary:
We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare its hitting probabilities with those of the homogeneous walk whose conductances are fixed at the starting time. These estimates give another proof of two results of Li and Park, who work under more general assumptions. If the upper network is recurrent, the walk visits every vertex infinitely often almost surely. If the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite.
  Let us first consider the probability of leaving a finite set before hitting a given vertex. The difference between this probability and its value for the frozen walk is bounded in absolute value by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. On an initially transient network, we obtain a lower bound on the probability of never hitting the vertex. Both proofs use a comparison of two Dirichlet forms and a contraction property of the killed transition operators.
  We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$ for a constant $a$ depending only on the dimension and the ellipticity bound.

Probability.title: Extension of results on generalized Pólya's urns for polynomially self-repelling walks
Probability.summary: This is a technical note which extends the results of Kosygina, Mountford and Peterson (Ann. Probab., 51(5):1684-1728, 2023, Section 4) about generalized Pólya's urns from a specific weight function $w(n) = (n+1)^{-α}$ to a general family of weight functions satisfying $(w(n))^{-1}=n^α\left(1+2Bn^{-1}+O\left(n^{-2}\right)\right)$ as $n \to \infty$. The latter was considered by Tóth (Ann. Probab., 24(3):1324-1367, 1996) as a part of his study of polynomially self-repelling walks. This extension is used in the study of scaling limits of these walks and related processes; see arXiv:2610.28935 and arXiv:2610.38591.

Probability.title: Directed acyclic graph-type distributed ledgers via young-age preferential attachment
Probability.summary: Distributed Ledger Technologies provide a mechanism to achieve ordering among transactions that are scattered on multiple participants with no prerequisite trust relations. This mechanism is essentially based on the idea of new transactions referencing older ones in a chain structure. Recently, DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are based on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) were proposed to increase the system scalability through sacrificing the total order of transactions. In this paper, we develop a mathematical model to study the process that governs the addition of new transactions to the DAG-type Distributed Ledger. We propose a simple model for DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are obtained from a recursive Young-age Preferential Attachment scheme, i.e. new connections are made preferably to transactions that have not been in the system for very long. We determine the asymptotic degree structure of the resulting graph and show that a forward component of linear size arises if the edge density is chosen sufficiently large in relation to the `young-age preference' that tunes how quickly old transactions become unattractive.
Probability.comment: Revised manuscript incorporating journal revisions and additional minor corrections. 22 pages, 4 figures

Probability.title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
Probability.summary: We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.

Probability.title: Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI
Probability.summary: We study the ferromagnetic random field Ising model (RFIM) on a graph $G=(V,E)$ having maximal degree $Δ$, where the external field at each vertex is an i.i.d. random variable. When the random field distribution is sufficiently anti-concentrated, we prove that with high probability over the quenched randomness of the external field, the Glauber dynamics of this RFIM mixes in polynomial time as a consequence of a Poincaré inequality. This model is relevant to the Griffiths phase where the correlations decay exponentially fast in expectation over the quenched random field, but contraction does not hold point-wise due to the existence of weak fields that lead to low-temperature behavior. Previously, fast mixing of Glauber dynamics under large disorder was only proven on the integer lattice, and for RFIM on general graphs, only a sampling algorithm based on self-avoiding walks was known. Under a further technical condition that the random fields are bounded, we prove a modified log-Sobolev inequality for the Glauber dynamics. When the random field is weaker but still satisfies weak spatial mixing (exponential decay of correlations from boundary to bulk) in expectation, and the graph has $α$-stretched-exponential growth for some $α<1$, we prove a weak Poincaré inequality. If weak spatial mixing holds uniformly along a given sequence of growing induced subgraphs, we further obtain a polynomial-time sampling algorithm based on Glauber dynamics with warm starts. These results extend the corresponding weak Poincaré and sampling results from the integer lattice to graphs with $α$-stretched-exponential growth.
Probability.comment: 33 pages. Conference version accepted in RANDOM 2026, journal version to appear in Random Structures & Algorithms

Probability.title: Universality for persistence exponents of local times of self-similar processes with stationary increments
Probability.summary: We show that $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)=(c_X+o(1))T^{-(1-H)}$, where $\ell_X$ is the local time measure at $0$ of any recurrent $H$-self-similar real-valued process $X$ with stationary increments that admits a sufficiently regular local time and $c_X$ is some constant depending only on $X$. A special case is the Gaussian setting, i.e. when the underlying process is fractional Brownian motion, in which our result settles a conjecture by Molchan [Commun. Math. Phys. 205, 97-111 (1999)] who obtained the upper bound $1-H$ on the decay exponent of $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)$. Our approach establishes a new connection between persistence probabilities and Palm theory for self-similar random measures, thereby providing a general framework which extends far beyond the Gaussian case.
Probability.comment: Revised manuscript incorporating journal revisions; corrected the boundary-measure condition in Theorem 4(ii). 32 pages

Probability.title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
Probability.summary: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

Probability.title: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions
Probability.summary: The quadratic Wasserstein distance between Gaussian distributions is given by the classical Bures-Wasserstein formula, which depends only on the means, the covariance matrices $Σ_0$ and $Σ_1$, and their interaction $K=(Σ_0^{1/2}Σ_1Σ_0^{1/2})^{1/2}$. The same formula holds for elliptical distributions with a common radial law. In this paper, we extend this representation to general elliptical distributions by identifying an additional transport cost $Γ$ that depends on the radial laws and the spectrum of $K$. We describe $Γ$ via a weighted quadratic transport problem involving Dirichlet distributions and show that optimal couplings preserve directions within the eigenspaces of $K$. When $K$ has a single eigenvalue, we obtain an explicit cost formula and an optimal Monge map. For general spectra, we derive remarkably tight lower and upper bounds for $Γ$ using nested spectral projections and Knothe-Rosenblatt couplings. The lower bound is based on one-dimensional integrals and can be computed fast. For Gaussian, Student-$t$, uniform ball, and uniform sphere distributions, the upper bound also admits computationally efficient representations via dynamic programming. Numerical experiments demonstrate that we reduce the gap between the previously known bounds by more than 80% in many settings, and by over 99.9% in certain scenarios, even in dimension $10^6$. These improvements are particularly valuable in high-dimensional or heavy-tailed settings, where accurate numerical computation of quadratic Wasserstein distances is challenging.

Probability.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
Probability.summary: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

Probability.title: Large deviation principle of error of Euler--Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations
Probability.summary: We study large deviations for the error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation with $C_b^3$ coefficients and a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient. We prove that the error at the terminal time, without rescaling, satisfies a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n$, where $n$ is the number of steps, with a good rate function that vanishes only at the origin. In particular, the probability that the error exceeds a fixed level decays exponentially in $n$. Two effects determine the rate function. A single Brownian increment of fixed nonzero size has finite cost at speed $n$, and the cumulative effect of smaller Brownian increments depends on the states at which their squares accumulate. To capture both effects, we introduce, for a cutoff $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, an empirical enhanced control that records the state-dependent quadratic variation of the small increments together with the time, state and size of each increment exceeding $\varepsilon$. We prove an LDP for the empirical enhanced control for every fixed $\varepsilon$, and deduce the LDP for the error by the contraction principle and an exponentially good approximation as $\varepsilon\to0$.

Probability.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
Probability.summary: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.

Probability.title: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment
Probability.summary: We introduce a sufficient criterion for ballistic motion of interface evolutions in random environments. More precisely, we consider interfaces moving by forced mean curvature flow in dimension $d=2$ with a spatially fluctuating (possibly negative) driving force. Such models arise e.g. from the motions of dislocation lines or magnetic domain walls in a material with impurities. We show that the evolution admits an `effective minimum speed on large scales' if for a sample of the random environment in some long and thin box there is a sufficiently large probability that an interface initialized in the bottom of the box evolves to reach its top. The concept of an `effective minimum speed on large scales' was introduced and is required for the quantitative stochastic homogenization result in the companion paper ``Quantitative homogenization of forced geometric motions through random fields of obstacles''. We show that our criterion and hence the requirements for the homogenization result in the companion paper are satisfied for compactly supported obstacle shapes distributed according to a Poisson point process with sufficiently low intensity.

Probability.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
Probability.summary: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing). We establish tight first-order asymptotics for the size of the reachable set from a fixed vertex, and also determine the first-order asymptotics of the lengths of the longest and shortest increasing paths with one or two fixed endpoints.

Probability.title: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals
Probability.summary: We study steady-state diffusion approximations for a many-server queue driven by overdispersed arrivals from a doubly stochastic Poisson process. Its arrival intensity follows a generalized Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) process, where $α\in [0, 1)$ governs how the arrival-count variance scales as $λ^{1+α}$ with the baseline arrival rate $λ$ under Taylor's law. For $α> 0$, arrival-intensity fluctuations grow faster with $λ$ than counting fluctuations from arrivals and departures, so normalizing by $λ^{(1+α)/2}$ pairs a nonvanishing intensity volatility with a vanishing queue-length volatility. This two-scale formulation differs critically from conventional diffusion approximations, which either apply a single $λ^{1/2}$ scaling with nonvanishing volatilities or drop the vanishing queue-length noise in the heavy-traffic limit. Retaining both scales, we compare two diffusions: one replaces the scaled intensity with its limiting Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process, and the other preserves the exact CIR intensity. Using Stein's method, we establish steady-state error bounds for smooth test functions of arbitrary polynomial growth that depend on $α$ in opposite directions. Both diffusions achieve the classical $O(λ^{-1/2})$ rate at $α= 0$. For $α\in (0, 1)$, however, the OU rate degrades to the sharp order $O(λ^{-(1-α)/2})$, whereas preserving the CIR intensity improves the rate to $O(λ^{-(2+α)/4})$. Our proofs establish new derivative bounds for the associated Poisson equations that remain valid when the diffusion has vanishing volatility and nonsmooth drift.

Probability.title: The sharp uniqueness threshold for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on regular trees
Probability.summary: We study Gibbs uniqueness for the $q$-state antiferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite rooted $d$-ary tree and the infinite $(d+1)$-regular tree, where $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. An edge has weight $p\in[0,1]$ if its endpoints have the same color and weight $1$ otherwise. We prove that there is a unique Gibbs state if and only if $p\geqslant p_c:=\max\{0,1-q/(d+1)\}$, except when $(q,p)=(d+1,0)$, thus completes the uniqueness thresholds for all $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. Our proof use a convex potential for the tree recursion and show that it strictly decreases away from the uniform distribution. Together with the result of Gu, Wu and Yang, our theorem gives the exact critical power law whenever $p_c>0$.

Probability.title: Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs
Probability.summary: We study backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) in infinite horizon and {design} efficient numerical schemes for solving them. We establish a probabilistic representation of the solution of the BSDE using Malliavin derivative and prove results for contraction of a Picard scheme. We develop three numerical schemes, of which the first two are based on a fixed point argument using contraction, imposing additional assumptions compared to what is needed for existence and uniqueness of the solution. The first scheme is a space grid based approximation where we establish tight numerical error bounds using a growth truncation argument; it performs well in low dimensions but computational times increase exponentially with dimension. The second scheme uses neural network approximations for which we have proved a convergence result. Using neural networks alleviates the curse of dimensionality, giving good accuracy in very high dimensions. The third scheme also uses neural networks but does not directly rely on a contraction scheme, showcasing good performance even for larger z-Lipschitz dependence outside the empirical domain of contraction.

Probability.title: Seed thresholds and degree variance in heterogeneous bootstrap percolation with growing degrees
Probability.summary:
We study bootstrap percolation with independent vertex thresholds taking values one and two, with threshold-one probability $(1-c/d)/d$ for fixed $c>0$. The seed set is chosen uniformly among sets of a prescribed deterministic size, independently of the graph and thresholds. We prove threshold statements at fixed relative margins. For uniform simple graphs with prescribed nonnegative integer degrees of even sum and exact mean $d$, assume $\max_i|d_i-d|\le C\sqrt d$ and $c+1-v_n\geκ>0$, where $v_n=\operatorname{Var}(D)/d$ and $C,κ$ are fixed. When $d\to\infty$ and $d=o(n^{1/7})$, the leading seed scale is $n(c+1-v_n)^2/(2d^4)$, without requiring a limit of $v_n$. At fixed relative margins below and above this scale, the final active set has size $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$, respectively, with high probability. For regular graphs, the supercritical conclusion strengthens to full activation. For $G(n,d/n)$, the same $O(n/d^3)$ and $n-o(n)$ conclusions hold when $d\to\infty$ and $d^5/n\to0$, with seed scale $nc^2/(2d^4)$. Thus regular and independent-edge graphs have different coefficients at the same asymptotic mean degree. Local exploration estimates yield explicit inactive remainders and survive conditioning on simplicity in the prescribed model. We also quantify the precision obstruction to static inclusion transfer and compute deterministic response-barrier corrections, without identifying a shrinking random critical window.
  A separate appendix gives the corresponding fixed-margin terminal bounds for iid thresholds of fixed bounded support, with unchanged threshold-one probability and threshold-two mass bounded away from zero.
Probability.comment: 31 pages. In v3, Appendix C extends the fixed-margin terminal bounds to iid thresholds of fixed bounded support

Probability.title: Coexistence and extinction in stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems with Volterra--Lyapunov stable interactions
Probability.summary: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(α+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)Γ\,dB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. Let $β=α-\frac12\mathrm{diag}(ΓΓ^\top)$ be the vector of noise-corrected growth rates and $m=-A^{-1}β$. We show that the process has a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities if and only if $m>0$. In that case the process is strongly stochastically persistent, and its stationary distribution is unique and has mean $m$. When $m>0$ fails, the species that survive are those present in the unique saturated nonnegative equilibrium $\bar x$ of the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(β+Ax)$. Almost surely, the occupation measures converge to the stationary distribution of this subcommunity, and $\log X_i(t)/t$ converges to $(β+A\bar x)_i\le0$ for every species $i$. The proofs rely on the theory of invasion rates of Hening and Nguyen. For Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Combined with two quadratic identities, this provides explicit weights $Dm$ for their persistence theorem and identifies the limiting regime when persistence fails, without enumerating the invariant measures on the boundary.

Probability.title: Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resistance forms
Probability.summary: In this paper, we study discrete approximations of semi-Dirichlet forms obtained by adding non-symmetric drift terms, expressed in terms of mutual energy measures, to resistance forms whose associated resistance metric spaces are compact. The main novelty is that the drift terms need not to be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Under suitable smallness assumptions, we prove generalized Mosco convergence of the approximating forms and derive weak convergence of the associated Feller processes. We also demonstrate the applicability of our main theorem to post-critically finite self-similar fractals and describe the resulting perturbation of the approximating jump chains in the case of the Sierpiński gasket.

Probability.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
Probability.summary: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.
Probability.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. This Letter is aimed at physicists and mathematicians who are primarily interested in the global picture. Full mathematical details will be presented in a forthcoming paper

Probability.title: The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
Probability.summary: We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.

Probability.title: The clumsy coupon collector's problem
Probability.summary: We consider a generalisation of the classical coupon collector's problem, in which at each time step a collector either receives a new copy of a randomly chosen coupon, or loses all their previously collected copies of that coupon. We consider the amount of time it takes this clumsy coupon collector to obtain the full set of $m$ coupons. We establish limit theorems as $m\to\infty$ for the clumsy coupon collection time, and describe the large $m$ asymptotics of its mean and variance. We identify three regimes, depending on how the probability of a clumsy update, $p$, scales with $m$.
