If $p=o(1/m)$, we obtain a Gumbel limit theorem, as is the case for the classical coupon collector. If $p=ω(1/m)$, we instead show weak convergence to an exponential random variable. In the critical case, $p\sim c/m$, we give a full characterisation of the limiting distribution in terms of a birth-and-death process. We also describe the asymptotics of the mean and variance in these three regimes.

Probability.title: Counting tree-child and reticulation visible networks
Probability.summary:
For tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulations, we identify an entire critical scaling function at $k=x\sqrt n$ and its first uniform correction. The function is a Gaussian factor times the Laplace transform of Brownian excursion area. An exact coefficient integral then yields the explicit amplitude $π\Ai'(a_1)$ for the maximal-reticulation count, where $a_1$ is the largest negative Airy zero, together with three logarithmic corrections. A summable defect expansion transfers these results to the total number of tree-child networks.
  For reticulation-visible networks, we construct an exact weighted refinement over maximal tree-child networks. The total defect from $3n-3$ reticulations splits into a skeleton defect, an arity excess, and an ordinary-leaf count. The skeleton defect has a uniformly bounded exponential moment, and the full partition function differs from its maximal-skeleton sector by a bounded factor, smaller than $30$ at activity one. A positive algebraic kernel and an explicitly solved variational problem give the pressure with logarithmic error $O(n^{2/3}\log^{2/3}n)$. This determines the total exponential growth, the location of every mode, a full large-deviation principle, and limiting structural densities. At activity $z=t/n$ with fixed $t>0$, we also prove a $\operatorname{Poisson}(19t/4)$ limit and coefficient asymptotics uniform for defects $q=o(n^{1/3})$.

Probability.title: Reflection positivity of discrete and Brownian loop-soup occupation fields
Probability.summary: The intensities guaranteeing reflection positivity of loop-soup vertex occupations on every reflection-symmetric finite graph with positive semidefinite cross-conductance matrix of rank $r$ form the real Wallach set $\W_r$. For the renormalized occupation field on the massless planar Dirichlet strip, the exact set is $\bigcap_{r\geq1}\W_r=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$.

Probability.title: Computing expectations associated with McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations via probability-flow ordinary differential equations
Probability.summary: This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. The resulting mean-field ODE eliminates the need to approximate Itô integrals and permits the use of higher-order integration schemes in time and stochastic space. However, simulating trajectories requires the score function of the MV-SDE's marginal law, which is approximated using a statistical estimator based on a system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional ODEs. The proposed estimator combines randomized quasi-MC in the stochastic variables and Runge--Kutta integrators in time, with efficient score estimation. Under assumptions on weak-error and variance convergence, the resulting estimator achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\text{TOL}^{-\left(\max\{β/α,2\} + 1/γ\right)}\right)$, where $α$ and $β$ denote, respectively, the weak-error and variance convergence rates with respect to $P$, and $γ$ is the order of the time-integration scheme.

Probability.title: Invariant measures for stochastic heat equations with dissipative drift in the whole space
Probability.summary: We study the long-time behavior of a nonlinear stochastic heat equation on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, driven by a Gaussian noise that is white in time and spatially homogeneous. The equation features a reaction term $f$ satisfying a one-sided Lipschitz condition and a bounded, globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient $σ$. Solutions are constructed in a scale of weighted continuous function spaces. Under an additional dissipativity condition on $f$, which covers reaction terms of the form $f(u)=u-u^{3}$, we prove that the transition semigroup admits an invariant measure on some weighted space $C_ρ$. This constitutes the first step toward a complete ergodic theory for dissipative stochastic heat equations on unbounded domains, a setting that has so far remained largely open in the literature.

Probability.title: Noncommutative $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed beta functions of first and second kind : beta gamma relations, shift identities and symmetrisation
Probability.summary: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $φ_{1}>φ_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominusφ_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplusφ_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $φ_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/Γ_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all complex arguments with positive real parts; we derive its general shift identity, its exchange defect $φ_{1}^{(y-x)(x+y-1)/2}$, a commutative symmetrisation unique up to a constant, its asymptotics and a deformed Euler integral for a deformed Gauss hypergeometric function, which yields a deformed Gauss summation. The second kind function is evaluated through Ramanujan's ${}_{1}ψ_{1}$ summation and involves a second deformed gamma function, differing from the first one by a one periodic theta quotient, so that its exchange defect persists in the one parameter case. We prove a Bohr Mollerup type characterisation and a multiplication formula for the deformed gamma function, show that it is logarithmically convex on the positive half line if and only if $φ_{1}\geq1$, obtain the joint logarithmic convexity of normalised beta functions with a deformed Turán identity, and compute the moments of the associated deformed beta distributions. Gauge invariance covers the Jagannathan Srinivasa Rao, Chakrabarti Jagannathan, generalized $q-$Quesne and Hounkonnou Ngompe deformations, and every identity is confirmed numerically to thirty digits.

Probability.title: Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model
Probability.summary: We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ is $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\}) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where the conductances $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\})$ are independent, uniformly elliptic and have a common mean. Below the critical exponent $(d+2)$ the walk converges to a stable process; above it, to Brownian motion with diffusive $\sqrt{t}$ scaling. At criticality the second moment of the jump kernel diverges logarithmically. We establish quantitative homogenization of the associated heat equation at the rate $1/\sqrt{|\ln \varepsilon|}$. As a consequence, we deduce annealed convergence of the random walk to Brownian motion under the anomalous $\sqrt{t \log t}$ scaling. Unlike in standard homogenization, the effective diffusivity is determined by the mean conductance alone, with no corrector contribution at leading order.
Probability.comment: 16 pages, 1 Figure. This version has been revised, streamlined, and shortened. New sections on Lean formalization and the use of AI have also been added. Lean formalization available at https://github.com/nitromannitol/critical-long-range-conductance

Probability.title: Gaussian integrals on symmetric spaces (the complex case and beyond)
Probability.summary: The present work deals with Gaussian integrals on Riemannian symmetric spaces of the non-compact type. These integrals arise in statistics as well as in physics. The present work offers a systematic approach to their asymptotic behavior in the high-rank limit. First, this limit is computed explicitly in the complex case (the isometry group is a complex Lie group). To go beyond the complex case, a variational formulation is introduced, which yields the required limit as (minus) the minimum of a certain energy functional defined on the space of probability distributions on the real line. This new formulation allows for the high-rank limit to be recovered in explicit form, from the original expression found in the complex case. This two-step approach is illustrated for two classes of symmetric spaces : symmetric cones and classical symmetric domains.

Probability.title: Uniformly positive correlations in the dimer model and phase transition in lattice permutations on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d > 2$, via reflection positivity
Probability.summary: Our first main result is that correlations between monomers in the dimer model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ do not decay to zero when $d > 2$. This is the first rigorous result about correlations in the dimer model in dimensions greater than two and shows that the model behaves drastically differently than in two dimensions, in which case it is integrable and correlations are known to decay to zero polynomially. Such a result is implied by our more general, second main result, which states the occurrence of a phase transition in the model of lattice permutations, which is related to the quantum Bose gas. More precisely, we consider a self-avoiding walk interacting with lattice permutations and we prove that, in the regime of fully-packed loops, such a walk is `long' and the distance between its end-points grows linearly with the diameter of the box. These results follow from the derivation of a version of the infrared bound from a new general probabilistic settings, with coloured loops and walks interacting at sites and walks entering into the system from some `virtual' vertices. In dimension $d=3$ we use a transfer matrix argument to obtain a sharper infrared bound.
Probability.comment: 42 pages, 9 figures. This version corrects an error in the computation of a constant in v3 that left the proof of long-range order for the three-dimensional dimer model incomplete

Probability.title: A note on slicing
Probability.summary: We give a short proof of Bourgain's slicing theorem with the explicit bound $L_K\leq\sqrt{5/π}$ for every convex body $K$. The argument combines the strong thin-shell inequality obtained from the moment-measure method of Chen and Klartag with an entropy estimate along Eldan's stochastic localization. The proof uses neither $M$-ellipsoid theory nor the reverse Santaló inequality.

Probability.title: Breaking Resonance: Square-root acceleration for Metropolis-adjusted randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
Probability.summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a fixed integration time can fail to mix because of resonances, and randomizing the integration time removes them. We prove that Metropolis-adjusted HMC with velocity Verlet and random integration times mixes from a warm start in a number of transitions that does not depend on the condition number, for every integration-time law satisfying a Fourier condition that we call non-resonant; uniform, exponential and triangular laws are examples. For a target density proportional to $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$, where $U$ is $m$-strongly convex with $L$-Lipschitz gradient and $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian and $κ=L/m$, the number of gradient evaluations needed to reach a fixed total variation accuracy is, up to constants and logarithmic factors, $\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}\,(d/m)^{3/4}$. This is the first square-root condition-number bound for this sampler beyond Gaussian targets. The proof converts relative-entropy contraction of the unadjusted proposal into a conductance bound for the adjusted chain, and shows that the integration-time law enters only through its characteristic function. Hessian regularity cannot be dropped for a fixed step size: without it there are targets in the class for which the cost is at least of order $κ^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic factors, even from a warm start.
Probability.comment: 40 pages, 5 figures. Lean 4 formalization of the main results at https://github.com/nawafbourabee/breaking-resonance-lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24483261)

Probability.title: Explicit two-sided estimates and exact boundary regularity for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation
Probability.summary: Consider the transition density $\mathrm{p}^D_t(x,y)$ of the underdamped Langevin process absorbed outside of the cylindrical domain $D:=(0,1)\times\mathbb{R}$. We prove explicit and sharp \emph{two-sided estimates} satisfied by $\mathrm{p}^D_t$ on $D\times D$. We also establish the $C^\infty$ regularity of $\mathrm{p}^D$ on $\mathbb{R}_+^*\times(\overline{D}\setminusΓ^0)\times(\overline{D}\setminusΓ^0)$ where $Γ^0$ corresponds to the grazing boundary points. It is also shown to be $(1/6,1/2)$ Hölder continuous in the $(q,p)$ coordinates in a neighborhood of $Γ^0$. Finally, the long-time asymptotics of the absorbed transition density $\mathrm{p}^D_t(x,y)$ is obtained allowing to prove the uniform conditional ergodicity of the absorbed semigroup.
Probability.comment: Two main changes: extension of the two-sided estimates to general smooth forces, description of the exact boundary regularity of the absorbed transition density. Also, mistakes in the previous draft were corrected

Probability.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
Probability.summary: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].

Probability.title: Poisson Statistics for Values of Binary Quadratic Forms in Short Intervals
Probability.summary: We study the number of integers represented by a binary quadratic form in short intervals. Extending the work of Freiberg, Kurlberg, and Rosenzweig on sums of two squares, we formulate an analogue of the Hardy--Littlewood prime $k$-tuple conjecture for the integers represented by a genus of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of a fixed negative discriminant. We show that this hypothesis implies that the number of integers represented by a genus, and by each class in the genus, in a random interval $(n,n+y]$ with $n\le x$, where $y$ is $τ$ times the average spacing $\sqrt{\log x}/b(d)$, is asymptotically Poisson distributed with parameter $τ$. The proof uses the method of moments, with Bernays' asymptotic for the number of represented integers in place of the prime number theorem, and an adaptation of Ford's simplified argument for the average of the singular series. We also give numerical evidence for the hypothesis.

Probability.title: The smallest singular value of a random sign matrix: the Spielman-Teng conjecture
Probability.summary: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with independent uniform entries in $\{-1,1\}$. We prove that $\mathbb{P}(s_{\min}(A) \leq \varepsilon n^{-1/2}) \leq \varepsilon + e^{-cn}$ for all $\varepsilon \geq 0$ and an absolute $c > 0$, as conjectured by Spielman and Teng. For $e^{-cn} \leq \varepsilon \leq n^{-θ}$, with $θ> 0$ absolute and $n$ sufficiently large, the upper bound improves to $\varepsilon(1 - 1/(2n) + O(n^{-1.02}))$. The proof does not give numerical values for the dimension threshold or the exponential rate. We obtain the first-order improvement by comparing a Gaussian surface integral for the sign ensemble with its counterpart for independent spherical rows. An arithmetic small-ball estimate transfers this comparison to exponentially small scales. At polynomial scales, weighting by a coordinate of the least left singular vector yields a negative quadratic term in the crossing density.

Probability.title: Support geometry of the stationary distribution for a parabolic nonlinear AR(1) process with binary innovations
Probability.summary: This paper studies the nonlinear AR(1) process \(X_{n+1}=f(X_n)+σξ_{n+1}\), \(n\ge0\), driven by binary innovations \(ξ_n\in\{0,1\}\), where \(f\) is strictly increasing and strictly concave, with \(f(0)=0\), \(f'(0)=1\), and \(f'(x)<1\) for \(x>0\). The process is shown to have a unique stationary distribution. The geometry of its support is described in terms of the noise amplitude \(σ\) and the function \(f\): the support is either an interval or a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero, and the two regimes are separated by the relation between \(σ\) and the unique number \(c_σ>0\) solving \(c_σ-f(c_σ)=σ\). Namely, the support is an interval when \(c_σ\ge2σ\) and a Cantor set when \(c_σ<2σ\). Under the additional condition \(\ell_\infty:=\lim_{x\to\infty}f'(x)<1/2\), there exists a unique critical value \(σ_c>0\), characterized by \(f(2σ_c)=σ_c\), such that the support is an interval for \(0<σ\leσ_c\) and a Cantor set for \(σ>σ_c\); if \(\ell_\infty\ge1/2\), the support is an interval for every \(σ>0\). In the Cantor regime the stationary distribution is non-atomic, and hence singular continuous.

Probability.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and α-stable processes
Probability.summary: In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $α$-stable Lévy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/α_2,\,1/(ν+2)\}}$, where $α_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $ν$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows. We first derive the intermediate step of the averaging principle to average out the effect of fast-variable oscillations on the system, although the averaged variable still depends on $\varepsilon$. We obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1-1/α_2}$. Furthermore, under the uniformly quasi-periodic conditions, we show that the slow component converges strongly to the solution of some autonomous averaged equation, whose coefficients independent of $\varepsilon$. We thus obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1/(ν+2)}$. The main contribution of this paper is to extend the additive Lévy noise to multiplicative Lévy noise and extend the fast equation of the system from the autonomous setting to the non-autonomous setting. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the quasi-periodic setting, extending the corresponding results for the periodic case.

Probability.title: An extended Matsumoto--Yor property for free GIG distributions
Probability.summary: We prove a two-parameter extension of the Matsumoto--Yor property for free generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. The transformation is the reciprocal form of a known matrix Yang--Baxter map. Our proof combines the independence-preserving property for matrix generalized inverse Gaussian distributions with asymptotic freeness. Since the relevant spectra stay in compact subsets of the positive half-line, continuous functional calculus and polynomial approximation suffice to handle all inverses. The same argument yields the free Matsumoto--Yor property itself for all positive rates of the free Poisson law, including those for which this law has an atom at zero. We also discuss the limit in which one of the two parameters tends to zero: the limiting laws are free Poisson only when the rate is at least one, so for smaller rates this limit does not recover the free Matsumoto--Yor property.

Probability.title: The Anatomy of Piecewise-Linear Learned Indexes
Probability.summary:
Piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) learned indexes (PGM-index, FITing-Tree, RadixSpline, PLEX, PLIN) compress sorted keys into $\pm\varepsilon$ segments, yet prior theory stops at coarse $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ single-segment bounds. At the bottom layer, optimal greedy PLA covers $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2/v_0 \approx 3.54\,\varepsilon^2/v_0$ keys per segment on independent gaps and $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2$ under any smooth density ($v_0=1$), while anchored and chord fitters retain $Θ(\varepsilon^2/v_0)$ coverage. Across recursive layers, a law-of-large-numbers heuristic--invoked to claim $O(\log\log n)$ height for the PGM-index--suggests summing $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ gaps averages out fluctuations. We prove this fails under Endpoint Promotion (EP): stopping-time fluctuations reset relative gap variance at every depth, locking fanout at $C_\varepsilon \approx 19.861\,\varepsilon^2$, expected height at $\log n/\log C_\varepsilon + O(1)$, and lookup at $Θ(\log n)$.
  To break this barrier, Rank-Equispaced Promotion (RE) samples pivots at equal rank strides. Each stride sums a fixed number of base gaps, so relative variance decays across layers and cumulative coverage squares at each step. Expected height drops to $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + O(1)$ on independent gaps and $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + \log_2^+(\log n/\log(\varepsilon/δ)) + O(1)$ on smooth densities with curvature $δ$. A compact bucket directory routes across unaligned RE pivots with $<1$ extra comparison per layer on average, giving RE-PGM $O(\log\varepsilon \cdot \log\log_\varepsilon n)$ expected lookup in $Θ(n/\varepsilon^2)$ space and $O(n)$ build time without radix skew sensitivity. Our constants match empirical fanout within $0.3\%$ down to $\varepsilon=2$, and all core theorems are formalized in Lean 4.
Probability.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables; core theorems machine-checked in Lean 4

Probability.title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
Probability.summary:
We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$.
  The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are real-analytic and strictly convex.
  The principal innovation of the article is the use of a slide resampling that preserves the conditioned law. The slide acts by cutting the long finite connection at a given $\pmb{\ell}$-height and relocating the upper piece by a random shift. The mass gap is obtained by a delicate analysis of an iterated version of the slide operation along a positive density of attempted heights.
Probability.comment: 270 pages with thirteen figures. This paper supersedes arXiv:2408.16636 incorporating much of its content into Part I. The earlier preprint may be consulted for a freestanding proof of a stretched-exponential bound on renewal-block height

Probability.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature
Probability.summary: In this paper, we introduce the generalized Volterra signature \(\gvsig(\bX)\) of a path \(\bX\), extending the classical Volterra signature introduced in [Hager, Harang, Pelizzari \& Tindel, arXiv:2603.04525, 2026], which extends Lyons' path signature to the Volterra setting. We establish a new algebraic structure to encode the generalized Volterra signature. We also establish a generalized Chen's identity. By restricting the differential trees to ladder trees, we introduce the geometric Volterra signature \(\geovsig(\bX)\) and establish the shuffle product of its signature components. To the best of our knowledge, the shuffle product for the Volterra signature is the first of its kind and allows us to formulate a universal approximation theorem for geometric Volterra signatures. For a special class of kernel functions, we prove the existence of an extended path \(\Bar{\bX}\) and relate its classical signature to the geometric Volterra signature of the original path \(\bX\).

Probability.title: A Markov duration model with power-law decay via level-slope matching
Probability.summary: We develop a two-dimensional Markov duration model with power-law rate decay and a flexible residual distribution. The two state variables specify the excitation level and decay scale of a single power-law rate curve, and each update matches the level and slope jumps of a power-law Hawkes intensity. Under a sufficient stability condition, a finite residual mean, and a positive continuous residual density, the state at event times is positive Harris recurrent and converges geometrically in total variation to a unique invariant distribution. With unit exponential residuals, the sufficient region contains every parameter value for which the matched Hawkes process is subcritical. We apply the model to E-mini S\&P 500 futures and NVDA midquote durations at several price-change thresholds. Flexible residual laws improve likelihood-based fit, and power-law decay lowers one-step negative log predictive scores relative to exponential decay. An autoregressive conditional duration model generally leaves less residual autocorrelation, while forecast rankings vary with the price threshold and evaluation criterion.
Probability.comment: Updated the title, revised the model formulation and stability proofs, and added an empirical study of financial durations

Probability.title: Turnpike Estimates and Limiting Behavior for $N$-Player Differential Games under Displacement Monotonicity
Probability.summary: We study the long-time behavior of open-loop Nash equilibria of $N$-player stochastic differential games with nondegenerate idiosyncratic noise, under displacement monotonicity of the costs and joint strong convexity of the Lagrangians. We prove an exponential turnpike estimate: as the remaining horizon grows, the decoupling fields of the finite-horizon Pontryagin systems converge exponentially fast to the solution of a stationary Pontryagin system, which is unique in a natural stability class, and on bounded time intervals the equilibrium states and controls converge to those generated by this solution. The limiting control is a strong open-loop equilibrium of an associated ergodic $N$-player game, and the ergodic constant $λ^{i,N}$ of each player is the same at every such equilibrium. For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

Probability.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
Probability.summary:
The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data.
  Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

Probability.title: Pathwise Uniqueness for Cyclically Catalytic Branching Diffusions
Probability.summary: We study pathwise uniqueness for cyclic catalytic stochastic differential equations whose state-dependent square-root diffusion coefficients are non-Lipschitz and degenerate on the boundary. The approach is the direct construction of a strong solution using a Malliavin compactness criterion. The key is the development of a new family of boundary-sensitive weighted Malliavin estimates for the tangent processes of the smooth approximations. Pathwise uniqueness then follows from the dual Yamada-Watanabe argument together with the weak uniqueness available in the literature.

Probability.title: Generalized Wishart processes under nonlinear expectation
Probability.summary: We develop a theory of generalized Wishart processes within the framework of $G$-expectation, with $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and the $G$-Wishart process as two typical examples. In contrast to the classical setting, we show that $G$-Dyson Brownian motion may exhibit collisions and provide a sufficient condition ensuring the non-collision property of the eigenvalues of generalized Wishart processes. We then derive the equations governing the high-dimensional limits of the empirical spectral measures under $G$-expectation, leading to the corresponding semicircle law for $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and Marchenko--Pastur law for the $G$-Wishart process.

Probability.title: Analytic properties of distributions associated with multi-state Random Number Generators
Probability.summary: We analyze the analytic properties of probability distributions associated with possibly unfair, multi-state Random Number Generators (i.e., dice). Specifically, given a $q$-sided die, if $x_i\in \{0,\ldots, q-1\}$ denotes the outcome of the $i^{\text{th}}$ toss, then $F(x)=\mathbb{P}[X\leq x]$ is the associated cumulative distribution function---a probabilistic generalization of the famed Cantor function. We first establish easily computable bounds for the $L^1$-distance between the possibly unfair $F$ and the uniform distribution $y=x$. We then show that $F$ is both upper- and lower-Hölder continuous, where the associated Hölder exponents are shown to be sharp. Finally, we establish recursive formulae for the moments, $\mathbb{E}[X^n]$, associated with $F$ and use these moments to provide sequences of step-functions that converge uniformly to $F$ from above and below.

Probability.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
Probability.summary: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

Probability.title: A Direct Approach to Rough Differential Equations Driven by Controlled Rough Paths
Probability.summary: We study rough differential equations driven by controlled rough paths. Given a rough path $\mathbf X$ and an $\mathbf X$-controlled rough path $\mathbf Z$, we develop a direct controlled rough paths approach to the rough differential equation $dY_t=F(Y_t)\,d\mathbf Z_t$. More specifically, we establish rough integral estimates and the universal limit theorem directly in the space of $\X$-controlled rough paths.

Probability.title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
Probability.summary: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.

Probability.title: Concentration of the half-space Airy line ensembles
Probability.summary: The half-space Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{hs};\varpi}$ ($\varpi\in\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$), introduced in arXiv:2505.01798, arXiv:2601.04546, are natural analogues of the Airy line ensemble and are expected to arise as universal scaling limits of models in the half-space Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) class. We prove that, at each fixed time $t\geq 0$, the height of the $k$th curve concentrates about $-(3πk/2)^{2/3}$ on the scale $k^{-1/3}\sqrt{\log(2+k)}$, with exponential tails.

Probability.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
Probability.summary: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^β$ Poincaré inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $λ(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-β}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.

Probability.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
Probability.summary: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erdős--Rényi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $Θ(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit the minimum degree of~$G(n,W)$, giving simplified proofs of results of Hladký and Viswanathan~\cite{HV} and establishing the limiting distribution of $δ(G(n,W))$ under a second-order decorrelation condition.

Probability.title: Improving the efficiency of the ratio-of-uniforms method
Probability.summary: In 1977, Kinderman and Monahan showed that under certain conditions, a random variable can be expressed as the ratio $V/U$, where $(U,V)$ is uniformly distributed over a bounded region $S\subset{\mathds R}^2$. Thus, by generating values of $(U,V)$ and computing the indicated ratio, samples from the random variable can be obtained. This procedure is now known as the ratio-of-uniforms method and relies heavily on our ability to produce uniform samples from $S$, for which an acceptance-rejection method is customarily used. In this paper, we propose three sampling schemes based on the polar representation of $S$. The first uses a covering consisting of triangles, the second uses a covering based on circular sectors, while the third employs rectangular coverings of an associated angular density. Numerical examples illustrate that these schemes can achieve acceptance rates close to $100\%$.

Probability.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
Probability.summary: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.

Probability.title: Estimation for High-Dimensional Hawkes Processes with Inhibition via CIR Approximation
Probability.summary: In this paper, we develop a parametric estimation method for a high-dimensional Hawkes processes with inhibition. The proposed approach relies on a quantitative approximation of the Hawkes process by a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the joint large-population and long-time regime. This result requires specific techniques to handle the non-Lipschitz diffusion coefficient of the limiting CIR process.Based on this approximation, we construct explicit and easily implementable estimators of the model parameters. We establish their consistency and asymptotic normality. We also conduct numerical experiments to illustrate our findings.

Probability.title: Height function covariance and point-to-line coalescence in the directed landscape
Probability.summary: We prove an integration-by-parts formula for the KPZ fixed point with a deterministic $C_b^1$ terminal reward. For flat data, let $C(x)$ denote the spatial height covariance at time one. For almost every $x>0$, we show that $-C'(x)$ is the probability that the point-to-line geodesics started at $0$ and $x$ coalesce by time one. The proof uses Gaussian integration by parts for the O'Connell--Yor polymer, followed by the zero-temperature and directed-landscape limits.

Probability.title: Quantitative Convergence of the Nodal Length of Random Trigonometric Polynomials
Probability.summary:
We establish quantitative convergence results for the distribution of the nodal length of two-dimensional random trigonometric polynomials with independent and identically distributed centered coefficients towards that of the corresponding Gaussian limiting field. More precisely, we obtain an explicit polynomial rate of convergence.
  The proof combines probabilistic and geometric arguments. First, we establish quantitative convergence estimates for the underlying random fields. Using a suitable functional representation, this problem is reduced to the quantitative convergence of an empirical field towards a Brownian sheet in a Wasserstein-type distance. Second, Crofton's formula allows us to express the nodal length in terms of the zeros of the restrictions of the random trigonometric polynomials to parametrized affine lines. This reduction makes it possible to adapt one-dimensional arguments based on Kac's counting formula and transfer the convergence estimates for the random fields to the associated nodal lengths.

Probability.title: Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model
Probability.summary: We prove that the shape function of planar directed last-passage percolation with general i.i.d.\ real-valued weights is differentiable on the open first quadrant, under a moment assumption of order $p''>4$ on the positive part of the weight and a nearly optimal order $p'>1$ on the negative part. Due to known results, only directions outside a percolation cone need be considered. The proof is a multiscale path-counting argument that uses the shape theorem, oriented percolation on a coarse-grained lattice, a simple change of measure in a finite region, and the van den Berg--Kesten inequality. Our Lean-formalized proof is an AI-assisted adaptation and improvement of the OpenAI proof of differentiability in planar first-passage percolation.

Probability.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
Probability.summary: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_σ(\mathbb R^3)$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(Ω, \mathcal F_0; L^3_σ(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.
Probability.comment: 72 Pages, The minor compilation error due to \cref has been fixed. No changes in proofs and results

Probability.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
Probability.summary: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. Tóth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since Tóth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. Tóth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.

Probability.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
Probability.summary: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities. It distinguishes triangles supported by a common group from those requiring three distinct groups. Second, explicit representations of global and average local clustering reveal their different dependence on model parameters and the role of shared groups in edge correlations. Finally, by varying the strength and spatial range of group memberships, we establish convergence to random connection, random geometric, random intersection, Erdős--Rényi, and complete graphs. We characterize the corresponding clustering limits and show that clustering need not converge to that of the limiting graph, highlighting the distinction between spatially local convergence and global graph statistics.

Probability.title: Mortgage Backed Securities with p-Laplacian Diffusion and Random Prepayment
Probability.summary: In this note we consider deterministic and stochastic versions of a PDE pricing model for mortgage backed securities, driven by p-Laplacian motion. We show the existence of weak solutions in the $1<p<2$ case, for sufficiently small initial data. In the stochastic case, we consider a random prepayment function, when $p=2$. Herein we derive results concerning the uniform first order sensitivity and mean squared sensitivity of the solution, to the pricing model.

Probability.title: Concentration Inequalities for Exchangeable Tensors and Matrix-valued Data
Probability.summary:
We study concentration inequalities for structured weighted sums of random data, including (i) tensor inner products and (ii) sequential matrix sums. We are interested in tail bounds and concentration inequalities for those structured weighted sums under exchangeability, extending beyond the classical framework of independent terms.
  We develop Hoeffding and Bernstein bounds provided with structure-dependent exchangeability. Along the way, we recover known results in weighted sum of exchangeable random variables and i.i.d. sums of random matrices to the optimal constants. We also derive a concentration bound for combinatorial sums of matrix arrays with an improved constant in the bias term compared with that by the method of exchangeable pairs.
  For applications, the richer structures provide us with novel analytical tools for estimating the average effect of multi-factor response models and studying fixed-design sketching methods in federated averaging. We apply our results to these problems, and find that our theoretical predictions are corroborated by numerical evidence.
Probability.comment: 49 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in the SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science (SIMODS)

Probability.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
Probability.summary: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

Probability.title: Peripheral Traps and Lower Bounds on Mixing Times for Random Walks on Sparse Heavy-Tailed Random Intersection Graphs
Probability.summary:
This paper analyzes mixing time lower bounds for random walks on sparse, heavy-tailed Random Intersection Graphs. In sparse feature regimes, heavy-tailed feature distributions lead to the formation of peripheral trap -- chains of overlapping low-weight feature cliques attached to high-weight hub nodes within the graph's giant component.
  By modeling escape trajectories from these traps as continuous limit hitting times for reflected Brownian motion, the analysis demonstrates that random walks experience logarithmic squared delays. Consequently, the mixing time is bounded below by $Ω(\log^2 n)$, and the local total variation distance exhibits non-concentrated decay, formally preventing a sharp cutoff phenomenon.

Probability.title: Simultaneous coordinate-wise Wasserstein central limit theorem in high dimensions
Probability.summary:
For independent centered random vectors $(X_i)_{i=1}^n$ of finite fourth moments, we obtain dimension free Wasserstein bound between its normalized sum $W_n = n^{-1/2}\sum X_i$ and a Gaussian whose covariance equals that of $W_n$. The coupling between $W_n$ and the Gaussian is strong in the sense that a single coupling controls controls every projection onto a subset of those eigen coordinates. The proof combines stochastic localization, Hermite expansion on a Gaussian prior with exchangeable pairing. This proves the Conjecture surmised in \cite{fang2026sharp} and improves the coefficient on the fourth-moment term from $2$ to $197/108$.
  The same Wasserstein error bound extends to real separable Hilbert space. For Hilbert-valued i.i.d. observations, the $L^2$ prediction error bound has an order of $O(n^{-1/2})$, with no dimension factor or restriction on covariance eigenvalue decay, and the same coupling retains bounds for every spectral projection. In an $\ell^2$ example, we demonstrate that the coordinate-wise error gives sharp error order of $n^{-1/2}$.

Differential Geometry.title: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8π^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperkähler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

Differential Geometry.title: On triviality and scalar curvature estimation of gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons
Differential Geometry.summary: In this study we have explored gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons on both compact and complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. We have established several sufficient conditions for the triviality of such solitons with respect to integral inequalities involving the scalar curvature and the soliton function. In this regard, we have acquired scalar curvature estimation under certain $L^1$ and $L^2$ integrability conditions, and defined signal of the function $h$. Our results extend and refine former works on almost and $h$-almost Yamabe solitons, and characterize the geometric structures of generalized Yamabe solitons.

Differential Geometry.title: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
Differential Geometry.summary: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-Kähler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally products of two $3$-Sasakian manifolds. We construct compact examples for which these local decompositions are not global. Finally, compact normalized hyper contact pairs have finite fundamental group and are finite quotients of products of compact $3$-Sasakian manifolds, in contrast with normalized hyper contact--symplectic pairs, which may have infinite fundamental group.

Differential Geometry.title: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
Differential Geometry.summary:
Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins.
  Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

Differential Geometry.title: Polynomial Maximal Surfaces in $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ and Spherical Polygons
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the moduli space of complete maximal surfaces in pseudo-hyperbolic space $\mathbf{H}^{2,2}$ with polygonal asymptotic boundary a lightlike $(n+4)$-gon in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, up to the action of $\mathsf{SO}_0(2,3)$. Importantly, this space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ is disconnected for $n\geq 2$. We introduce a \emph{turning invariant} $Θ$ that classifies the components in terms of the geometry of the boundary polygons in the Einstein universe $\mathbf{Ein}^{1,2}$, which is related to \emph{spherical polygons} in $\mathbf{S}^2$. We provide a geometric parametrization of the moduli space $M_{n+4}(\mathbf{H}^{2,2})$ via holomorphic data, namely a pair of polynomials $α$, $β$. These polynomials appear in relation to certain components of the complexified second fundamental form of the corresponding surface. We then relate the holomorphic data $α$, $β$ to the turning invariant $Θ$. This leads to a characterization of the \emph{Hitchin component} of polygonal maximal surfaces studied by Tamburelli-Wolf.
Differential Geometry.comment: 39 pages, 3 figures, No AI. Minor expositional changes from v1

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $γ\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a closed, embedded, connected, oriented $C^1$ submanifold in $\mathbb R^n$ of dimension $m-1$ where $2\leq m<n$. We prove that the area of any immersed $m$-dimensional submanifold with oriented boundary $γ$ is bounded in terms of its curvature energy, unless $γ$ lies in an $m$-plane. The problems leads to a weak formulation involving oriented curvature varifolds with given oriented boundary, and we solve a boundary-value minimization problem with obstacle in this class.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp Casorati Inequalities for Pointwise Bi-Slant Riemannian Maps into Sasakian Space Forms
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish Casorati inequalities for pointwise bi-slant Riemannian maps into Sasakian space forms with the characteristic vector field tangent to the range. The Sasakian structure imposes specific conditions on the second fundamental form, leading to refined inequalities for the normalized horizontal scalar curvature that also account for O'Neill's tensor. For proper pointwise bi-slant maps, equality in the two principal inequalities is characterized by the vanishing of the second fundamental form on the orthogonal complement of the characteristic direction in the range. We also derive corresponding inequalities for pointwise semi-slant, hemi-slant, and slant Riemannian maps and construct examples attaining equality.

Differential Geometry.title: An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups
Differential Geometry.summary: By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.

Differential Geometry.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $π$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $π$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.

Differential Geometry.title: Elliptic Monotonicity Formulas for $p$-Green Functions
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we derive $p$-Laplace analogues of Colding's three monotonicity formulas in the original metric on complete noncompact $n$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, for $n\geq3$ and $1<p<n$. We assume a normalized positive minimal $p$-Green function vanishing at infinity with Euclidean pole asymptotics. Two complementary linearizations and the $p$-Bochner formula yield exact derivative identities with a common nonnegative defect involving an anisotropic trace-free Hessian and Ricci curvature. These identities give exterior cone rigidity and integral defect estimates, and recover the sharp gradient estimate and Euclidean rigidity of Mari--Rigoli--Setti. A one-parameter extension of Colding--Minicozzi type connects the formulas with known monotonicity and convexity identities for $p$-capacitary potentials.

Differential Geometry.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Erös--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fréchet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.
Differential Geometry.comment: 40 pages, 1 figure, some typographical corrections, final version

Differential Geometry.title: Dubrovin duality for open Hurwitz flat F-manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the Dubrovin dual of a Hurwitz Frobenius manifold extends naturally to an F-manifold with compatible flat connection on the universal curve, in the sense of the open WDVV equations. A similar result is proven for the Frobenius manifold itself in arXiv:2503.09258 . This equips the universal curve with two F-manifolds with compatible flat structure, and we study their duality. We show that they combine into a bi-flat F-manifold. Conditions on open WDVV solutions imposed in previous work are retrieved in this setting, thus providing them with a geometrical meaning. Finally, explicit examples are computed. For Saito Frobenius manifolds of types $A$ and $D$, the extended prepotentials coincide with open WDVV solutions computed independently, whereas even the existence of the solution in type $E$ had not been previously discussed. On the other hand, new non-homogeneous solutions are constructed by duality.
Differential Geometry.comment: Improved presentation and clarified relation to previous work; version accepted for publication in Comm. Math. Phys

Differential Geometry.title: Teichmüller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
Differential Geometry.summary:
We study Teichmüller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $θ= 2πβ$. For all $β>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $ω_β$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $β$, the form $ω_β$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit.
  For positive integers $β=n$, $ω_β$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $θ=2πn$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichmüller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

Differential Geometry.title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
Differential Geometry.summary: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.

Differential Geometry.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $ω\in Ω_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

Differential Geometry.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
Differential Geometry.summary: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.
Differential Geometry.comment: 43 pages. v2 substantially revised and extended. Source classes now use relative normal residues and supported Thom induction; the quadratic common-twist claim is corrected. Adds analytic K-theory and periodic cyclic computations (supported pairings reduce to rank and degree), filtered profiles, mixed-line criteria, an explicit Euler ASD connection and a foliation realization

Differential Geometry.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
Differential Geometry.summary: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $Λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12π/Λ$, for de Sitter, or at most $4π/Λ$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $π_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

Differential Geometry.title: Harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms and deformations of branched covers of special Lagrangians
Differential Geometry.summary: This article introduces the notion of a non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-form on a manifold $X$ in terms of immersed submanifolds of $T^*X$ and develops a deformation theory extending Donaldson's work on harmonic non-degenerate $\mathbf{Z}/2\mathbf{Z}$ $1$-forms. More precisely, the universal moduli space of harmonic non-degenerate multi-valued $1$-forms is shown to be a tame Fréchet orbifold whose projection onto the space of Riemannian metrics is a submersion and whose fibres are locally parametrised by their periods. The proof relies on Hörmander's subelliptic estimates and the Nash--Moser submersion theorem. As an application of this analytic framework, harmonic multi-valued $1$-forms on a special Lagrangian are shown to control deformations of its branched covers, extending work of He for multiplicity two.

Differential Geometry.title: Rotationally symmetric fractional minimal surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary: In this paper, we provide a non-trivial example of an $s$-minimal surface that is invariant under rotations. More precisely, we study alternating radial sets whose boundaries are finite or locally finite unions of concentric spheres and prove that, fixing the outer radius to $r=1$, there exists a radial configuration for which the fractional mean curvature $H_s$ vanishes at every free interface. We then show that rescaling radial maximizers by their innermost radius and passing to the limit yields a properly embedded, rotationally symmetric, locally finite hypersurface satisfying $H_s=0$ at every point of the boundary.

Differential Geometry.title: A question of Ulam and a theorem of de Rham
Differential Geometry.summary: We generalize de Rham's decomposition theorem to proper metric spaces: every proper metric space has a unique decomposition as the product of a Euclidean space and a finite or countable pointed $\ell^2$-product of nontrivial irreducible non-Euclidean factors. A slightly weaker unique decomposition statement is verified for general complete metric spaces. We use this to resolve a question of Ulam on the uniqueness of square roots of complete metric spaces.
Differential Geometry.comment: Added a resolution of Ulam's question for complete metric spaces

Differential Geometry.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

Differential Geometry.title: On the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator on higher-dimensional almost Kähler manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every smooth exact $J$-invariant two-form on a closed almost Kähler manifold admits a unique scalar potential, and that the associated generalized Monge-Ampère equation has at most one solution. In real dimension four, \textcolor{black}{we establish} local existence and uniqueness for nearby volume forms with the same total volume under the condition $h_J^-=b^+-1$. We also construct a nonintegrable almost Kähler four-torus and volume forms on it that cannot be realized by cohomologous $J$-compatible forms. These volume forms have the same total volume as the original volume form and can be chosen arbitrarily close to it. Finally, we relate the resulting trace potential to existing \textcolor{black}{a priori} estimates.

Differential Geometry.title: A Pogorelov-type estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampère equation
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a Pogorelov type interior $C^2$ estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampere equation without assuming uniform ellipticity. This equation is fully nonlinear and elliptic, but is neither concave nor a function of the eigenvalues of the Hessian, so the standard techniques for interior second-derivative estimates do not directly apply. Building on the partial Legendre transform formulation of Streets and Warren, we derive a differential identity for the associated positive-definite matrix $W(D^2u)$ and use some linear algebra to control the third-order terms arising in the maximum principle argument. As an application, we prove a Liouville theorem for entire split convex solutions with quadratic growth, extending the rigidity theorem of Streets and Warren by replacing their uniform ellipticity hypothesis with suitable quadratic growth assumptions.
Differential Geometry.comment: 27 pages. Revised title. Improved arguments to take place purely in direct coordinates

Differential Geometry.title: From n-systems to Lie and Courant algebroids
Differential Geometry.summary: This paper introduces a method for constructing pure algebroids, dull algebroids, and Lie algebroids. The construction relies on what we call $n$-systems on vector bundles, and we provide explicit formulas for all resulting structure maps. Analogously, metric $n$-systems defined on metric vector bundles allow us to construct metric algebroids, pre-Courant algebroids, and Courant algebroids.

Differential Geometry.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
Differential Geometry.summary: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn.
