The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4π$ with deficit $4πb^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\barσ_1^\star(b)=8π-16π\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

Differential Geometry.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
Differential Geometry.summary: We consider one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.

Differential Geometry.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
Differential Geometry.summary: We study strong positivity and Hodge--Riemann relations for real $(1,1)$-forms satisfying generalized $m$-positivity conditions. Every good prefix, defined via the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant, has a strictly strongly positive product and satisfies the Hodge--Riemann relations in all bidegrees. Allowing boundary factors, we prove that the hyperbolicity cone of every nonzero product of an almost-good prefix coincides with the polarizing component of its exterior-algebra quotient. As a special case, we obtain the full mixed Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary $m$-positive forms without assuming semipositivity. We also establish the Hodge--Riemann relations for weakly $(m,l)$-positive forms in all bidegrees $(p,q)$ with $p+q\le m$ and $\max\{p,q\}\ge l$. For $l=1$ and $m\ge2$, we deduce that the associated $(m-1)$-th power map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto the cone of strictly positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Adapting the $L^2$ method of Dinh and Nguyên, we pass from these pointwise results to the cohomology of compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we study numerical criteria, generalized complex Hessian equations, and sharp reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities in the sequential setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Non-Hermitian Yang--Mills Connections with Vanishing Chern Classes
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct non-flat non-Hermitian Yang--Mills connections with vanishing Chern classes whose induced and conjugate-dual holomorphic bundles are both stable, giving a negative answer to Kaledin and Verbitsky's flatness question even under these stability assumptions. We also give negative answers to their questions about the étaleness and bijectivity of the harmonic-class map. The examples are explicit connections on smoothly trivial rank-two bundles over projective Kähler surfaces and admit explicit positive harmonic metrics. For the family of fixed stable bundles studied here, the harmonic-class map is surjective. Every fibre contains exactly one flat point, but some fibres also contain positive-dimensional families of non-flat connections. The entire flat locus is a smooth component mapped biholomorphically onto the target. For a range of parameters, we determine the complete reduced analytic germ at a distinguished nonunitary flat point. It has two smooth branches of different dimensions whose intersection contains two-sided stable points arbitrarily close to that point. Finally, a single fibre of the pair of holomorphic projections contains infinitely many flat classes and an embedded copy of $\CC^*$ with exactly two flat members. Thus the two holomorphic isomorphism classes together do not determine flatness.

Differential Geometry.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
Differential Geometry.summary: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimesΛ_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenböck formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors of the spinor valued forms, and derive vanishing theorems, heat trace invariants and index formulas. Finally, in four dimensions we use these Weitzenböck formulas to construct non-negative functionals whose absolute minima define two generalizations of the Seiberg--Witten monopole equations to right spinor valued $p$-forms, one based on the Dirac operator and one on the twisted de Rham Laplacian, and discuss the resulting integrability conditions.

Differential Geometry.title: The Whitney sphere and tori as self-shrinkers
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the Whitney sphere in $\C^n$ is a self-shrinker for the Hamiltonian gradient flow of volume. We construct an explicit family of Lagrangian self-shrinking tori in $\C^2$ containing infinitely many pairwise noncongruent examples. We also characterize closed connected Lagrangian immersions whose Legendrian lifts lie in a Korányi sphere by showing that, up to scaling and a unitary transformation, they factor through the Whitney immersion via a diffeomorphism for $n\geq2$ and a finite covering for $n=1$.

Differential Geometry.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
Differential Geometry.summary: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

Differential Geometry.title: A singular Lawson cone minimizing the fractional perimeter in dimension seven
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that the nonlocal Lawson cone constructed by Davila, del Pino, and Wei (J. Differential Geom. 2018) in $N=7$ minimizes the fractional perimeter for all sufficiently small orders $s$. Thus nonlocal minimal surfaces can have singularities already in dimension $7$. This contrasts both with the classical theory, where the first singular example occurs in dimension $8$ (Bombieri-De Giorgi-Giusti, Invent. Math. 1969), and with the fractional theory for orders $s$ close to $1$ (Caffarelli-Valdinoci, Adv. Math. 2013).

Differential Geometry.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
Differential Geometry.summary:
We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$.
  As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$).
  As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for foliations of constant mean curvature embedded hypersurfaces near a stable minimal surface. The resulting foliation supplies nonlocal barriers thanks to known results of uniform convergence of the nonlocal mean curvature to the classical one when $s \to 1$.

Differential Geometry.title: Sharp Barycentric Costs in Teichmuller Space
Differential Geometry.summary: The affine Beltrami fiber over a closed hyperbolic surface has a quadratic normal response whose least vertical $L^2$ energy equals the tangent norm dual to the hyperbolic cotangent supremum norm. We prove this calibration using a curvature identity and exact localized responses. Its strictness determines the energy measures of near-minimizers and, under an amplitude constraint, gives a positive excess with an explicit quadratic lower coefficient when the supporting differential has nondegenerate maxima. Pointwise Poincar'e barycenters of representatives in one fiber give a nonlinear realization: equal-weight pairs attain prescribed small outputs exactly, and their creation energy approaches the calibrated norm if and only if the output scale is negligible relative to the squared amplitude bound. Restoring the full local fiber graph has leading cost four times the squared Weil--Petersson norm. For degenerating surfaces, we identify the additive limit of the calibrated norm across persistent components and collar directions. The induced length metric completes to marked augmented Teichm"uller space and has distance $\fracπ{2}\sum_i \ell_i + O((\sum_i \ell_i)^2)$ to a fixed pinching stratum. Systole-dependent estimates also yield exact nonlinear realizations along degenerating families.

Geometric Topology.title: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.

Geometric Topology.title: Multivariable Alexander polynomials of twisted torus links via Dehn surgery
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $T(p,q;r,s)$ be the twisted torus link obtained from the torus link $T(p,q)$ by adding $s$ full twists to $r$ adjacent strands, and let $C$ be an unknotted circle encircling those strands. For all $p$, $q$, and $r$ we compute the multivariable Alexander polynomial of $T(p,q)\cup C$ in closed form. A relation of Silver and Williams between the Alexander polynomials of a link and of its $1/n$ Dehn fillings then gives a closed formula for the multivariable Alexander polynomial of every twisted torus link $T(p,q;r,s)$, answering a question of Adnan and Park. When $\gcd(p,q)=1$, so that $T(p,q;r,s)$ is a knot, the formula is a sum of $pr$ monomials with coefficient $+1$, divided by cyclotomic factors, and its exponents are governed by an elementary counting function on the orbit of $q$ modulo $p$. Because the numerator has no cancellation, we are able to give the degree for all $s$ and simple non-fiberedness and non-L-space criteria for infinite families of twisted torus knots.
Geometric Topology.comment: version 2 removes exposition left from a previous draft. Section 6 is expanded to give infinite families of twisted torus knots which are not L-space knots

Geometric Topology.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
Geometric Topology.summary: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.
Geometric Topology.comment: 21 pages, final version. To appear in Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo, II. Ser

Geometric Topology.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
Geometric Topology.summary: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $ω\in Ω_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

Geometric Topology.title: The Gilmer-Masbaum map is not injective on the Kauffman bracket skein module
Geometric Topology.summary: Gilmer and Masbaum use Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev (WRT) invariants to define a map from the Kauffman bracket skein module to a set of complex-valued functions defined on roots of unity in order to provide a lower bound for its dimension. We compute the image of the evaluation map for a family of mapping tori of the 2-torus and find that the restriction of the map to certain homology classes is not injective. This provides an answer to a question posed by Gilmer and Masbaum in the latter paper. Moreover, we give a basis for the Kauffman bracket skein module in the case of the mapping torus of a power of the Dehn twist along the meridian of the 2-torus.

Geometric Topology.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
Geometric Topology.summary: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

Geometric Topology.title: Alexander modules and Milnor fibers of topological line arrangements
Geometric Topology.summary: We study the Alexander module and a distinguished cyclic cover, which we call the \textit{topological Milnor fiber}, of the complements of topological line arrangements. For every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines, where $n$ is not a prime power, we prove that the first Betti numbers of its topological Milnor fibers are unbounded. Moreover, any finite abelian group occurs as a direct summand of the integral homology of a topological Milnor fiber within the given combinatorial type. As an application, we show that every topologically realizable combinatorial type with $n \geq 2$ lines admits a realization whose complement has no $2$-dimensional CW model.

Geometric Topology.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

Geometric Topology.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
Geometric Topology.summary: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.

Geometric Topology.title: Spectral Summation and Critical Asymptotics of Newton Knot Invariants
Geometric Topology.summary: The symmetric colored invariants of a knot are defined at integer colors, and Newton interpolation assembles them into a formal function of a continuous color variable. We sum it by $q$-Borel--Laplace summation and use the resulting analytic function to study the invariants as $q\to1$. For every knot and every rank, the critical summation level is a rational number determined by the growth of the colored invariants; when it is positive, the critical Borel transform is meromorphic in the whole plane. When the Newton coefficients have analytic tails, the Borel transform is assembled from convergent sums of simple poles along geometric progressions, and for such sums the Stokes jump of the Laplace sum determines every pole and residue. For an infinite family of twist knots containing the figure-eight knot, a positive Markov kernel gives an exact formula for the remainder of the Newton series. With it we show that, near a root of the Alexander polynomial, the rescaled analytic interpolation converges to Gaussian and Scorer-type profiles, uniformly for complex values of the rescaled color, and we determine how fast the rank may grow before these limits change. Finally, continuation in $\log q$ produces a logarithmic monodromy whose coefficient is a convergent pairing of the same Borel residues that give the Stokes jump. For the figure-eight knot, the asymptotics of this coefficient are governed by the hyperbolic volume at every rank.

Geometric Topology.title: Fibered-knot braids and symplectic fake quadrics
Geometric Topology.summary: We construct aspherical symplectic four-manifolds with the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$ by summing ruled surfaces along braided multisections. For each $m\geq1$, we form two symplectic sums with the same gluing map in the chosen surface markings and normal framings, using a stabilized braid for the trefoil in one sum and for the torus knot $T(2,7)$ in the other. Both sums have integral first homology $({\mathbb Z}/2)^2\oplus{\mathbb Z}/(4m)$. Their fundamental groups admit respectively $36$ and $24$ epimorphisms onto $S_3$, so the sums are nonhomeomorphic. We also vary the gluing while keeping the multisections fixed. In each of five product, twisted, and hybrid cases, this gives an infinite sequence in which the first homology groups have strictly increasing finite orders. All but finitely many members of each sequence admit no complex structure.

Geometric Topology.title: Positivity of minimal volume entropy for some closed manifolds with zero simplicial volume
Geometric Topology.summary: For every integer $m\ge4$, we construct a closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold whose simplicial volume is zero and whose minimal volume entropy is positive. This answers negatively the question, attributed to Gromov, whether vanishing simplicial volume implies vanishing minimal volume entropy. Each example has a connected regular five-sheeted covering with zero minimal volume entropy, so vanishing of this invariant does not descend through finite coverings.

Geometric Topology.title: 10/8-inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary and its application
Geometric Topology.summary: As an application of 10/8 inequality for a spin 4-orbifold with boundary, we give criteria of homology 3-spheres represented by certain framed links for having infinite order in the homology cobordism group of homology 3-spheres. Such a class of homology 3-spheres includes certain plumbed 3-manifolds, 1/odd surgeries along certain knots with many twists, for example, certain Montesinos knots, $(p,q)$ cable knots of any knot with some large $p$, $q$, etc.

Geometric Topology.title: Homological Topological Quantum Field Theories
Geometric Topology.summary: We develop a new framework for quantum invariants of $3$-manifolds by extending to cobordisms a homological construction of mapping class group representations. More specifically, we construct a $(2+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theory (TQFT) that assigns to each surface the twisted homology of its unordered configuration space. The construction requires a choice of local systems on configuration spaces together with additional data. We formulate sufficient conditions on these data that guarantee the TQFT axioms, and we show that there are at least two useful examples satisfying them. One of them yields a homological construction of the projective Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, while the other recovers the Frohman--Nicas--Donaldson TQFT. In contrast to the classical algebraic constructions of quantum invariants, our approach is purely topological and relies on multi-trajectory spaces of cobordisms.
Geometric Topology.comment: 61 pages. Revised version. Corrected a coefficient hypothesis and revised Morse compatibility to use left and right locality. Clarified handle maps on small cycles, corrected the Schroedinger coefficient maps, and gave the degreewise normalization for the monoidal De Renzi--Martel comparison. The main conclusions are unchanged. The additional claim of a Hermitian TQFT has been withdrawn

Geometric Topology.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
Geometric Topology.summary: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f\to G$ and $Q_f\to G$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free. For a classical knot quandle, the canonical inner augmentation is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot. For every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$, the canonical inner augmentation is also free.

Geometric Topology.title: Combinatorial characterizations of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of positive alternating links and 3-braids
Geometric Topology.summary: The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link polynomial is a higher rank relative of the Jones polynomial which can be studied entirely diagrammatically using Kuperberg's web calculus. Building on the work of Harper and Kalfagianni, we construct formulae for the fourth and fifth coefficients of the quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ link invariant on positive alternating link diagrams in terms of data read from the associated Seifert graph. Then, we give a characterization of the invariant on positive alternating fibered links in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials. We also discuss behavior of our formulae under connected sums. We give formulations for the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ invariant of even powers of the Garside element $Δ_3\in B_3$ and a closed formula for the invariant on positive $3$-braids, resulting in a formula for the invariant on all $3$-braids.

Geometric Topology.title: A new class of affine $K(π,1)$ arrangements
Geometric Topology.summary: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(π,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(π,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.
Geometric Topology.comment: Updated following referee report, including many new figures and expanded exposition. To appear in Adv. Math

Geometric Topology.title: An elementary proof that linking problems are hard
Geometric Topology.summary: We give a new, elementary proof of what we believe is the simplest known example of a "natural" problem in computational 3-dimensional topology that is NP-hard---namely, the Trivial Sublink Problem: given a diagram $L$ of a link in $S^3$ and a positive integer $k$, decide if $L$ contains a $k$ component sublink that is trivial. This problem was previously shown to be NP-hard in independent works of Koenig-Tsvietkova and de Mesmay-Rieck-Sedgwick-Tancer, both of which used reductions from 3SAT. The reduction we describe instead starts with the Independent Set Problem, and allows us to avoid the use of Brunnian links such as the Borromean rings. On the technical level, this entails a new conceptual insight: the Trivial Sublink Problem is hard entirely due to mod 2 pairwise linking, with no need for integral or higher order linking. On the pedagogical level, the reduction we describe is entirely elementary, and thus suitable for introducing undergraduates and non-experts to complexity-theoretic low-dimensional topology. To drive this point home, in this work we assume no familiarity with low-dimensional topology, and---other than Reidemeister's Theorem and Karp's result that the Clique Problem is NP-hard---we provide more-or-less complete definitions and proofs. We have also constructed a web app that accompanies this work and allows a user to visualize the new reduction interactively.
Geometric Topology.comment: V2 has many more figures and expanded exposition. See URL on page 9 for accompanying web app. Many thanks to Martin Tancer and Yo'av Rieck. To appear in Involve - a journal of mathematics

Geometric Topology.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
Geometric Topology.summary: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.
Geometric Topology.comment: The mathematics in this article was developed by the authors without the use of AI

Optimization and Control.title: Repair-Based Duality for Distributionally Robust Optimization via Conditional-Moment Optimal Transport
Optimization and Control.summary: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) models often admit dual representations that replace optimization over probability distributions with more tractable formulations, but estab- lishing primal-dual equality can be challenging when ambiguity sets involve conditional moment restrictions, noncompact uncertainty spaces, or unbounded losses. We study these questions through the conditional-moment optimal transport (CM-OT) framework, which encompasses transport-, divergence-, and jointly perturbed DRO models. Our main contribution is a repair- based sufficient condition for primal-dual equality. The approach constructs feasible couplings from nearly feasible ones by mixing with suitable reference couplings, while a local conditional uniform integrability condition on positive-loss tails ensures that the resulting repairs do not incur a nonvanishing loss in objective value. This establishes the closedness of the associated perturbation value function without relying on compactness or conventional interiority condi- tions. We further distinguish primal-dual equality from the additional steps required to obtain pointwise dual representations, providing conditions under which essentially bounded measurable conditional-moment multipliers can be replaced, at the level of optimal values, by bounded continuous multipliers and under which optimization and integration can be interchanged. Finally, we apply the framework to a class of DRO models combining divergence-based ambiguity with distributional calibration, including contextual resource-allocation and reliability applications.

Optimization and Control.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
Optimization and Control.summary: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and often accelerates in practice. One of our main contributions is to disprove the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions. We develop a taxonomy of memory mechanisms by window length and forgetting rate. We consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. For this class, uniform acceleration requires either a window of length at least of order the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate at least of order the inverse square root. For one fixed-factor filter pair with a bounded window this forgetting scale is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions quadratic near the minimizer. A short window converges locally quadratically over blocks when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Constructive upper bounds reach this forgetting scale without problem constants. Geometric filter pairs created at fixed times give uniform acceleration with logarithmic memory, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor uses two vectors and attains an accelerated linear rate up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

Optimization and Control.title: Controlling discrete semilinear wave equations toward flocks
Optimization and Control.summary: We construct pointwise bounded controls that steer a finite, periodic, fully actuated active harmonic lattice with Rayleigh-Helmholtz velocity forcing to flock states in finite time. In our setting, an initial Lyapunov-feedback phase brings the velocities and elastic forces into a prescribed small neighborhood of zero. Then, subsequent trajectory planning and cancellation of the known drift achieve exact arrival at a moving flock. For prescribed stationary or moving profiles satisfying a strict control-admissibility condition, a two-stage interpolation reaches the target. We provide explicit sufficient time intervals for the stages following the initial feedback phase. Finally, we formulate the associated minimum-time problem and its formal Hamilton-Jacobi equation, leaving the continuity of the value function open.

Optimization and Control.title: An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
Optimization and Control.summary: In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.
Optimization and Control.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, Technical Report previously published at https://automatica.dei.unipd.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/consensus-based_localization_tech_note.pdf in 2013

Optimization and Control.title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
Optimization and Control.summary: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

Optimization and Control.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Unlike conventional matrix-preconditioned methods that use fixed decay parameters, NABLA adjusts the second-moment averaging coefficient through a closed-loop feedback rule determined by the cumulative stochastic-gradient energy and its running average. The first-moment coefficient remains fixed, allowing the trajectory-dependent adaptation to act directly on the structured preconditioners. The resulting method is horizon-free, requires no prior knowledge of the noise level, and automatically adjusts the memory of its second-moment estimators to the observed optimization dynamics. Under standard lower boundedness, smoothness, unbiasedness, bounded-variance, and spectral-boundedness assumptions, we establish uniform stability and variation bounds for the time-varying block preconditioners and control their interaction with momentum estimation and parameter updates. These results yield the noise-adaptive stationarity guarantee $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2}+σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4})$, which automatically reduces to the nearly deterministic $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ rate when the stochastic-gradient noise vanishes. NABLA therefore provides a principled approach to combining closed-loop trajectory feedback with memory-efficient structured matrix preconditioning.

Optimization and Control.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
Optimization and Control.summary: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

Optimization and Control.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels
Optimization and Control.summary: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. The BBN evaluates the probability and severity distribution of hazardous events, which are aggregated into a bounded scalar risk index. During the search, this risk index is evaluated at sample points along candidate edges. The planner optimizes a composite cost function comprising path distance, heading change penalties, and accumulated risk, subject to a hard constraint enforcing a risk acceptance limit. Each search tree vertex stores the BBN posterior at its state, enabling the tree to function as an explainable risk map for individual hazards. We define design requirements for the BBN to serve as the risk model in this context and introduce a runtime model that translates replanning deadlines into strict limits on single risk calculation times. The planner is demonstrated in a simulated harbor entry scenario involving collision and grounding hazards. Measured run times validate that the planner operates within the computational bounds predicted by the runtime model for a single replanning cycle.

Optimization and Control.title: Variance Reduction Note 5: The Convergence of Loopless SVRG
Optimization and Control.summary: A snapshot in loopless SVRG has no prescribed lifetime. At each step the algorithm may keep using an old full gradient or compute a new one. How does this choice enter the convergence proof, and how often is a new full gradient worth its cost? For a strongly convex finite sum we follow the age and objective gap of the snapshot. Its expected gap is a geometrically weighted average of earlier iterate gaps. This identity determines a weight for the snapshot in a one-step contraction argument and gives an objective bound for the last iterate. A two-component quadratic makes the estimator variance explicit, including on the step immediately after a refresh. We also evaluate the work bound as a function of the refresh probability and compare its minimizer with the condition-number-independent choice $p=1/n$.

Optimization and Control.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
Optimization and Control.summary: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

Optimization and Control.title: Pyoframe: A Python Library to Easily and Efficiently Construct Large Optimization Models
Optimization and Control.summary: Researchers and industry practitioners are constructing increasingly large optimization models to tackle problems in fields such as manufacturing, logistics, and energy systems planning. As the performance of solvers like Gurobi keeps improving, the performance of modeling frameworks like gurobipy which let users interact with solvers is increasingly becoming a bottleneck. We present Pyoframe, an open-source Python modeling framework to construct optimization models of various types (LPs, MIPs, QPs, and QCQPs). Pyoframe adopts a novel DataFrame-based software architecture that enables parallelized computations while also offering a legible syntax and a friendly user experience. We benchmark Pyoframe against other modeling frameworks (AMPL, CVXPY, Gurobipy, JuMP, Linopy, PuLP, Pyomo, and PyOptInterface) and find that Pyoframe is faster on every large or complex benchmark, while almost always using less memory and fewer lines of code. Switching to Pyoframe reduces the total time, memory, and code needed to solve these benchmark problems by up to 83%, 68%, and 64%, respectively, demonstrating the significant impact that modeling frameworks, not only solvers, can have in applied optimization. Overall, Pyoframe makes it easier and faster to develop and run large linear or quadratic optimization models.
Optimization and Control.comment: Under review at Mathematical Programming Computation

Optimization and Control.title: Bicriteria Traffic Assignment
Optimization and Control.summary: The classical traffic assignment problem determines the equilibrium flows on a congested network with many infinitesimal users who choose paths to minimize their own travel times. Travelers care about cost (including tolls) as well as time, and different travelers put different weights on these two criteria. We study a bicriteria traffic assignment problem in which travelers differ in their tradeoff between a flow-independent cost, such as tolls, and a flow-dependent cost, such as travel time. Existing formulations require either finitely many user classes or positive preference densities, including formulations for positive preference densities that are either infinite-dimensional or nonconvex. We formulate a finite-dimensional convex optimization problem for arbitrary preference distributions with bounded support, including distributions with a mixture of atoms, densities, and gaps in their support, and we show how to convert an optimal solution to an equilibrium of the bicriteria traffic assignment problem. We propose an algorithm that alternates between solving a convex problem for a (typically small) number of paths, and solving a parametric shortest-path problem. Computational experiments on benchmark networks illustrate the performance of the algorithm relative to existing methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Burn and density control in uncertain tokamak models with prescribed error bounds
Optimization and Control.summary: The stored energy and the electron density of a burning tokamak plasma must be kept inside prescribed bands, with the auxiliary heating power and the fuelling rate as actuators. For the standard zero-dimensional burn model with a dynamic confinement closure we show that this two-actuator configuration has vector relative degree $(2,1)$, independently of the confinement parameters. We design a model-free funnel controller which uses an input filter instead of output derivatives and meets all actuator constraints - sign, amplitude and rate - by construction, the input deficit being returned to the loop as a correction of the reference. For a system class containing the model we prove, under the compatibility assumption that the corrections stay bounded by constants fixed in advance, that the tracking errors evolve in prescribed funnels about the corrected references. Sufficient conditions for the assumption are given, and the design is illustrated on an ITER benchmark.

Optimization and Control.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, defines the sampling subspace of a guided evolution strategy rather than being used as a direct update. For any guiding subspace, the expected update is a descent direction of the smoothed objective, so an inaccurate guide adds variance while the expected step still descends. For six problem families, both guided estimators outperform the baseline. The decision-focused version reduces the mean gap by three-quarters, and on the two families with the most integer variables the reduced sets beat the exact solver's two-hour incumbent in most runs, using a fifth of the time.

Optimization and Control.title: Deterministic Oracle Complexity for Goldstein Stationarity in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization with Constraints
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the deterministic oracle complexity of finding a $(δ,ε)$-Goldstein stationary point of a Lipschitz function under constraints. Our main result concerns products of convex bodies. Each block contains an inner ball and lies in a concentric outer ball. The inner radii have a common positive lower bound, and each outer radius is at most a fixed multiple of the corresponding inner radius. This class includes common constraints such as balls and boxes. On each prescribed feasible set of dimension $d$ in this class, every deterministic algorithm using a local oracle needs $\exp(Ω(d))$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case at fixed, sufficiently small accuracies $δ$ and $ε$. The objective Lipschitz and initial objective-value gap bounds are fixed, and each constructed function has a global minimizer in the interior of the feasible set. For broader classes of constraints, supplementary results show that every deterministic algorithm needs $Ω(ε^{-2})$ objective-oracle calls in the worst case when $d\gtrsimε^{-2}$ and $δ\lesssimε$. The constants depend on the interior-ball radius and, for inequalities, the local Lipschitz and Slater bounds. These supplementary results cover closed sets that are star-shaped with respect to a ball and convex coercive inequalities with a Slater point, and hold even for convex objectives.
Optimization and Control.comment: 33 pages, no figures. Reformatted for journal submission; author information, funding, declarations and reference formatting updated. Mathematical results unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Aerodynamic Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres in Very Low Earth Orbit: Exploiting Lift for Short Warning Times and Reduced Orbital Decay
Optimization and Control.summary: Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO, below $450\,\mathrm{km}$ altitude) offer promising mission capabilities for future spacecraft, but increasing traffic and the presence of orbital debris create collision risks that pose a particular challenge for satellites without conventional propulsion. Aerodynamic drag, resulting from interaction with the residual atmosphere, has been shown effective for performing collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs). However, short warning times remain challenging, and current methods do not exploit aerodynamic lift forces that enable out-of-track manoeuvres, which could help enhance control authority and mitigate drag-induced orbital decay. This work addresses both gaps by developing and evaluating two complementary optimisation methods: a heuristic approach using reachable set analysis to determine minimum lead times, and a direct shooting method to limit the increase in orbital decay due to the manoeuvre. Analyses using data derived from real conjunctions show that achieving a sufficient reduction in collision risk in the considered scenarios is feasible with lead times lower than one orbital period. Results also show that lift-based manoeuvres outperform drag-only approaches, with modest lead time reductions and more pronounced benefits in limiting orbital decay. Performance sensitivity to variations in control authority due to the type of gas-surface-interaction, altitude, and the encounter geometry is characterised. The methods and results presented highlight the potential of aerodynamic CAM for short warning time scenarios, contributing to sustainable operations in the increasingly congested VLEO environment.
Optimization and Control.comment: 23 pages, 22 figures, 1 table, submitted to Acta Astronautica

Optimization and Control.title: On Observability Decomposition of Boolean Control Networks
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We characterize when a BN admits an observability decomposition in terms of the equivalence classes induced by indistinguishability. We prove that a decomposition exists if and only if all such equivalence classes have the same cardinality, and we explicitly construct the coordinate transformation together with the matrices of the observable and unobservable subsystems. The observable subsystem is shown to be the quotient graph obtained by contracting each class into a single vertex. For BNs whose equivalence classes have unequal cardinalities, we propose an extended observability decomposition by adding virtual states, and show that every finite BN admits an observability decomposition in an extended sense. These results are further generalized to BCNs, for which an algorithm and an illustrative example are provided.

Optimization and Control.title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
Optimization and Control.summary: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of topology and latent states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian: a flexible generative transition can absorb graph-induced changes of the conditional mean, whereas a Gaussian transition discards the information in the residual shape. We develop a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, and a frozen diffusion emulator represents the conditionally centered residual. First, a score--topology duality expresses edge-wise likelihood gradients as edge projections of the residual diffusion score, so topology learning requires neither transition densities nor differentiation through the sampler. Second, we prove identifiability from intermittent observations, invariance of the population minimizer across noise levels, and global strong convexity above an explicit smoothing threshold for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. With known support and oracle state pairs, the asymptotic covariance approaches the Cramér--Rao bound as smoothing vanishes and is strictly smaller than that of any Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimator under an explicit non-Gaussianity condition; for unknown sparse support we characterize the boundary limit, and we quantify the topology bias caused by residual-score mismatch. Third, we couple score-driven graph updates with an approximately fully adapted generative particle filter and prove, for bounded residuals under explicit excitation and forgetting conditions, a mean-square closed-loop bound with a step-size-independent small-gain condition. Synthetic and real-data experiments confirm these gains under non-Gaussian forcing.

Optimization and Control.title: Exact Last-Iterate Bounds and Optimal Stepsizes for Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent
Optimization and Control.summary: Proximal Stochastic Gradient Descent minimizes the sum of an $L$-smooth convex function $f$, known through unbiased stochastic gradients of bounded variance, and a nonsmooth convex function $R$, known through its proximity operator. We derive the exact worst-case value of the expected objective gap of its last iterate, for every predetermined stepsize schedule in a broad class, which contains all the schedules with stepsizes at most $3/(2L)$. This extends to the composite setting a recent result of Grimmer and Shen for the smooth case $R=0$. The value is the sum of an initial-error term and of one term per iteration, which is the price of the noise injected at this iteration, damped by the stepsizes that remain after it. The upper bound is proved with a simple potential, the Moreau envelope of the objective with a smoothing parameter proportional to the remaining stepsize sum, and it is attained by an explicit instance. The formula shows that a logarithmic factor is unavoidable with a constant stepsize, and it gives the exact price of the proximity operator, relative to the smooth case. It also makes the choice of the stepsizes a tractable optimization problem: for a uniform variance bound $σ^2$, the best schedule is unique, decreasing, and computed by a scalar search, and it is minimax optimal among all predetermined schedules, unless the noise level is low. Asymptotically, the minimax value $M_T$ after $T$ iterations satisfies $(Dσ/M_T)^2=T+\log T+C_\star+o(1)$, where $D$ is a bound on the initial distance to a solution and $C_\star\approx1.768$ is a universal constant; unlike in the smooth case, $L$ plays no role at this order. This law is achieved by an explicit schedule, which is the optimal one when $f=0$.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust stochastic first order methods in heavy-tailed noise via medoid mini-batch gradient sampling
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider a first order stochastic optimization framework where, at each iteration, $K$ independent identically distributed (i.i.d.) data point samples are drawn, based on which stochastic gradients can be queried. We allow gradient noise to be heavy-tailed, with possibly infinite variances. For the considered heavy-tailed setting, many algorithmic variants have recently been proposed based on gradient clipping or other nonlinear operators (e.g., normalization) applied over noisy gradients. In this paper, we take an alternative approach and propose a novel gradient estimator. The core idea of proposed estimator is to split the $K$-sized data batch into $M$ distinct data chunks, form for each chunk the stochastic gradient, and select the stochastic gradient of the chunk that is medoid of gradients of all data-chunks. For a broad class of symmetric heavy-tailed gradient noise distributions, we show that the proposed estimator has a finite second moment even when the underlying gradient noise has an infinite second moment. For nonconvex objectives, this yields convergence to a neighborhood of zero in expected squared gradient norm at a rate of $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$. We explicitly characterize the size of this neighborhood in terms of the noise and algorithm parameters. When the time horizon $T$ is known in advance, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence rate. A diminishing step size achieves the same rate up to a logarithmic factor. Incorporating clipping or a more general nonlinear transformation yields high-probability convergence guarantees with the same rate up to logarithmic factors. Experimental results indicate that R-SGD-Mini and its clipped or nonlinear variant consistently perform favorably compared to SGD, clipped SGD, Nonlinear SGD and Median-of-Means based methods.

Optimization and Control.title: Safety stock calculation with heteroscedastic, autocorrelated and heavy-tailed forecast errors, an adaptive parametric method.e
Optimization and Control.summary: This study develops and validates an adaptive parametric method for sizing safety stock when forecast errors are autocorrelated, heteroscedastic, asymmetric, and heavy-tailed. Using four years of weekly forecasts from a fast-moving consumer goods company, the analysis identifies substantial positive autocorrelation, departures from normality, systematic forecast optimism, and heterogeneous relationships between forecast volume and error variance. The proposed method integrates several corrections into a modular, sequential safety-stock architecture. It constructs cumulative forecast errors over the operational action period, selects an SKU-specific parametric distribution, and determines a baseline protection point using an expected-shortage condition consistent with the target beta fill rate. A forecast-scaled module adjusts dispersion when error variance depends on forecast volume, while a Cycle-End Exposure safeguard limits within-cycle shortage risk when large replenishment lots increase exposure. Performance is evaluated through discrete-event simulation against the company's current method. The proposed method reduces average inventory by 9.9% and maximum inventory by 19.5%, with no statistically significant deterioration in beta fill rate or average stockout duration. The proportion of weeks without stockouts declines slightly, without evidence of more persistent or operationally severe shortages. The heteroscedasticity module provides selective benefits, with greater service improvements as variance dependence intensifies. The resulting framework is interpretable, adapts to SKU-specific statistical profiles, links distributional features to safety-stock outcomes, and can be integrated into existing ERP environments.

Optimization and Control.title: Explicit KL Exponents for PLQ Functions on the Sphere
Optimization and Control.summary: Let $φ$ be a proper piecewise linear-quadratic (PLQ) function whose domain meets the unit sphere $\mathcal{S}$. We prove that $f:=φ+δ_{\mathcal{S}}$, where $δ_{\mathcal{S}}$ is the indicator function of $\mathcal{S}$, satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property with exponent $3/4$ throughout its domain. This exponent is sharp even for the convex PLQ class. We characterize the smallest KL exponents of quadratics restricted to affine sections of $\mathcal{S}$, obtaining the values $0$, $1/2$, $2/3$, and $3/4$. A tangential projection identity shows that, at each point of ${\rm dom}\,f$, the maximum of the exponents from the relevant affine sections is admissible for $f$. When $φ$ is piecewise affine (PA), each of these smallest exponents is $0$ or $1/2$. Thus $f$ satisfies the KL property with exponent $1/2$ throughout ${\rm dom}\,f$, and this exponent is sharp over the class of sphere-constrained PA functions. When ${\rm dom}\,φ$ is a finite union of closed polyhedral cones, $f$ admits KL exponent $1/2$ for homogeneous quadratic pieces and exponent $0$ for nonnegative $φ$ that is linear on each cone. For any convex polytope $C$ containing the origin, we use the KL exponent $0$ to show that the full-step manifold proximal point iterates for minimizing the support function of $C$ over $\mathcal{S}$ stabilize at a critical point in finitely many steps.

Optimization and Control.title: Soft projections for robust data-driven control
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider data-based predictive control based on behavioral systems theory. In the linear setting this means that a system is described as a subspace of trajectories, and predictive control can be formulated using a projection onto the intersection of this behavior and a constraint set. Instead of learning the model, or subspace, we focus on determining this projection from data. Motivated by the use of regularization in data-enabled predictive control (DeePC), we introduce the use of soft projections, which approximate the true projector onto the behavior from noisy data. In the simplest case, these are equivalent to known regularized DeePC schemes, but they exhibit a number of benefits. First, we provide a bound on the approximation error consisting of a bias and a variance term that can be traded-off by the regularization weight. The derived bound is independent of the true system order, highlighting the benefit of soft projections compared to low-dimensional subspace estimates. Moreover, soft projections allow for intuitive generalizations, one of which we show has superior performance on a case study. Finally, we provide update formulas for soft projectors enabling the efficient adaptation of the proposed data-driven control methods in the case of streaming data.

Optimization and Control.title: Fractional minimality of the Simons cone for $s$ close to $1$
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove that the Simons cone in $\mathbb R^8$ minimizes the fractional perimeter $P_s$, under compact perturbations, whenever $s$ is sufficiently close to $1$.

Optimization and Control.title: Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models
Optimization and Control.summary: Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Started close enough to a local minimum with a nondegenerate Hessian and with a small enough step size, the ($μ$/$μ$w, $λ$)-ES with stepsize adaptation converges linearly to this minimum with high probability, at the rate of its quadratic model, and the probability of failure vanishes when the initial step size and the initial distance to the minimum tend to zero. The proof views the normalized process as an adaptive chain and couples it, with high probability, with the Markov chain associated with the quadratic model.

Optimization and Control.title: On Approximate Computation of Critical Points
Optimization and Control.summary: We show that computing even coarse approximations of critical points is intractable for simple classes of nonconvex functions. We first present a family of $n$-variate cubic polynomials with coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ that have exact critical points but for which no polynomial-time algorithm can write down a $\sqrt{n}/4$-approximate critical point in its standard representation. We then show that computational hardness persists when an exact critical point has a short representation. More specifically, we prove that for every fixed $η>0$, unless P $=$ NP, no polynomial-time (or even pseudo-polynomial-time) algorithm can take an $n$-variate cubic polynomial with rational coefficients ${c_α}$ and return a point with gradient norm at most $(\max_α|c_α|)n^{1/2-η}$ whenever the polynomial has a critical point in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$. The algorithm may return an arbitrary point on all other inputs. Both results are essentially tight in their dependence on the dimension $n$. We also prove hardness results for lower-bounded functions and for an alternative notion of approximation, in which approximation is measured by distance to an exact critical point. Overall, our results stand in contrast to the commonly held belief that, in nonconvex optimization, approximate computation of critical points is a tractable task.

Optimization and Control.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
Optimization and Control.summary:
For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[
  \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\fracπ{n}\,A
  +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2,
  \qquad
  c_n=1-\frac{\tan(π/n)}{\tan(π/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

Optimization and Control.title: On Semilocal Convergence of a Semismooth* Newton Method
Optimization and Control.summary:
We give conditions under which the semismooth$^*$ Newton method solves $0\in F(x)$ from a given initial point. At each step, we bound the distance from the corrected point $(x_{k+1},0)$ to the graph of $F$ by a function of the correction length. We also bound $\|A^{-1}B\|$ uniformly over the selected coderivative pairs $(A,B)$. Together, these bounds give a test on the initial graph residual and the radius of a prescribed ball. If the test holds, the iterates converge to a solution in that ball. If the decrease modulus tends to zero, every infinite run converges $q$-superlinearly.
  For mixed complementarity problems on a box, we assume that the smooth part has a Lipschitz continuous Jacobian and that every nonempty principal submatrix is nonsingular. We bound the error after one step for each regular pair. The bound is quadratic in the distance to a solution and depends explicitly on the norm of the correction matrix. For affine problems, we give a threshold on the norm of the vertical component of a graph point. Below this threshold, all regular pairs at that point give the same solution in one step, even when their rows come from different branches. Hence any run with vanishing graph residuals terminates in finitely many steps. For integer affine data, we give a test for an exact step using only the problem data and the current iterate.

Optimization and Control.title: Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes
Optimization and Control.summary: The long-step Barzilai-Borwein (BB1) method, cyclic BB1, and limited memory steepest descent (LMSD) are special cases of limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR), a family of methods using historical Ritz step sizes. We analyze a cyclic Ritz-step rule within LMSDR and a sampled LMSDR variant on strictly convex quadratics, seeking R-superlinear convergence guarantees in higher spectral dimensions. Let $n$ be the problem dimension and $m$ the history length. In exact arithmetic, we begin at $n=m+1$, the first dimension beyond the finite-termination case, and obtain an exact doubly exponential rate per gradient update for rolling reuse outside an explicit, possibly empty exceptional set. We extend this rate to nonempty open sets for $m+1<n\le2m$ when each Ritz step is reused $\ell\ge4$ times. To go beyond this range, we rebuild the history with $m$ sampling updates at each cycle. With positive sampling steps $τ$ chosen in advance and factors $1-τλ_i$ uniformly bounded in modulus and away from zero, this gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{n-1}{m}$. For any $n>m$, increasing $\ell$ eventually satisfies this condition. Geometrically spaced choices among finitely many sampling lists preserve the guarantee.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust decision-dependent information discovery is harder than robust optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we consider a four-stage variant of robust optimization with cost uncertainty described by the budget uncertainty polytope, known as decision-dependent information discovery (DDID). In this problem, the decision maker first queries a subset of the cost coefficients. Then, the adversary responds by revealing worst-case values for the queried elements, after which the decision maker chooses a feasible solution while facing the remaining uncertainty on the unqueried costs. Our contribution is twofold. On the negative side, we prove that, the DDID is NP-complete even when the underlying nominal problem is the 2-selection problem, for which only a polynomial number of feasible solutions exist. This contrasts with the min-max robust counterpart with budget uncertainty, known to be not harder than the nominal problem. On the positive side, we prove that the more general $p$-selection problem can be solved in polynomial time under the additional assumption that all deviations are equal.

Optimization and Control.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. We propose KKT Atlas, which partitions contexts into local charts and identifies a low-dimensional subspace per chart from decision gradients of the scenario cost. It generates shared scenarios by jointly fitting subspace coordinates and context-dependent probabilities. We show that one more scenario than the subspace dimension suffices to approximate the conditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality condition under regularity conditions, yielding decision and risk bounds under local strong convexity, with generalization error scaling with the compact parameter dimension. On three synthetic problems, Atlas uses 4-18 scenarios per decision versus 500 for direct-solve full-support integrated learning. It attains comparable or lower risk with about $4$-$23\times$ construction and $13$-$61\times$ batch deployment speedups. Atlas also achieves lower risk than clustering-based reduction at matched support budgets. In real-world European grid reserve commitment, Atlas compresses 728 scenarios to 8-9, cutting construction and deployment times by factors of about 4 and 3 relative to full-support integrated learning. Its loss is lowest over 11 quarters and, over 17 later quarters with fixed settings, slightly higher than with full-support integrated learning and significantly lower than with the remaining benchmarks.

Optimization and Control.title: Learning Linear Time-Varying Koopman Models for Constrained Nonlinear Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper presents a learning-based Koopman framework for solving constrained nonlinear optimal control problems. Despite significant advances in Koopman-based modeling and control, challenges remain in achieving accurate representations of controlled nonlinear dynamics and constraints while maintaining computational efficiency for optimal control. Motivated by these challenges, a linear time-varying (LTV) Koopman representation is developed to provide a more expressive representation of controlled nonlinear dynamics while preserving a linear prediction structure suitable for efficient convex optimization. Modeling errors and their propagation over extended prediction horizons are analyzed, motivating a neural-network-based Koopman framework that jointly learns lifted dynamics and constraint representations with stability-oriented regularization to improve long-horizon prediction performance. Based on the learned Koopman model, the original constrained nonlinear optimal control problem is reformulated as a convex quadratic program with conservative constraint tightening to account for modeling uncertainty during constraint enforcement. Numerical results on a low-thrust orbit transfer problem and a Mars entry guidance problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and constrained optimal control performance.

Optimization and Control.title: Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness
Optimization and Control.summary: Under classical assumptions, performance of first-order methods has been studied quite comprehensively with the developed theoretical apparatus of modern optimization. The development of the Performance Estimation Problems (PEP) framework led to even deeper understanding and allowed computer-assisted derivation of exact worst-case guarantees. Unfortunately, PEP is not directly applicable for systems that involve SDP-incompatible constraints. This includes a wide range of non-standard assumptions, some of them are highly relevant for practice such as generalized smoothness. In this paper proposes an approach of utilizing template solutions to derive guarantees in settings that do not admit an equivalent SDP formulation of exact worst-case performance problem. The approach is showcased by studying the performance of the gradient descent method for convex functions that also satisfy $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness assumption. Despite the inherent conservatism of the approach, this paper improves and generalizes an existing convergence guarantee to showcase the approach.
Optimization and Control.comment: This is the extended version of the paper Krivchenko, V. O. (2026). Computer-Aided Analysis of Gradient Descent under Generalized Smoothness. Doklady Mathematics, 530(1), 5-13. The extended version is much more detailed. It contains expanded discussion of the approach as well as descriptions of PEP experiments

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Weighted Volume Dissipativity and Sobolev Regularity at Limiting Rate
Optimization and Control.summary: Sharp pointwise divergence bounds for a nonlinear flow are studied under the requirement that the logarithm of the adapted positive density also be an exponentially decaying Lyapunov function. Invariant-measure duality supplies the unrestricted benchmark. Under two-sided quadratic Lyapunov bounds, scaling a prescribed Lyapunov function realizes every strictly suboptimal pointwise rate without reducing its decay rate, and the closure of the joint rate region is a rectangle. For a fixed reference volume form, the limiting pointwise rate has a smooth compatible certificate exactly when the differential of the reference divergence vanishes at the equilibrium. Otherwise, the infimal second-derivative supremum norm grows inversely with the gap to the limiting rate. Matching Sobolev cost bounds are proved in every finite dimension when the integrability exponent exceeds the dimension and the prescribed Lyapunov rate does not exceed half the baseline rate. The upper construction uses a regularized square root of the baseline Lyapunov function and keeps the potential and its gradient uniformly bounded. Matching contraction deficits under a Sobolev norm budget follow. A scalar borderline family has bounded second-derivative mass and a Lipschitz limit with atomic second derivative. The limiting exponent also holds in the reference measure with an explicit uniform volume prefactor, even when no smooth compatible instantaneous certificate exists. Scaling preserves the full baseline Lyapunov rate.

Optimization and Control.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

Optimization and Control.title: Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
Optimization and Control.summary: Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching.
