To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.
Optimization and Control.comment: 49 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables, including a 16-page e-companion

Optimization and Control.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
Optimization and Control.summary: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4π$ with deficit $4πb^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\barσ_1^\star(b)=8π-16π\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

Optimization and Control.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

Optimization and Control.title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of $\mathcal{O}(m)$ updates with a total stepsize of order $m^2/L$. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice $m\asymp(L^2/(ρ\varepsilon))^{1/4}$ for small $\varepsilon$. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.

Optimization and Control.title: Turnpike Estimates and Limiting Behavior for $N$-Player Differential Games under Displacement Monotonicity
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the long-time behavior of open-loop Nash equilibria of $N$-player stochastic differential games with nondegenerate idiosyncratic noise, under displacement monotonicity of the costs and joint strong convexity of the Lagrangians. We prove an exponential turnpike estimate: as the remaining horizon grows, the decoupling fields of the finite-horizon Pontryagin systems converge exponentially fast to the solution of a stationary Pontryagin system, which is unique in a natural stability class, and on bounded time intervals the equilibrium states and controls converge to those generated by this solution. The limiting control is a strong open-loop equilibrium of an associated ergodic $N$-player game, and the ergodic constant $λ^{i,N}$ of each player is the same at every such equilibrium. For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

Optimization and Control.title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret under Heavy-Tailed Noise
Optimization and Control.summary: We study online convex optimization on a compact convex domain of diameter $D$ in which the learner observes, at each round, one stochastic subgradient and no loss values. The observations are conditionally unbiased, and the noise has an unconditional $p$-th moment at most $σ^p$ for an unknown $p\in(1,2]$; for $p<2$ its variance may be infinite. For a comparator sequence of path length $P_T$ we write $Λ_T=1+P_T/D$, and we show that the minimax expected dynamic regret is, up to numerical constants, \[ \min\Bigl\{GD\sqrt{TΛ_T}+σDT^{1/p}Λ_T^{(p-1)/p},\ GDT\Bigr\}, \] where $G$ bounds the subgradients. The lower bound holds on every compact convex domain of positive diameter. An algorithm that combines AdaGrad learners restarted at different frequencies through exponential weights with a data-dependent learning rate attains this rate for each fixed $p>1$, without knowing $G$, $σ$, $p$, or $P_T$: the constant of the first term is numerical, the constant of the second is $O(1+\log(p/(p-1)))$, and no logarithmic factor of $T$ appears. The analysis bounds the gradient energy separately on each restart block, which gives the exponent $(p-1)/p$ of $Λ_T$ in the noise term; a bound over the whole horizon gives the exponent $1/2$. Running the algorithm on epochs of doubling length removes the need to know $T$ at the cost of a factor $2+\sqrt2$. The appendices give a high-probability version and a synthetic study.

Optimization and Control.title: Constrained Online Learning with Noisy Constraint Values
Optimization and Control.summary: We study online convex optimization with time-varying constraints when the constraint values are observed only through noise. In each round the learner picks an action, pays a convex loss, and incurs a convex constraint value that should be nonpositive; it then receives unbiased estimates of the loss and constraint gradients, and an unbiased observation of the constraint value whose error has bounded variance. Performance is measured against the best fixed action in hindsight among those that satisfy every constraint, and violation by the largest total overspend over any interval of consecutive rounds, which we call budget violation. Our algorithm, LEDGER, has $O(\sqrt T)$ expected regret and $O(\sqrt{T\log T})$ expected budget violation over $T$ rounds, uses one projection per round, and needs no strictly feasible action. The logarithm cannot be removed: with Gaussian noise of fixed positive variance, every algorithm with $O(\sqrt T)$ worst-case regret has worst-case budget violation of order at least $\sqrt{T\log T}$, even if only the final total overspend is counted, and budget violation $O(\sqrt T)$ forces linear regret. When violation is instead the sum of the positive parts of the per-round constraint values (hard violation), no algorithm keeps both expected regret and expected hard violation sublinear if the noise distribution is not fixed, even for affine constraints. With a fixed and known Gaussian noise law of standard deviation $σ$, a worst-case lower bound of order $\min\{σ,1\}T(\log\log T/\log T)^2$ shows that regret and hard violation cannot both be made polynomially sublinear. Noisy constraint values therefore still allow a signed budget to be controlled, at the cost of a logarithmic factor, but not the hard violation.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal control of SDEs with merely measurable drift: an HJB approach
Optimization and Control.summary:
We investigate an optimal control problem for a diffusion whose drift and running cost are merely measurable in the state variable. Such low regularity rules out the use of Pontryagin's maximum principle and also invalidates the standard proof of the Bellman principle of optimality. We address these difficulties by analyzing the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Working in a weak formulation of admissible controls, we first establish the state-equation solvability and Krylov estimates needed to make the control problem well defined. Using PDE techniques together with a policy iteration scheme, we prove that the HJB equation admits a unique strong solution, and this solution coincides with the value function of the control problem. Based on this identification, we establish a verification theorem and recover the Bellman optimality principle without imposing any additional smoothness assumptions.
  We further investigate a mollification scheme depending on a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. It turns out that the smoothed value functions $V_{\varepsilon}$ may fail to converge to the original value function $V$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and we provide an explicit counterexample. To resolve this, we identify a structural condition on the control set. When the control set is countable, convergence $V_{\varepsilon} \to V$ holds locally uniformly.

Optimization and Control.title: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
Optimization and Control.summary:
The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data.
  Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

Optimization and Control.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of cones definable in o-minimal structures
Optimization and Control.summary: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined by a complementarity problem over a closed convex cone. We show that every closed convex cone that is definable in an o-minimal structure is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra of symmetric matrices relative to the cone (the sets of their cone-constrained eigenvalues) have uniformly bounded cardinality. In particular, we derive explicit uniform bounds for semialgebraic cones, and the explicit uniform bound we obtain for a Löwner cone depends only on the order of the matrices in the cone. Using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show that the number of singular values relative to two closed convex cones definable in a common o-minimal structure is uniformly bounded. Finally, we provide a closed convex cone that is not definable in any o-minimal structure and for which the spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but have no uniform cardinality bound.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

Optimization and Control.title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a Lévy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

Optimization and Control.title: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
Optimization and Control.summary: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, stable log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out consecutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

Optimization and Control.title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.

Optimization and Control.title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
Optimization and Control.summary: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

Optimization and Control.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Estimation with Convex Models
Optimization and Control.summary: A linear functional of an object from a convex symmetric set can be optimally estimated, in a worst-case sense, by a linear functional of observations made on the object. This well-known fact is extended here to a nonlinear setting: other simple functionals of the object can be optimally estimated by functionals of the observations that share a similar simple structure. This is established for the maximum of several linear functionals and even for the $\ell$th largest among them. Proving the latter requires an unusual variation of the analytical Hahn--Banach theorem. The existence results are accompanied by practical recipes relying on convex optimization to construct the desired functionals, thereby justifying the term of estimation algorithms.

Optimization and Control.title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
Optimization and Control.summary: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

Optimization and Control.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
Optimization and Control.summary: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.

Optimization and Control.title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
Optimization and Control.summary: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Saúde (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

Optimization and Control.title: Splitting Compositions of Monotone Operators
Optimization and Control.summary:
Coupled convex optimisation equilibria and nonlinear circuits lead to inclusions of the form $0 \in Hx + A(Bx) - b$, where $A$ and $B$ are maximally monotone but the complete operator need not be monotone. We develop a one-parameter family of triangular warped-resolvent algorithms on product Hilbert spaces to solve such inclusions. Introducing $y \in Bx$ exposes a directed lift, and a composition-adapted kernel organizes each iteration into one evaluation of $H$ and one ordinary resolvent evaluation per factor block.
  A nonnegative multi-block gain matrix certifies a unique lifted solution, global linear convergence, and residual error bounds. An exact Schur reduction converts the $2n \times 2n$ condition into an equivalent $n \times n$ criterion. For nonpositive extrapolation, this criterion is necessary and sufficient to guarantee a unique fixed point and global linear convergence for all problems satisfying the given gain bounds. Minimum-gain estimates characterize its exact finite-stepsize feasibility boundary. A negative-coupling rotation family exhibits certified convergence when neither the original operator nor its specified lift admits a fixed positive-definite monotonicity metric. For a nonlinear periodic RLC circuit, we establish continuous-time nonmonotonicity and derive a computable convergence certificate. Our algorithm is demonstrated on a periodic circuit simulation problem.
Optimization and Control.comment: 23 pages, 4 figures. Revised manuscript with new multiport convergence results, a minimum-gain analysis of stepsize feasibility, and a nonlinear RLC circuit application

Optimization and Control.title: Controllability of the Cahn Hilliard System at Finitely Many Observation Points
Optimization and Control.summary: We study approximate controllability of the Cahn-Hilliard (CH) system with prescribed targets at finitely many points in the spatial domain. Our aim is to design a L^2 control such that given a finite set of observation points and target values, the solution reaches arbitrarily close to the prescribed targets at these points. First we study the associated linearised system using variational methods and then extend the results to the semi-linear CH system using fixed-point arguments. Further, we investigate approximate controllability in more general setting where we allow the control to be measure valued (in specific, Dirac delta type controls). This formulation is more challenging to obtain requisite regularity due to the simultaneous presence of pointwise observations and pointwise controls. Hence we restrict ourselves to the study of linearised CH system and devise a control which exhibits approximate controllability. We achieve this by approximating measure valued control with L^2 controls and showing appropriate convergence.

Optimization and Control.title: Stochastic Optimization for Switch-System Identification under Errors-in-Variables
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we address the identification of switched dynamical systems under errors-in-variables, where both input and output measurements are corrupted by noise, and the number of operating modes and subsystem orders are unknown. We propose a unified identification framework that simultaneously estimates the subsystem parameters, latent switching sequence, and model structure. The proposed formulation combines a variance-normalized data-fitting criterion with temporally regularized soft mode assignments and sparsity-inducing penalties for selecting the active modes and relevant input-output lags. To solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we develop an alternating algorithm that incorporates convex mode-assignment updates and proximal stochastic variance-reduced gradient optimization for parameter estimation. While the existing approaches in the literature require exhaustive searches over candidate structures, the proposed method performs structure selection within a single model. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate recovery of the underlying system structure and favorable computational efficiency compared with a generalized total least squares and dynamic programming approach, particularly as the number of candidate structures increases.

Optimization and Control.title: Stochastic Optimization with Network Distribution Dynamics via Local Jacobian Approximation
Optimization and Control.summary: Network systems feature complex interactions among agents, whereby local decisions can influence the state distributions observed by other agents through coupled network dynamics. Such endogenous distribution shifts across large-scale networks pose significant challenges and call for distributed and adaptive decision-making pipelines. To address these challenges and collectively optimize a steady-state performance objective, we propose a distributed network-aware decision-response (D-NAD) gradient algorithm. This algorithm enables each agent to approximate network-response sensitivity using only local information (i.e., the Jacobians of local dynamics and objectives) and neighborhood communication. We establish a non-asymptotic closed-loop convergence guarantee and quantify the impact of the Jacobian approximation errors therein. Numerical experiments on a semi-synthetic networked electric-vehicle price--demand problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Optimization and Control.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
Optimization and Control.summary:
Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments.
  APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. Experiments are specified through validated configurations, which can also be generated by a planner agent. Before execution, APEX estimates the maximum number of forward simulations required. If the estimate exceeds a user-defined threshold, submission is held for approval. Each run records provenance information, while studies repeat problems across variants and paired replicates and compare results using paired statistical analyses. Scientific and computational components, including methods, simulators, metrics, and optimizers, are implemented as plugins. A command line interface, Python client, REST service with a web interface, and tools for language model agents access these capabilities through a common service layer.

Optimization and Control.title: Using block coordinate descent for solving the close enough traveling salesman problem
Optimization and Control.summary: The Close Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP) is a variant of the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem in which the salesperson must visit some point within a disk associated with each customer. Evaluating a visiting sequence requires determining an optimal visit point within each disk. This building block of virtually every CETSP algorithm is typically computed either by solving a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem with a general-purpose solver, which can be expensive, or by discretizing the disks, which sacrifices optimality. We propose a block coordinate descent (BCD) method that computes these visit points exactly, without discretization, optimizing one visit point at a time. We show that the resulting single-disk subproblem reduces to a one-dimensional minimization, and we characterize its stationary points through the roots of a quartic polynomial. Of the three resulting solution strategies, which agree up to machine precision, Newton's method is the most efficient. Compared with an off-the-shelf SOCP solver, BCD evaluates fixed tours more than an order of magnitude faster. Embedded in an iterated local search (ILS-BCD), it finds the known optimal solutions of 720 small benchmark instances and, on 62 large ones, outperforms all heuristics of their original study in 47 and matches the best of them in 11 others. Within the memetic algorithm MA-CETSP, replacing the general-purpose SOCP solver with BCD and adding an exact local search based on the single-disk solver yields a method that, over the best of 20 runs, is better than the original algorithm in 20 of the 62 large instances and equal in the others, and improves on its best published values in 21. BCD is a fast and exact building block for evaluating visiting sequences that can replace general-purpose SOCP solvers within CETSP algorithms and enables searches that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive.
Optimization and Control.comment: 38 pages, 2 figures, 12 tables. Source code available at https://github.com/rsmatos11/berma2026-cetsp

Optimization and Control.title: A block coordinate descent method for nonconvex multiobjective optimization under Hölder continuity
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper, we propose a block coordinate descent method for unconstrained multiobjective optimization problems with possibly nonconvex objectives and Hölder continuous gradients, intended for large-scale instances, in which updating all the variables simultaneously is expensive. In each iteration, only one block is updated along a descent direction common to all objectives, obtained by minimizing the maximum of their regularized quadratic models. We show that, unlike the single-objective case, stationarity on each block does not imply Pareto stationarity, and that no method that updates only the blocks of a partition of the variables and is monotone in all the objectives reaches, in general, an $ε$-Pareto stationary point. Therefore, when none of the blockwise stationarity measures exceeds the tolerance, the algorithm performs a joint step across all coordinates and terminates only at $ε$-Pareto stationary points. We establish a complexity bound of $O(ε^{-(β+1)/β})$ iterations, where $β$ is the smallest Hölder exponent, the same order as that of methods that update all the variables, as well as bounds on the numbers of function and gradient evaluations, which also hold with one regularization parameter per block.

Optimization and Control.title: Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we study the convergence of a generalization of the Douglas--Rachford algorithm for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators, where reflected resolvents are extended to relaxed resolvents. This extension allows for different step sizes in the resolvents under cocoercivity. We show that the resulting method converges weakly when its parameters lie in a range determined by the cocoercivity constants, which reduces to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Our main results concern the cocoercive case when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, in which the composition is a strict contraction. For both monotone inclusions and convex minimization, we compute the contraction factor and its optimal parameters in closed form, and show that the resulting rates are tight. Whenever the second operator is cocoercive, the optimal rates are strictly smaller than the corresponding rates of forward-backward splitting and of the classical Peaceman--Rachford and Douglas--Rachford algorithms and, in convex minimization, than those of FISTA. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

Optimization and Control.title: Sensitivity to Information Channel and Model Perturbations in Partially Observable Stochastic Control
Optimization and Control.summary: Studying the stability of partially observed Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with respect to perturbations in the transition and observation kernels is a significant problem. While asymptotic robustness/stability results, as approximate transition kernels and/or measurement kernels converge to the true ones, have been previously reported, explicit bounds on value differences and mismatch costs have been limited in scope for POMDPs. The main technical contribution of this paper is a collection of explicit and uniform bounds on the distance between the filter kernels (that is, the kernels of the belief-MDP reduction) of two POMDPs, in the bounded-Lipschitz and Wasserstein metrics, in terms of the total variation and Wasserstein distances between their transition and measurement kernels; we also establish the sharpness of these bounds, demonstrate through counterexamples that the metrics employed cannot be weakened, and present verifiable conditions, stated directly in terms of the defining system functions, under which they apply. Building on these kernel proximity bounds, we show that control policies optimized for approximate models yield explicit performance guarantees when applied to the true model, under both discounted and average cost criteria. Two settings are treated separately: policy transfer, where the controller knows the true model and only the policy is designed for the approximate one, and model misspecification, where the controller also computes its beliefs with the approximate model. As a particular application, we consider the case where the state space and the measurement spaces are quantized to obtain finite models, and we obtain explicit error bounds which decay to zero as the approximations get finer. This provides explicit performance guarantees for model reduction in POMDPs.

Optimization and Control.title: The Traveling Salesman Problem with non-convex polygonal neighborhoods: A hybrid Iterated Local Search--Block Coordinate Descent approach
Optimization and Control.summary: The Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) generalizes the classical TSP by requiring a tour to visit a set of regions in the Euclidean plane rather than fixed point coordinates. It has applications in last-mile delivery, surveillance, and remote sensing in precision agriculture. In this paper, we address the Euclidean TSPN with arbitrary, non-convex polygonal neighborhoods---a highly complex setting due to the joint continuous and combinatorial optimization challenges. To solve the continuous subproblem of determining optimal visit points for a given visiting sequence, we propose a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method based on solving fast one-dimensional geometric subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate that BCD computes optimal visit points for a fixed sequence in almost all instances in which optimality is certified, more than six orders of magnitude faster than a commercial solver solving the equivalent Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Programming (MIQCP) formulation. This efficiency enables an effective hybrid Iterated Local Search metaheuristic (ILS-BCD) that thoroughly explores the combinatorial search space at low computational cost. Extensive computational tests on 235 benchmark instances derived from the Generalized TSP (GTSP), with up to 100 neighborhoods, show that ILS-BCD matched or improved upon the best-known GTSP tours in all cases, obtaining strictly shorter tours in 234 instances. On the 80 instances for which optimality is proven, ILS-BCD attains the optimal tour length in all of them, within a relative difference below 0.001%. On 60 larger instances, with as many as 6,325 neighborhoods, ILS-BCD remains competitive up to about 220.
Optimization and Control.comment: 40 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Supplementary material available as an ancillary file

Optimization and Control.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

Optimization and Control.title: Global Exponential and Inverse Optimal Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
Optimization and Control.summary: For the 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated in surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate, we construct continuous time-invariant feedback laws that stabilize both the roll-free and roll-augmented kinematic models to a target position and orientation in spherical coordinates. The design uses a spherical coordinate transformation with a singular set of codimension two and measure zero. We first present a backstepping design that yields explicit unidirectional, cusp-free feedback laws and strict barrier control Lyapunov functions (CLFs). These establish global exponential stability in spherical coordinates with user-assigned decay rates, while ensuring bounded Cartesian trajectories and exponential convergence to the target, consistent with Brockett's obstruction. The barrier terms guarantee avoidance of the coordinate singularities away from the target. The strict CLFs are then used to develop families of asymptotically stabilizing inverse optimal feedback laws for both systems that minimize a meaningful infinite-horizon cost. These laws inherit infinite gain margins from driftlessness, respect user-defined input bounds through Legendre-Fenchel transformations, and are implementable with either bidirectional or unidirectional surge actuation. Two penalty choices are illustrated: a quadratic input penalty whose associated state running cost approaches a prescribed quadratic form, and an input-constraining penalty that enforces user-defined bounds. This paper lays the foundation for constructive stabilization of the 3D nonholonomic vehicle.
Optimization and Control.comment: Journal version, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control. Unifies and extends two conference papers: v1 of this entry (accepted to the 2026 IEEE Conference on Decision and Control) and arXiv:2609.36212 (submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference), which this version supersedes. v1 remains available as the CDC conference version. 16 pages, 7 figures

Optimization and Control.title: Closing the Accuracy Gap in Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the stochastic first-order complexity of smooth nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization with fresh, conditionally unbiased gradient samples of bounded variance. We assume globally $L$-Lipschitz gradients, bounded $f_y$, $μ$-strong convexity of the lower objective, and $ρ$-Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks. Let $κ=L/μ$, $\vartheta=ρ/μ$, and $χ=1+\vartheta$. For $κ\ge2$, $1\le\vartheta\leκ^2$, every initial-gap budget $Δ>0$, and $0<ε\le c\min\{L,\sqrt{LΔ}\}$, we establish $\mathsf{T}_{\mathrm{SFO}}(ε)=\widetildeΘ(Lχκ^{5/2}Δε^{-2}+Lκ^4σ_f^2Δε^{-4}+L^3\vartheta^2χκ^8σ_g^2Δε^{-6})$, where $σ_f^2$ and $σ_g^2$ are the upper- and lower-level variance budgets. The comparison assumes a finite lower-initialization certificate, holds uniformly over both nonnegative noise budgets, and uses an accuracy constant $c$ independent of conditioning. Three lower-bound families capture the deterministic, upper-noise, and lower-noise contributions. The bounds cover arbitrary randomized adaptive queries and terminal outputs under worst-case expected costs, even for conservative sample gradients. The upper bound combines accelerated frozen-linear-tilt solves with displacement-based reuse of the full upper gradient. An independently chosen base-chain length yields the uniform accuracy range, while a projection and homotopy argument separates undisclosed coordinates from a newly disclosed source, allowing $\vartheta/κ$ to grow without bound. The bounds match polynomial orders and noise transitions; exact logarithmic exponents and coarser accuracies remain open.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Envy-Free Cake-Cutting for Five Agents
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
We study the envy-free cake-cutting problem, in which a divisible resource must be divided among a set of agents with heterogeneous preferences in a way that ensures that no agent envies the piece obtained by another. Remarkably, under some mild continuity assumptions on the agent valuations, it is known that an envy-free division where each agent receives a \emph{connected} piece of the cake is always guaranteed to exist.
  When the valuations are monotone, prior work has shown that a connected $\varepsilon$-envy-free division can be obtained using $\poly(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries for up to four agents, leaving the case of five or more agents open. In this work, we develop a new simpler approach that yields such an efficient algorithm for five agents. Our algorithm uses $\mathcal{O}(\log^3(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and also yields a novel proof of existence for five agents that does not rely on any fixed-point theorems beyond the intermediate value theorem.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Improved Downward-Closed Delegation Bounds
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
We study delegated choice under a downward-closed feasibility constraint, where the principal and agent values of each item may be arbitrarily correlated but items are independent. We give a deterministic, agent-oblivious menu that guarantees the principal more than $29/70\approx0.41429$ of the expected offline optimum under every best response, including ties resolved against the principal. The menu depends only on the feasible family and the principal's value distributions, and verifies a proposal using only its items and their principal values. The previous best guarantee for downward-closed constraints was $0.1098$.
  Matroid constraints admit a guarantee of one half, which is tight already in rank one, but downward-closed constraints do not: a five-item knapsack instance bounds every deterministic menu by $500/1011$ of the optimum, and no rule with randomized acceptance, even one that knows the agent's utilities, can guarantee more than $30/61$. An explicit computer-assisted family of instances lowers the bound to $0.48105$ for all such rules.
  The guarantee is proved by contradiction. If every menu in a fixed family earns at most a $29/70$ fraction of the optimum, then a normalized instance satisfies a finite system of affine inequalities among the survival functions, stop-loss transforms and overshoot means of its clipped optima. An exact rational certificate shows that the system is infeasible. We also give a short analytic proof that a single threshold on the reported total value guarantees $3/10$.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 57 pages. Ancillary files contain the certificates for the computer-assisted parts of the proofs

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We study linear swap regret in self-play against all affine self-maps of each player's strategy polytope. Efficient adversarial bounds for this class scale as $\sqrt{T}$. On compact polytopes given by linear inequalities, our deterministic uncoupled dynamics achieve $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\mathrm{poly}(D)T^{1/3})$ cumulative regret, where $D$ is the binary length of the game description. The bound is independent of the number of vertices. In perfect-recall $n$-player extensive-form games with at most $M$ terminal sequences per player, we obtain $\mathcal{O}(n^2M^4\log T)$ regret against all linear deviations, extending the logarithmic trigger-regret bound of Anagnostides, Farina, and Sandholm [AFS23]. This class can strictly contain the trigger deviations [FP23] and consists exactly of the deviations implementable by untimed communication (UTC), in which a player interleaves moves with mediator queries along a separate feasible path [ZFS24]. The proof combines optimistic log-barrier learning on a compact matrix lift with stability of the Gordon fixed point, using treeplex geometry in extensive form.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS Allocations
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We study maximin share (MMS) allocations of $m$ indivisible items among $n$ agents with additive valuations. We prove that for both goods and chores, the optimal MMS approximation factor converges to $1$ as $n$ grows. In particular, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large $n$, and any $m$, we give polynomial-time algorithms that compute a $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for goods and a $(1+\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for chores. Furthermore, both algorithms can be implemented using a polynomial number of bundle comparisons.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 37 pages

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Approximate MMS allocations for large number of agents
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We consider allocation of indivisible items to agents with non-negative additive valuations, under the maximin share (MMS) fairness benchmark. We prove that for every $ρ< 1$, there exists some $n_ρ$ such that every allocation instance with $n \ge n_ρ$ agents has a $ρ$-MMS allocation. This was explicitly stated as a conjecture in a recent paper of the authors, where it was shown to hold if the number of items is at most $(2 - ε)n$ (and $n \ge n_{ρ, ε}$). We build on some techniques from that earlier paper, including the construction of $\textit{ordinal MMS}$ allocations that give $n - O(\log^2 n)$ agents their full MMS. Among the new techniques that we introduce is the definition of $\textit{block-matchings}$ between the MMS partitions of two agents, and a proof that if the number of item types is small, then block-matchings of small width necessarily exist.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Scaling Chance-Constrained Correlated Equilibrium Computation for Exclusive Resource-Assignment Games
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: The chance-constrained correlated equilibrium concept provides a robust coordination technique for self-interested agents whose costs are uncertain to a central coordinator, but the number of joint actions considered in its computation grows exponentially with the number of agents. We develop a reduced-rank formulation based on convex combinations of chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria to improve scalability. To further reduce computation, we propose an exact-one resource-assignment restriction for games in which agents compete for shared resources and simultaneous use of a resource is undesirable or unsafe. The restriction allows each resource to be assigned to exactly one agent, reducing the number of joint actions considered from O(2^(nr)) to O(n^r) for n agents and r resources. The resulting problem is solved over the restricted joint action set while retaining all incentive constraints associated with unilateral deviations. We show that the feasible set of the restricted problem is exactly the convex hull of the chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria contained in the exact-one assignment set, yielding a necessary and sufficient condition for nonemptiness. We further derive a sufficient condition under which all chance-constrained pure Nash equilibria of the unrestricted game are retained by the restriction. Numerical experiments in a vertiport departure-corridor coordination scenario demonstrate a 99.81% reduction in median computation time relative to the unrestricted formulation while achieving equivalent coordination performance.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: k-Submodular Cover Problem with a Matroid Constraint
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: We investigate k-submodular cover problem with a matroid constraint on an n-element ground set V , which seeks k disjoint subsets of V with minimal cost, where their union is an independent set for some matroid defined on V and the k-submodular utility function surpasses a specified threshold. This problem generalizes the k-submodular cover problem and has a wide range of applications in artificial intelligence and combinatorial optimization. In this paper, we propose a matroid extended greedy algorithm for this problem, analyze its bi-criteria approximation ratio, and further derive an improved approximation ratio under the special case of unit costs.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Playing Markov Games Without Observing Payoffs
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Optimization under uncertainty is a fundamental problem in learning and decision-making, particularly in multi-agent systems. Previously, Feldman, Kalai, and Tennenholtz [2010] demonstrated the ability to efficiently compete in repeated symmetric two-player matrix games without observing payoffs, as long as the opponents actions are observed. In this paper, we introduce and formalize a new class of zero-sum symmetric Markov games, which extends the notion of symmetry from matrix games to the Markovian setting. We show that even without observing payoffs, a player who knows the transition dynamics and observes only the opponents sequence of actions can still compete against an adversary who may have complete knowledge of the game. We formalize three distinct notions of symmetry in this setting and show that, under these conditions, the learning problem can be reduced to an instance of online learning, enabling the player to asymptotically match the return of the opponent despite lacking payoff observations. Our algorithms apply to both matrix and Markov games, and run in polynomial time with respect to the size of the game and the number of episodes. Our work broadens the class of games in which robust learning is possible under severe informational disadvantage and deepens the connection between online learning and adversarial game theory.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Why Last-Iterate Scale-Invariant Regret Matching Converges Linearly?
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Scale-invariant extragradient regret matching (IREG-PRM+) normalizes the cumulative regret vector by its own norm and attains optimal regret without knowing the payoff scale. On two-player zero-sum matrix games, its last iterate converges linearly in experiments. Prior theory leaves this behavior unexplained. Analysis is difficult because the algorithm lacks a fixed step size. The step size is the inverse of the regret norm, which changes along the trajectory. Existing proofs of linear rates for regret-matching dynamics rely on restarts or modified updates. We explain the unmodified algorithm's convergence through norm saturation. The regret norm grows to a finite limit, so the step size converges as well. We prove that saturation always occurs and provide an explicit upper bound. The last iterate then converges to a single Nash equilibrium in every two-player zero-sum matrix game, even with multiple equilibria. Near a unique equilibrium, the set of active actions freezes after one round, and the linearized dynamics have a closed form. Take the payoff matrix restricted to these active actions and centered by the game value. Whenever the limiting step size times this matrix's largest singular value is less than one, the last iterate converges linearly at a closed-form rate. Across $216$ random games, all $184$ instances with a numerically resolved limit satisfy this condition. The predicted rate matches the empirical rate with a median ratio of $1.000$. Our analysis also shows that the per-round increase in the squared regret norm scales with the squared Nash gap, which measures distance to equilibrium. In sequential games (extensive-form games), exact gap computation requires a costly best-response pass. On Kuhn and Leduc poker, the analogous norm increase tracks the Nash gap between infrequent passes. Our code is available at https://github.com/lbn187/NormCert
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 66 pages, 3 figures

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 19 pages

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Query-Sample Tradeoffs for Revenue Maximization
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
We introduce and study the full query-sample tradeoff for revenue maximization with a single buyer whose value follows an unknown distribution. A learner may adaptively combine value samples, which reveal full buyer values, with pricing queries, which reveal only whether a fresh buyer accepts a selected price. The goal is to learn a price that achieves a $(1-\varepsilon)$-multiplicative approximation to optimal revenue with high probability. We ask when, and by how much, reducing the sample budget increases the number of pricing queries required.
  We establish tight tradeoff bounds for monotone-hazard-rate (MHR), regular, and quasi-monotone-hazard-rate (quasi-MHR) distributions, and almost tight bounds for quasi-regular distributions. Our results reveal sharply different benefits from combining the two information sources. Quasi-MHR distributions admit a smooth intermediate tradeoff: additional samples can reduce the query requirement by polynomial factors. For MHR and regular distributions, however, a sufficiently small constant fraction of the sample-only requirement still leaves the learner facing the full asymptotic query cost attainable with one sample. Our upper bounds are achieved by algorithms that collect all value samples before making queries, while our lower bounds hold even under arbitrary adaptive interleaving of the two forms of access. Along the way, we also fully characterize the sample-only and single-sample query complexities for all four families, eliminating the extra logarithmic dependence on $1/\varepsilon$ in the literature.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 59 pages, 8 figures. This paper substantially extends arXiv:2602.10483 by establishing the full query-sample tradeoffs and obtaining tight sample-only and single-sample query complexity bounds

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: The Oracle Is Not Enough: Secure Settlement for Prediction Markets
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
Prediction markets are becoming an important mechanism for aggregating information and forecasting uncertain real-world events. As they grow in scale and value, reliable settlement becomes critical because settlement determines the winning outcome and allocation of market collateral. Yet many heterogeneous markets require market-specific evidence and interpretation, and incorrect settlement can create direct financial incentives for manipulation. In this paper, we ask how to settle heterogeneous markets correctly and efficiently at scale. We first compare existing settlement designs in their support for heterogeneous markets, reliance on direct operator intervention, and resistance to manipulation, motivating a layered architecture that combines incentivized crowdsourcing with stake-backed voting and selective post-settlement review.
  Building on this architecture, we develop a stake-backed settlement protocol that provides economic security and settlement liveness under market-specific verification costs. Specifically, we prove that manipulation is unprofitable for every settled market and give two constructions that support sufficient self-enforcing participation with controlled reward expenditure. Using historical Polymarket and UMA data, we evaluate the protocol under real-world conditions. We find that 99% of admitted markets can be settled with modest participation rewards even under high verification costs.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: An allocator knows the indivisible goods, the number $n$ of agents, and the $k$ possible additive valuations. Each agent reveals their type on arrival and must immediately receive an irrevocable bundle. Kulkarni, Mehta, and Shahkar established a deterministic guarantee of $1/k$ of maximin share (MMS) and an upper bound of $2/(\sqrt{k}-2)$ for $k>4$. We determine the optimal order $Θ(k^{-1/2})$ by constructing a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select. On every arrival sequence, it gives each agent a fraction $(1/\sqrt{2}-o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ of their truncated proportional share. This share dominates MMS and is the largest target $y$ for which the item values capped at $y$ sum to at least $ny$. By specializing the construction of Kulkarni et al. to two arrivals and counting its types exactly, we sharpen the upper bound to $(\sqrt{2}+o(1))/\sqrt{k}$ even for binary valuations. For two arrivals with binary valuations and every $k\ge2$, the optimal fraction is $1/p$, where $p$ is the largest integer with $1+\binom{2p}{2}\le k$. In particular, up to six binary types permit full maximin share. For two arbitrary additive types, a different polynomial-time algorithm guarantees $4/7$ of maximin share for any number of agents. This ratio is tight for the algorithm. With three arrivals and two types, the optimal deterministic fraction is exactly $9/10$. For randomized policies with $k$ known additive types, the optimal MMS fraction guaranteed to all agents with probability at least $1-δ$ on every fixed arrival sequence is $Θ(\max\{k^{-1/2},\sqrtδ\})$ for $0\leδ<1$.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: 27 pages. Lean 4 formalization: https://github.com/EsperZhou/online-mms-lean/tree/lean-v1.0.1

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Beyond the Limits of Welfarism: An Affordable Proportional Approval Voting Rule
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Two of the most widely studied voting rules in approval-based multiwinner elections are Proportional Approval Voting (PAV), which maximizes a welfare score over committees of a fixed size, and the Method of Equal Shares (MES), which gives voters equal budgets and selects candidates whose supporters can pay for them. MES guarantees priceability and laminar proportionality, both of which can fail for PAV. Can PAV offer similar guarantees without giving voters budgets? To answer this question, we go beyond the limits of welfarism by allowing PAV to select committees of varying size, while penalizing larger committees. Both our exact rule and its polynomial-time local-search variant produce outcomes that admit a priceable completion and, on laminar instances, a laminar-proportional one. Our analysis carefully separates the roles of two marginal stability conditions. At suitable thresholds, addition stability gives a strong proportionality guarantee in the form of EJR+, while deletion stability limits overrepresentation and ensures affordability. We use these conditions to derive welfare and coverage guarantees for different completions of our rules. The same welfare comparison also improves the best known lower bound on the utilitarian ratio of standard PAV.

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Job-Scheduling Games with Time-Dependent Processing Times
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary:
Job-scheduling games have traditionally assumed fixed processing times. However, in many realistic environments, ranging from cyber-security response to high-frequency trading, a task's duration depends on its starting time. We study job-scheduling games with time-dependent processing times, where job lengths are linear functions of their start times, exhibiting either positive deterioration (increasing length) or negative deterioration (decreasing length). We analyze these games under various coordination mechanisms and priority policies. By introducing the concept of delay-averse agents, we provide a unifying framework to characterize equilibrium existence. For delay-averse jobs, we show that stability is maintained and pure Nash equilibria (NE) can be computed efficiently. In contrast, for non-delay-averse jobs, we demonstrate that a NE may not exist, and prove that deciding its existence is NP-complete, even on identical machines - a fundamental departure from classical coordination mechanisms.
  Regarding equilibrium inefficiency, we show that the Price of Anarchy (PoA) can be significantly higher than in environments with fixed processing times. To mitigate this, we propose and analyze three coordination mechanisms: SBPT (Shortest Basic Processing Time), which reduces the PoA in games with positive deterioration to a constant, and SDR (Smallest Deterioration Rate) and LBDR (Largest Basic-Deterioration Ratio) for negative deterioration, which achieve tight constant PoA bounds of $2$ and $\max\{\frac{e}{e-1}, 2-\frac{1}{m}\}$, respectively. Our results bridge the gap between centralized time-dependent scheduling and decentralized game-theoretic analysis.
Computer Science and Game Theory.comment: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (Sofsem 2027)

Computer Science and Game Theory.title: Consumer Search and Social Learning in Agentic Markets
Computer Science and Game Theory.summary: Motivated by agentic markets -- where AI tools facilitate search -- we propose a model of consumer search and market-wide learning. A sequence of consumers engage in costly search to acquire progressively refined signals of product fit prior to purchase. The market observes acquired signals and post-transaction feedback thereby impacting future searches. We solve for the per-consumer optimal search policy and characterize the steady-state of the learning dynamics. Search technologies (agentic or otherwise) that reduce costs at fixed inspection depth improve long-run learning and consumer surplus. In a special case with screen-level feedback, more informative search also improves these outcomes. In contrast, we show through counterexamples and numerical simulations that more informative search can degrade long-run learning and consumer surplus when the market observes only aggregate inspection and transaction feedback, highlighting the importance of feedback design.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling. This paper introduces a time-aware transformer that extends a Chessformer-style architecture with learned temporal conditioning tokens encoding player clock state, time control, and recent tempo, together with behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation. The model is trained on large-scale online chess data and evaluated against time-agnostic baselines and the state of the art. Results show that temporal conditioning yields modest overall accuracy improvements but substantially stronger gains under time pressure. Beyond move choice, it also produces more accurate thinking-time and resignation predictions. More importantly, the model better matches human move-quality degradation in critical time regimes, reducing the systematic over-strength observed in time-agnostic behavioral cloning models. These results suggest that temporal state is a previously underutilized but important signal for human behavioral cloning in chess.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Accepted manuscript of the paper published at the 2026 IEEE Gaming, Entertainment, and Media Conference (GEM). Code: https://github.com/Prof-it/temporal-chess-model; weights: https://huggingface.co/holymolyyy/temporal-chess-model

Human-Computer Interaction.title: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities. However, radar-based activity recognition remains constrained by the limited availability of large-scale datasets. We introduce the Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) dataset to addresses the gaps identified in existing work: 1) it expands the scale of available data by providing over eight hours of annotated recordings in which a person performs eight distinct activities; 2) it overcomes room configuration limitations by recording from five different locations in a two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartment; and 3) it extends beyond primitive actions to focus on high-level ADLs. In addition to the dataset, this paper introduces practical guidance for future ADL dataset construction. We conducted a detailed analysis of how ADLs are prioritized across academic research, health survey tools, and clinical trials to identify clinically significant ADLs. Furthermore, we provide our experimental design, data collection and annotation strategies, post-processing pipeline for forming the R-ADL dataset from raw data, and baseline results on standard machine learning architectures. The R-ADL dataset serves as a valuable resource for advancing ADL recognition systems as we continue building larger and more diverse datasets.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited. This study examined how supportive versus challenging chatbot interaction styles shape user experience and continuance intention, and whether people-pleasing tendency (PPT) moderates these effects across cultures. Taiwanese (N = 49) and Korean (N = 52) participants completed a collaborative tourism-planning task. Results showed that: (1) supportive chatbots consistently led to higher continuance intention, satisfaction, and trust; (2) PPT did not moderate these effects; and (3) cultural variation emerged only in perceived threat, where higher PPT was associated with greater baseline threat in the Taiwanese but not the Korean sample. These findings reveal how a general-purpose LLM style may differentially activate culturally situated social scripts, raising implications for culturally inclusive conversational AI design.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Accepted to the 4th Workshop on Cross-Cultural Considerations in NLP (C3NLP) at ACL 2026

Human-Computer Interaction.title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API).
