Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $σ^2/Δ^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.
Probability.comment: 29 pages, 8 figures. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24532266

Probability.title: Exponential integrability of SLE Minkowski content
Probability.summary: Let $0<κ<8$, $d=1+κ/8$, and $q=2/(2-d)$. Let $μ$ be the $d$-dimensional Minkowski content measure of either chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ in $\mathbb H$ from $0$ to $\infty$ or two-sided whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_κ$ through $0$. We prove that there exist constants $c_κ,C_κ\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \mathbb E\exp\left\{c_κ\left(\frac{μ(D)}{(\operatorname{diam} D)^d}\right)^q\right\}\le C_κ\] for every deterministic bounded Borel set $D$ of positive diameter in the corresponding domain. The exponent $q$ in this moment bound is optimal in both settings. We also show that, almost surely, $μ(B(z,r))=O\bigl(r^d(\log(1/r))^{1/q}\bigr)$ as $r\downarrow0$, locally uniformly in $z$.

Probability.title: Tightness for branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment
Probability.summary: We consider the maximum $M_t$ of branching random walk in a space-inhomogeneous random environment on $\mathbb{Z}$. In this model the branching rate while at some location $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ is randomized in an i.i.d. manner. We prove that there is a centering $\widetilde{m}_t$ depending only on the environment such that $(M_t-\widetilde{m}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is tight in an annealed sense.
Probability.comment: 58 pages, 3 figures; fixed typos, fixed the proof of Lemma 5.5, added a reference to arXiv:2601.09214

Probability.title: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
Probability.summary: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $μ$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $μ+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

Probability.title: The truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem
Probability.summary: We study the truncated moment problem on the one-dimensional full integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, seeking necessary and sufficient conditions for a prescribed sequence of $n$ real numbers to be $\mathbb{Z}-$representable, i.e. to be the sequence of the first $n$ moments of a probability measure supported on $\mathbb{Z}$. Building on the approach developed in 2017 in Infusino et al. for the truncated moment problem on the non-negative integers, we establish a complete characterization of $\mathbb{Z}-$representable sequences for every truncation order $n$. From this result, we derive an inductive and computable $\mathbb{Z}-$representability criterion. More generally, we also investigate the relationship between the truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem and the truncated Hamburger moment problem, seen as its continuous counterpart.

Probability.title: Prevalence of the periodicity of maximizing measures
Probability.summary: For a continuous map $T\colon X\rightarrow X$ on a compact metric space $(X,d)$, we say that a function $f\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ has the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ if its time averages along forward orbits of $T$ are maximized at a periodic orbit. In this article, we establish the Hunt--Ott conjecture (cf.~\cite{HO96a,HO96b}), that is, the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ is prevalent (in the sense of Hunt--Sauer--Yorke) in the space of Lipschitz functions with respect to a standard metric for subshifts of finite type. This result is a strengthening of \cite[Theorem~A]{BZ16} and \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DLZ24}, confirms the prediction mentioned in the ICM proceeding contribution of Bochi (\cite[Section~1]{Boc18}) suggested by experimental evidence.

Probability.title: Low-degree hardness rules out eigenvalue tests but not eigenvector tests
Probability.summary:
We study what low-degree hardness implies for spectral tests, with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) as the null distribution. We show that, once a fixed amount of Gaussian noise is added, it rules out every test based on eigenvalues, but not tests based on eigenvectors. For eigenvalues, if the low-degree advantage vanishes at logarithmic degree, then the joint law of the noisy eigenvalues converges to that of the GOE in total variation. For eigenvectors, we construct planted distributions with vanishing low-degree advantage whose eigenvalues follow the GOE law exactly at every noise level, yet whose noisy eigenvectors still distinguish them from the GOE. A single eigenvector can suffice. After a small amount of noise, a polynomial-time test that uses only the span of a fixed fraction of the top eigenvectors also succeeds, even when the low-degree advantage vanishes at a prescribed polylogarithmic degree.
  To prove the eigenvalue result, we split the noise into three increments. The first uses the low-degree assumption to establish eigenvalue rigidity. The second couples the two spectra through Dyson Brownian motion and applies homogenization to obtain a transport estimate. The third uses Gaussian smoothing to convert this estimate into closeness in total variation.

Probability.title: Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves
Probability.summary: We introduce a notion of continuity equation on metric spaces that is capable of describing curves of probability measures which are absolutely continuous or, more generally, of bounded variation (BV) with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance. This continuity equation is based on a notion of measure-valued derivations, whose basic theory is also developed in this paper. On $\mathbb{R}^n$, our formulation is consistent with the continuity equation with singular flux introduced by Almi--Rossi--Savaré (arXiv:2506.15333), including the corresponding notion of minimal solutions when the norm is strictly convex. In this work, we characterize BV-curves in the space of probability measures equipped with the (extended) 1-Wasserstein distance as those curves satisfying the continuity equation with a measure-valued derivation of finite mass. To this aim, we extend our previous work (Calc. Var. (2024) 63:16) on probabilistic representations on BV-curves and construct from them measure-valued derivations (resp. flux measures) on geodesic metric spaces (resp. on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Probability.title: Algebraic Transfer of Gaussian Chaoses: Moment Geometry and Spectral Ideals
Probability.summary: We prove the partition moment conjecture of Adamczak, Latała and Meller for decoupled Gaussian chaoses of every order with coefficients in arbitrary real Banach spaces. The corresponding pairing bound retains partition weights only on the unpaired slots. We give Talagrand's requested construction of admissible partitions for unions of operator ellipsoids and refute Bednorz and Martynek's Bernoulli increment comparison conjecture. For directed operator contractions, we obtain constant-one Schatten bounds and the optimal logarithmic loss for weak Schatten links. Strictly entrywise-positive block matrices refute Li and Zhao's trace-norm compression conjecture. For radial singular Wick multipliers on groups of polynomial growth, we determine exact Schatten thresholds, almost-sure singular-value decay and critical Weyl constants. The constants come from Gaussian Wick matrices in the virtually abelian case and powers of a free circular element otherwise. For finite-group convolutions, we classify projected Plancherel limits and give singular-value and Gaussian eigenvalue limits at general coefficient covariance.

Probability.title: Simultaneous ruin probabilities for Brownian risks with a deterministic splitting time
Probability.summary: We consider two Brownian risk processes which coincide up to a fixed time and subsequently evolve with correlated increments. For a finite time horizon after the split, we derive the exact asymptotics of their simultaneous ruin probability as the initial reserves tend to infinity proportionally. The terminal correlation separates the two asymptotic regimes for the ratio to the joint tail at the terminal time. If both coordinates contribute to the leading Gaussian tail, the ratio is a bivariate Piterbarg-type constant, for which we give an integral representation and explicit bounds. In the remaining regimes the ratio equals two, with a Gaussian factor in the endpoint tail at the transition. We also obtain asymptotics on intervals of length of order $u^{-2}$ near the terminal time and an exponential limit law for the first simultaneous ruin time, conditional on ruin by the horizon.

Probability.title: Iterated harmonic envelopes for multidimensional optimal stopping
Probability.summary: Motivated by the contrast between the classical least-concave-majorant representation of Dynkin and Yushkevich in one dimension and the substantially more complicated potential-theoretic structure of optimal stopping in higher dimensions, we identify a fundamental barrier: a localisation obstruction caused by the geometry of Brownian paths in dimensions $d\ge2$. We overcome it with an iterative construction based on harmonic-function envelopes, each an infimum of harmonic replacements on subdomains of the current non-contact set, with the previous envelope as boundary data. From a continuous gain function $g$, this produces a decreasing sequence of upper bounds $w_n$ converging uniformly to the value function $V$ of optimal stopping. The process may be Brownian motion or, more generally, any diffusion with a short list of properties, including polarity of points. For Brownian motion, every iterate inherits the modulus of continuity of the data. Exponential discounting may be included, and the state space may be a bounded regular domain with absorption at the boundary, or the whole space under a condition at infinity. Equivalently, the iterates converge to the solution of the associated obstacle problem. At each iteration an explicit stopping rule gives a lower bound for $V$. Both bounds are computed from the construction alone, without knowledge of $V$, and their gap falls below any given threshold after finitely many iterations. The first exit time from the limit non-contact set is optimal.
Probability.comment: 36 pages, 1 figure. Substantially revised and retitled

Probability.title: The Brownian Lévy transformation is exact
Probability.summary: We prove that the Lévy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.

Probability.title: A branching construction for nonlinear Hawkes processes - Application to a case of infinite inhibition
Probability.summary: This article aims at introducing a genealogical branching structure for a wide class of nonlinear Hawkes processes. This construction extends the well-known Poisson cluster decomposition for linear Hawkes processes to the nonlinear case. More precisely, we perform a past dependent pruning of a Crump-Mode-Jagers tree with immigration and obtain an explicit formula for the conditional intensity of the point measure charging the birth times of the individuals. This pruning can be interpreted as the spreading of a heritable mutation in the population, when the mutation rate depends on the past of the population. Changing the parameters of the underlying Crump-Mode-Jagers process, as well as those of the pruning, allows obtaining various intensity functions, including those of the nonlinear Hawkes processes, thus embedding the nonlinear Hawkes process in a larger family of past-dependent point processes. We thereby provide the first embedding of a genealogical structure within a nonlinear Hawkes process, and obtain as a byproduct a new coupling with an upperbounding linear Hawkes. We finally study the impact of adding periods of infinite inhibition after each event of a supercritical Hawkes process. In particular we show that depending on the existence of a delay for this infinite inhibition, the process can exhibit either linear or exponential growth of the number of events with time. We obtain explicit criteria for both behaviors depending on the reproduction function, the delay and the length of these inhibition periods.

Probability.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
Probability.summary: We prove that, for every noncommutative polynomial in independent GUE matrices, the empirical eigenvalue distribution converges almost surely to the Brown measure of the same polynomial in free semicircular variables. This is the Gaussian case of a conjecture of Belinschi, Śniady and Speicher. We also prove that the spectrum converges almost surely in Hausdorff distance to the spectrum of the limiting operator, so that the spectral radius converges as well; deviations have probability smaller than every inverse power of the matrix size. For this we show that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables is its whole spectrum, a statement about operators that involves no random matrices. We also give an algorithm, with a convergence guarantee, that computes the limiting Brown measure from matrices whose size depends only on the polynomial. A holomorphic rotation introduces an independent Ginibre component and yields the almost-sure limit without a least-singular-value bound for the original GUE polynomial. We also give a second-moment criterion for weak convergence of Brown measures. On free probability side, we use the Dyson equation of a linear pencil to show that harmonicity of its logarithmic potential forces invertibility.

Probability.title: Large deviations for integrated exponentials of Gaussian Volterra processes - application to variance options
Probability.summary: We prove small-time large deviations for the normalised time integral of the exponential of a Gaussian Volterra process, and complement it with a central limit theorem and moderate deviations. As an application, we obtain short-maturity asymptotics for out-of-the-money and at-the-money variance options in rough volatility models, as well as implied volatility expansions which we validate numerically.

Probability.title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
Probability.summary: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by Götze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.

Probability.title: Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit in the siblings of the coupon collector
Probability.summary: In the siblings (or brotherhood) variant of the coupon collector's problem, a main collector draws coupons until her own album is complete and passes every duplicate down a chain of siblings; the $j$th collector is then left with $U_j^N$ empty places, $j\ge 2$. It has been conjectured [stated as an open problem in the work that introduced the model] that, for every fixed number of coupon types $N$ and every $j\ge 2$, the expected deficit $\E[U_j^N]$ is maximized by the equiprobable coupon distribution. We prove this in a sharp, finite-$N$ form: $\E[U_j^N]$ is strictly larger at the uniform vector than at any other probability vector, and indeed strictly increases along every ray running from an arbitrary distribution toward the uniform one. The proof is exact and elementary in its ingredients. An inclusion--exclusion step turns the governing Poissonized integral into a one-dimensional integral with a separable integrand; a single integration by parts then rewrites the radial derivative of $\E[U_j^N]$ as a positively weighted covariance of an increasing function, whose sign is settled by Chebyshev's correlation inequality. We show that $\E[U_j^N]$ is \emph{not} Schur-concave, so that no majorization or pairwise-smoothing argument can yield the result, and we explain why the recent variance-extremality method of Long~[Long, arXiv:2604.25108, 2026] does not transfer. As by-products we obtain a finite closed form for $\E[U_j^N]$ over subsets of the coupon set and the exact Hessian of $\E[U_j^N]$ at the uniform vector. The argument extends without change to all real $j>1$.

Probability.title: A very short proof of Sidorenko's inequality for counts of homomorphism between graphs
Probability.summary: A fundamental extremality result due to Sidorenko (Discrete Math. 131.1-3, 1994) states that among all connected graphs G on k vertices, the k-vertex star maximises the number of graph homomorphisms of G into any graph H. We provide a new short proof of this result using only a simple recursive counting argument for trees and Hölder's inequality.
Probability.comment: 5 pages. v3: corrected minor mistake in statement and proof of Corollary 2 as well as some typographical errors. Main theorem unchanged

Probability.title: Fixed Points and Envelope Dynamics on Credal Hyperspaces
Probability.summary: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and consider the hyperspace $\mathscr C_X$ of nonempty weakly closed convex sets of Borel probability measures on $X$, called credal sets. These sets represent uncertainty about which probability law governs the phenomenon of interest. We equip $\mathscr C_X$ with the Hausdorff metric induced by a metric for weak convergence. Credal order intervals $[\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}] = \{ \mathcal{P}\in\mathscr C_X: \mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{B} \}$ are complete lattices, and every inclusion-monotone, Hausdorff-continuous self map of such an interval has least and greatest fixed points obtained as limits of iteration from $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. For families of inclusion-monotone updates that may vary with time, we construct lower and upper envelope maps that bound every admissible trajectory. When these envelope maps are Hausdorff-continuous, the distance of every trajectory from a limiting credal interval vanishes uniformly over all switching sequences and initial credal sets. Coalescence of the limiting interval endpoints yields convergence to a common credal limit. We then construct the credal evolution induced by a time consistent Nisio semigroup. Uniform $W_1$ contraction of the underlying Markov semigroups induces Hausdorff-Wasserstein contraction of the credal evolution, yielding a unique common invariant credal set, exponential convergence from every initial credal set, and a support functional equal to the robust ergodic limit. We also derive perturbation bounds from finite time Nisio discrepancies and one step kernel set discrepancies, and characterize the countable sequences of support coordinates that represent credal sets, providing an explicit reconstruction formula.

Probability.title: Self-similar co-ascent processes and Palm calculus
Probability.summary: We study certain renormalised first passage bridges of self-similar processes, generalising the "Brownian co-ascent process" discussed by Panzo (Sém. Prob. L, 2019) and introduced by Rosenbaum and Yor (Sém. Prob. XLVI, 2014). We provide a characterisation of co-ascent processes via Palm measures, namely that the co-ascent of a self-similar process is the process under the Palm distribution associated with its record measure. We use this representation to derive a distributional identity for alpha-stable Lévy-subordinators with alpha in (0,1).
Probability.comment: 18 pages. v2 updated to incorporate journal-version corrections and expanded proofs; two typographical errors in the journal version concerning the Brownian subordinator are also corrected

Probability.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
Probability.summary: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.

Probability.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
Probability.summary: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, μ)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, μ)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, μ)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, μ)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, μ)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.
Probability.comment: 25 pages, 15 pages of body, 9 pages of appendices, 2 pages of references

Probability.title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
Probability.summary: The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.

Probability.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
Probability.summary: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(θ)=|q_n(e^{iθ})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-Γ(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.
Probability.comment: 156 pages. This version presents a direct proof using real analysis. A shorter and simpler proof using complex-analytic methods will be available soon

Probability.title: Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results
Probability.summary: This paper investigates inverse problems for backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), with a particular focus on the converse comparison theorem and the uniqueness of generators solely through the initial values of the corresponding solutions. To this end, we develop a forward-SDE representation approach that combines a contradiction argument with a representation of generators in terms of solutions to associated forward stochastic differential equations (SDEs). As one of the main consequences, we prove that an ordering between two $g$-expectations necessarily implies the pointwise comparability of their generators, without requiring any additional structural assumptions beyond the standard Lipschitz condition. This removes the continuity, $y$-independence, and deterministic assumptions required in previous works, thereby yielding a complete solution to the converse comparison problem for $g$-expectations under the standard Lipschitz framework and, at the same time, establishing a general uniqueness theorem for generators of BSDEs.

Probability.title: On the applicability of the maximality principle in optimal stopping: an example involving a diffusion and its running maximum
Probability.summary: The maximality principle has proved to be a valuable tool for identifying the optimal stopping boundaries in optimal stopping problems involving one-dimensional time-homogeneous diffusions and their running maximum processes. The principle characterises the optimal stopping boundary as the maximal solution to a first-order nonlinear ODE that remains strictly below the diagonal in $\mathbb{R}^2$ or a "zero-level curve". In this paper, we construct a suitably tailored optimal stopping problem to which the maximality principle is not applicable.

Probability.title: Generic non-convergence of low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics on $\mathbb Z^2$
Probability.summary: We study how typical convergence is, in the topological sense of Baire category, for the heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the nearest-neighbour, zero-field Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ started from translation-invariant initial laws. At sufficiently low positive temperature, we show that the initial laws whose evolution has both the plus and the minus phase as weak subsequential limits form a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of translation-invariant laws with the weak topology. Consequently, the initial laws for which the dynamics converges in distribution form a meagre set, which gives a partial answer to an open problem posed by Liggett. In particular, a large initial magnetisation does not force convergence to the plus phase, even for spatially ergodic initial laws. The proof combines equilibrium and mixing estimates of Gheissari and Sly with a periodic grid of plus spins of vanishing density and Baire's theorem, and it applies to all reversible monotone Glauber dynamics for the Ising model.

Probability.title: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property
Probability.summary: We characterize the time-consistency of convex, cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures in terms of their minimal penalty. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities, which factorize across an intermediate date in many ways, according to how the discount is allocated to the two periods. We introduce an infimal cocycle property, in which the penalty is the infimum over all such factorizations, and show that it is equivalent to time-consistency, with the infimum attained. This holds on $L^\infty$ under continuity from below, and on $L^p$, $p<\infty$, without continuity assumptions. In the cash-additive case it reduces to the classical cocycle property. For risk measures induced by BSDEs, it represents the dynamic programming principle of a stochastic control problem whose value is the penalty.

Probability.title: Derivative Estimation from Coarse, Irregular, Noisy Samples: An MLE-Spline Approach
Probability.summary: We address numerical differentiation under coarse, non-uniform sampling and Gaussian noise. A maximum-likelihood estimator with $L_2$-norm constraint on a higher-order derivative is obtained, yielding spline-based solution. We introduce a non-standard parameterization of quadratic splines and develop recursive online algorithms. Two formulations---quadratic and zero-order---offer tradeoff between smoothness and computational speed. Simulations demonstrate superior performance over high-gain observers and super-twisting differentiators under coarse sampling and high noise, benefiting systems where higher sampling rates are impractical.

Probability.title: Two-type thinning with alternative leader rate for random partition structures
Probability.summary: A dust-free random partition structure with infinitely many parts is a random sequence $(\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots)$ with $\mathsf{X}_1>\mathsf{X}_2>\dots>0$ such that $\mathsf{X}_1+\mathsf{X}_2+\dots=1$, almost surely. The Poisson-Dirichlet $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ distributions for $0<m<1$ are defined such that $\mathsf{X}_n = ξ_n^{-1/m}/\sum_{ν=1}^{\infty} ξ_ν^{-1/m}$, where $0<ξ_1<ξ_2<\dots$ is a homogeneous Poisson point process. It is a model for thinning invariant random partition structures, where every one of the infinitely many parts $\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots$ are thinned IID at rate 1. We consider a 2-type thinning where the instantaneous leader is deleted with an alternative rate $1+r\geq 0$. Then we seek time stationary random partition structures. When $r =R\in \{0,1,\dots\}$ a solution is obtained by taking $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ and performing ``balayage,'' where balayage means simply excavating the first $R$ points. We find the solutions for all $r \in (-1,\infty)$, which we call $\mathrm{PD}^{(r)}(m,0)$. We motivate with an application, and we present graphical representations.

Probability.title: Vote-Left: A Deterministic Coordination Strategy for the Faithful in The Traitors
Probability.summary: The Traitors is a social deduction game in which an informed minority of Traitors face an uninformed majority of Faithful, and the recurring question facing the Faithful is how to vote. Eliminating a player chosen uniformly at random is optimal for the Faithful when it can be guaranteed, but when votes are cast individually a random vote is indistinguishable from a strategic one, leaving the Faithful exposed to coordinated Traitor collusion. We introduce the Vote-Left protocol, a deterministic rule under which every player votes for the next surviving player in a fixed cyclic ordering. It reproduces the banishment distribution of random voting, yet any deviation from it is immediately identifiable. Combined with a simple punishment rule, Vote-Left punishes every deviation in the main phase of the game that does not end it at once, whether by a single player or by the Traitors acting together. In the final rounds punishment arrives too late, and the Faithful should return to random voting there. Under this switching protocol no player gains by departing from Vote-Left in the main phase, and with a single Traitor it is a Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium of the whole game. Across the televised configurations, it raises the Faithful's winning probability by a factor of approximately four over random voting under collusion with three Traitors, and by a factor of 62 to 84 with four.

Probability.title: Reconstruction of Poisson Random Measures in the Variational Framework with Applications to Jump-Driven SPDEs
Probability.summary:
We establish a reconstruction principle for Poisson random measures arising in compactness arguments for jump-driven stochastic partial differential equations. A basic difficulty in such arguments is that, after a Skorokhod-type representation, almost sure convergence of the solution processes does not by itself identify the limiting stochastic integral, since integration with respect to a compensated Poisson random measure is not a pathwise continuous functional of the solution and the noise.
  We address this problem in the variational framework of a Gelfand triple $V\hookrightarrow H\equiv H^\ast\hookrightarrow V^\ast$ for equations with locally monotone drift. Starting from a tight sequence of approximating solutions in $D([0,T];H)\cap L^α(0,T;V),$ we construct, on the represented probability space, a time-homogeneous Poisson random measure with the original Lévy intensity and compensator, compatible with the limiting filtration, such that the limiting process solves the corresponding SPDE.
  The main ingredient is a noise bridge. Together with a shifted dyadic approximation of the solution, the increments of the solution path over dyadic time cells approximate the compensated noise increments; since the time integral of the drift is continuous in $H$, no regularisation of the drift is needed. The jumps are then recovered by a measurable registration procedure, while injectivity of the jump coefficient permits reconstruction of the corresponding marks through a Borel inverse obtained from the Lusin--Suslin theorem. The reconstruction is performed simultaneously at all truncation levels; consistency of the resulting finite jump measures and a monotone patching argument yield a Poisson random measure with the full Lévy measure. Under the injectivity assumption, no enlargement of the represented probability space is required.

Probability.title: Stochastic flows for SDEs with critically low regularity growing drifts in Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini spaces
Probability.summary: We study stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with critically low regularity drifts in a Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini class. Under suitable slowly varying and Hölder--Dini-type assumptions on the modulus of continuity, we prove that SDEs with linearly growing drifts in the critical class $L^p\big([0,T];{\mathcal C}^{\frac{2}{p}-1,ρ}_{l,d}(\mathbb{R}^n;\mathbb{R}^n)\big)$, $p\in(1,2]$, generate a unique stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. The proof relies on a maximal regularity theory for parabolic equations in non-divergence form with Lebesgue--Hölder--Dini coefficients, which enables us to apply the Itô--Tanaka trick and reduce the original SDE to one with Lipschitz coefficients.

Probability.title: Random walk on an induced component of the uniform spanning forest
Probability.summary: Let $T$ be the component of the origin in the uniform spanning forest of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and consider the induced graph $H$ obtained by retaining every lattice edge with both endpoints in $T$. Lyons, Peres and Sun (2020) showed that $H$ is recurrent if $d \ge 8$ and asked for which $d \in \{5,6,7\}$ this holds. We prove that simple random walk on $H$ is transient for $d=5$ and recurrent for every $d\ge6$. We also show that the quenched return probabilities to the origin satisfy $p^H_{2n}(o,o)=n^{-α_d+o(1)}$ a.s., where $α_5=4/3$ and $α_6=1$, while $α_7=4/5$ and $α_d=2/3$ for all $d\ge8$.

Probability.title: Stochastic extinction: convergence in distribution
Probability.summary: We develop a general framework to show the convergence in distribution of non-irreducible Markov processes to invariant distributions supported on lower-dimensional subsets of the state space. In applications, these singular supports signal the emergence of distinctive long-time behaviours, such as the extinction of species in ecology and the concentration on laminar states in fluid dynamics. The proposed approach is made widely applicable by tailoring its assumptions so that they can be verified using the theory of stochastic persistence/extinction. We illustrate the framework by applying it to stochastic perturbations of the Lorenz and Rosenzweig-MacArthur models and to a general two-dimensional Kolmogorov system.

Probability.title: Lower deviations for the maximum of a branching random walk in a random environment in time: quenched versus annealed
Probability.summary: We study lower deviations of the rightmost position in a supercritical branching random walk whose offspring laws are independent and identically distributed across generations. Every particle has at least one child, and displacements have a fixed law with finite exponential moments of all orders. For thresholds strictly between the lower endpoint of the step law and the speed of the maximum, the quenched lower deviation probability has a finite positive exponential rate precisely when the negative logarithm of the probability of a single child is integrable. We identify the rate by a variational formula. If a positive fraction of generations rule out single children and displacements are bounded below, the probability decays doubly exponentially. We compute its double-exponential rate in terms of the minimum offspring numbers, the lower endpoint of the displacement law, and the speed of the maximum. After averaging over the environment, the negative logarithm of the probability is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the generation number whenever single children are possible with positive probability. We obtain the exact exponential rate when the offspring mean is constant and the offspring second moments are uniformly bounded. With displacements bounded below, mixed environments thus yield double-exponential quenched decay and single-exponential annealed decay.
Probability.comment: 21 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to Journal of Theoretical Probability. Code and numerical data are provided as ancillary files

Probability.title: Weak monotonicity, Critical exponents, and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities on weighted graphs
Probability.summary: We study weak monotonicity of heat kernel and ball averaged functionals on weighted graphs, and the associated critical exponents. Under sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates, weak Bakry-Émery estimates for the semigroup are proved, with explicit values of the Hölder regularity exponent in the strongly recurrent case. Applications of the theory include Gagliardo-Nirenberg, Sobolev, Nash and isoperimetric inequalities on strongly recurrent graphs and their products.

Probability.title: Fixed-level profiles and fluctuations in age-dependent recursive trees
Probability.summary: How many vertices of a growing recursive tree lie at a prescribed distance from the root? We compare two linear attachment rules. When an arriving vertex chooses a parent with probability proportional to its label, each fixed level eventually stops growing. We determine the limiting covariance kernel and the probability that a level will change again after time $n$. Writing $L_\infty(h)$ for its final size, we show that $2^{-h}L_\infty(h)$ converges in mean square as $h$ tends to infinity to a random variable with mean $1$ and variance $1/3$. Consequently the limiting variance of the level size is asymptotic to $4^h/3$. When parents are chosen with probability proportional to their age, each fixed level grows. Its centered fluctuations have a joint Gaussian limit whose covariance constants come from repeated logarithmic integration of attachment noise at the root. An exact finite-size calculation illustrates the difference between the limiting and finite-size variances.

Probability.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
Probability.summary: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.

Probability.title: Sampling with graph wavelet kernels: optimality and adaptivity to regularity and geometry
Probability.summary: We construct wavelet-based determinantal samplers on manifolds and geometric graphs whose approximation rates adapt to the regularity of the observable. On a Riemannian manifold of dimension $m$, our wavelet DPPs satisfy variance reduction of order $n^{1-2s/m}$ for linear statistics of both $s$-Hölder and $H^s$ observables, where $0<s\le1$. Using these samplers, we further construct unbiased quadrature rules with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$ using at most $3n/2$ function evaluations, matching the classical optimal randomized integration exponent. For point clouds sampled from an $m$-dimensional manifold, we develop corresponding determinantal samplers on two standard classes of geometric random graphs: $\varepsilon$-graphs and symmetric $k$-nearest-neighbour graphs. These samplers satisfy the same variance reduction for linear statistics of $s$-Hölder observables and yield conditionally unbiased estimators of empirical averages with root mean square error $O(n^{-1/2-s/m})$, using at most $2n$ function evaluations. In both settings, the rates are governed by the intrinsic dimension $m$ and the regularity $s$ of the observable.

Probability.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
Probability.summary: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points. We prove that the sign of each passive eigenvalue equals the sign of the extinct species' density in the enlarged community, that every partial community containing $X_1$ is a saddle with one unstable direction for each extinct consumer, and that the coexistence state is the only stable fixed point. A WKB treatment of the master equation gives a $2N$-dimensional Hamiltonian whose fluctuational fixed points are obtained in closed form. The resulting extinction network has $3^{N-1}$ fluctuation-driven transitions, and its coarse-grained dynamics yield an exact recursion for every mean extinction time. We analyse the three-species omnivory module in full, including a minimal set of existence conditions, global stability of coexistence, numerical instanton actions for all nine transitions and the most probable extinction route, which we confirm with stochastic simulations. Finally, we show how deleting a single trophic link reshapes the extinction network.

Probability.title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
Probability.summary: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast iteration to control a certain fluid-scaled relative entropy error that arises in the ODE approximation. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm and compare it with the existing risk-sensitive Q-learning algorithms.

Differential Geometry.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
Differential Geometry.summary: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $ι$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichmüller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $α$-bundles and $β$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $α$ and $β$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $β$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_β$-Anosov and $α$-bundles are $P_α$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $σ\in \{α, β\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_σ)$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_σ(ρ)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $ρ:π_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $σ$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $ρ$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $π_1({\mathscr{M}}_σ(ρ))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $ρ$ in the space of $P_σ$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_σ$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.
Differential Geometry.comment: 55 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. No AI proof assistance. Expositional improvements to the introduction from v1

Differential Geometry.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
Differential Geometry.comment: 8 pages. v2: Fixed orientation consistency issues and typos

Differential Geometry.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.

Differential Geometry.title: Cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

Differential Geometry.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
Differential Geometry.summary: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.
Differential Geometry.comment: 9 pages, including three appendices. Revised proof with exact second-jet prescription for smooth metrics, fixed-support Gram lifts, and a self-contained finite-field proof of characteristic regularity

Differential Geometry.title: Time-optimal travel driven by two vector fields on a Riemannian manifold
Differential Geometry.summary: We study minimum-time travel on a Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ for a kinematic model in which finitely many drift fields contribute additively to the velocity, after independent rescaling of their components parallel and orthogonal to a chosen unit direction $u$. The velocity is then $\mathcal Y_x(u)=(η(x)+h_x(\widehat Z_x,u))u+\widehat W_x$, $u\in UT_xM$, for two effective vector fields $\widehat Z$, $\widehat W$ and a self-propulsion speed $η\geq0$. Let $F$ be the gauge of the radial hull $\mathcal B_x=[0,1]\cdot\mathcal S_x$ of the velocity set $\mathcal S_x=\mathcal Y_x(UT_xM)$. Where $η>0$, we characterize when $F$ is a Finsler metric and give two-sided estimates and representation formulae for it; where $η=0$ and $\widehat Z\neq0$, we recover the Randers, Kropina and strong-wind regimes of Zermelo navigation. Examples include Matsumoto's slope metric, traction-modified slope models, and alternative models for wildfire propagation and microswimmer navigation. Since $F$ need not be a Finsler metric, we treat the minimum-time problem with tools from differential inclusions. For distinct endpoints, the inclusions defined by $\mathcal S_x$ and $\mathcal B_x$ give the same infimum travel time, and so does the convex hull of $\mathcal B_x$ under local controllability at the terminal point. When $F$ is finite, the infimum is attained if $(M,h)$ is complete, $\mathcal Y$ is bounded and each $\mathcal B_x$ is convex. When $F$ is a Finsler metric on $\{η>0\}$, the set $\{η=0\}$ cannot be reached from $\{η>0\}$ in finite time and, on $\{η>0\}$, the minimum time is the Finsler distance; if moreover $(M,h)$ is complete and $η$ is bounded, $F$ is forward and backward complete and the minimum time is attained by geodesics. We also compute the support Hamiltonian directly from the velocity law, for every $η\geq0$.

Differential Geometry.title: Left-Invariant Kundt Structures on Almost Abelian Lie Groups
Differential Geometry.summary: We study left-invariant Kundt structures on almost abelian Lie groups. We establish algebraic existence criteria and characterize the admissible real Jordan forms according to the signature of the Abelian ideal. We then characterize the Kundt pairs defining pp-waves and plane waves in arbitrary dimension, with particular attention to recurrent and parallel null directions. Examples in dimension four illustrate both plane and non-plane pp-wave geometries.

Differential Geometry.title: Einstein manifolds and extended Poincaré algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: For any pseudo-Euclidean space $V \simeq \mathbb{R}^{p, q}, p \geq 3$, module $W$ over the even Clifford algebra $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$ and $V$-valued skew-symmetric bilinear $\mathfrak{so}(V)$-equivariant form $Π$ on $W$, V. Córtes constructed noncompact quaternion-pseudo-Kähler homogeneous space. In particular, such homogeneous space is always Einstein and for $p=3$ it is Riemannian. The current paper is devoted to the generalization of this construction for $p = 3$ to the case $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and an irreducible $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$-module. As a result we construct the new series of Riemannian Einstein homogoneous spaces $M_{p, q}$ with negative scalar curvature.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of submanifolds under extrinsic curvature pinching
Differential Geometry.summary: We investigate the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds whose curvature operator is bounded below by a nonnegative constant, under pointwise pinching conditions involving the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to many earlier results, we allow equality in these conditions without imposing additional assumptions on the mean curvature or restricting the fundamental group of the submanifold. Allowing equality reveals geometric and topological phenomena excluded by strict pinching. We establish classification theorems in all dimensions $n\geq4$, describing the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of such submanifolds. Our results also provide substantial information about the extrinsic geometry of the immersions, including precise conclusions concerning relative nullity, Dupin principal normals, and total geodesicity. As applications, we derive rigidity and sphere theorems for submanifolds of space forms and construct families of examples showing that the pinching conditions do not, in general, imply extrinsic rigidity. These results extend and refine several known rigidity theorems by providing a classification of the equality cases in a general ambient setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Tian-Yau-type metrics from K3 divisors with ADE contractions
Differential Geometry.summary: We construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler metrics on the complement of a smooth anti-canonical K3 divisor in a compact Kähler threefold, assuming that the normal bundle of the divisor is nef and big. Such a metric exists in every Kähler class whose exceptional periods are positive. We use a generalized Gibbons-Hawking ansatz to construct an approximate model on the normal bundle. When the normal bundle contracts an ADE configuration, this model combines an expanding Ricci-flat orbifold K3 metric with ALE metrics whose exceptional periods remain fixed. After improving the model by a finite iteration and transferring it to the divisor complement, we apply the Tian-Yau-Hein existence theorem.

Differential Geometry.title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
Differential Geometry.summary: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

Differential Geometry.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

Differential Geometry.title: Existence of complete singular solutions of the Yamabe equation at prescribed points
Differential Geometry.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be smooth, connected and closed, with $n\ge3$, and let $P$ be a prescribed nonempty finite set. We characterize the conformal classes $[g]$ that admit a complete metric of positive constant scalar curvature on $M\setminus P$. Such a metric exists precisely when $Y(M,[g])>0$ and either $[g]$ is nonround or $|P|\ge2$. In a nonround positive conformal class, the metrics can be chosen with Fowler asymptotics and arbitrary fixed ratios of their small asymptotic neck sizes. As the neck sizes tend to zero, every sequence of these metrics has a subsequence converging smoothly away from the punctures to a smooth Yamabe minimizing metric. The construction allows degenerate Yamabe minimizers and arbitrary curvature jets at the prescribed points. For nonempty closed singular sets $Λ\subset M$ with empty interior, we also announce the same existence criterion with the additional requirement that the Bessel capacity $C_{1+2/n,n/2}(Λ)$ vanish.

Differential Geometry.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
Differential Geometry.summary: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.
Differential Geometry.comment: 49 pages, LaTeX, 5 figures, minor changes (published version)

Differential Geometry.title: The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation
Differential Geometry.summary: We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.

Differential Geometry.title: Integrability and closed spacelike extremals of conformal arclength in the Einstein universe
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the conformal arclength functional for nondegenerate spacelike curves in the three-dimensional Einstein universe and classify its closed extremals up to conformal equivalence. We show that the extremals are projections of trajectories of a generically noncommutatively integrable Reeb flow. For extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants, closedness forces negative helicity and regular elliptic momentum. We prove that the restricted moment map over the corresponding invariant region defines a nontrivial principal $\mathbb T^3$-bundle, and construct explicit local trivializations that linearize the Reeb flow. This yields explicit parametrizations in terms of elliptic functions and integrals. We prove that the associated period map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto a bounded, convex planar domain whose rational points parametrize the conformal equivalence classes of closed extremals with nonconstant conformal invariants. We conclude with a study of the global geometry of closed extremals.

Differential Geometry.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on polarized manifolds
Differential Geometry.summary: In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system $T$ on the space of Fubini--Study metrics of a polarized manifold $(X,L)$, whose fixed points are the balanced metrics. In \cite{S}, Sano proves that the iterates of $T$ converge to a balanced metric, provided that a balanced metric exists and the automorphism group of $(X,L)$ is discrete modulo scalars. We remove the assumption on the automorphism group. Moreover, we show that the convergence is exponential with the optimal rate $ρ_*$ given by the linearization of $T$ at a balanced metric, which extends a result of Ioos and Polterovich (\cite{IP}) for discrete automorphism groups. We compute $ρ_*$ for $(\CP^n,\mathcal{O}(d))$ and $(\CP^1\times\CP^1,\mathcal{O}(d,d))$; for $\CP^1$ this confirms the rate obtained numerically by Sherman (\cite{Sh}).

Differential Geometry.title: Numerical algorithm for finding balanced metrics on vector bundles II: the non-simple case
Differential Geometry.summary:
In \cite{D3}, Donaldson defines a dynamical system on the space of Fubini-Study metrics on a polarized compact Kähler manifold. Sano proved that if there exists a balanced metric for the polarization, then this dynamical system always converges to the balanced metric provided that the automorphism group is discrete (\cite{S}).
  In \cite{DKLR}, Douglas, et.\ al., conjecture that the same holds in the case of vector bundles. In \cite{Se}, we proved their conjecture under the assumption that the bundle is simple. In this note, we remove the simplicity assumption. The main tool is Thompson's metric on the space of Hermitian inner products on the space of holomorphic sections, with respect to which the generalized $T$-operator is non-expanding.

Differential Geometry.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.
Differential Geometry.comment: 72 pages, 1 figure. The computational supplement (verification programs, certificates, reference logs) is included as ancillary files (see also Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24473074). v2: editorial corrections (explicit constant in the main theorem, notation and terminology, a few proof steps made explicit); results, numbering and ancillary files unchanged

Differential Geometry.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
Differential Geometry.summary: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $dΦ=θ\wedgeΦ$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $θ$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_θ\colonΓ(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\toΓ(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_θ$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|θ|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenböck formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.
Differential Geometry.comment: 14 pages. v2: substantially revised; incorrect rigidity statement and the Sp(2)/T^2 example removed; new main result (Theorem 6.3) on product manifolds N x S^1

Differential Geometry.title: Curvature inequalities and rigidity for constant mean curvature and spacetime constant mean curvature surfaces
Differential Geometry.summary:
We establish curvature inequalities and rigidity results for constant mean curvature (CMC) surfaces in Riemannian manifolds and spacetime constant mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces in Lorentzian manifolds. In three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we show that the Christodoulou-Yau inequality $H^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$ ($H$ denoting mean curvature and $|Σ|$ area) for stable CMC spheres also holds for CMC surfaces of arbitrary topology under a new stability condition controlling only the constant mode of the second variation of area. Under an extrinsic curvature sign condition, equality forces the enclosed region to be Euclidean without additional intrinsic assumptions. We extend these results to higher dimensions and to the hyperbolic and spherical settings.
  In the Lorentzian setting, we develop a variational stability theory for STCMC surfaces based on the second variation of area in the mean curvature vector direction. We introduce two independent stability notions: variational stability, which recovers classical volume-preserving CMC stability for surfaces in totally geodesic spacelike hypersurfaces, and constant-mode stability. Under the dominant energy condition, either yields the sharp inequality $|\vec H|^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$. In the equality case, under suitable geometric assumptions, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the enclosed spacelike region is a Minkowski causal diamond. These results imply nonnegativity and rigidity of the Hawking quasi-local energy for stable STCMC surfaces. Finally, we analyze known spacelike and null STCMC foliations, showing that asymptotic leaves are stable under positive mass conditions, whereas the local matter density and trace-free extrinsic curvature govern the instability of local foliations.
Differential Geometry.comment: 40 pages. Substantially revised version. The variational stability condition has been reformulated to recover classical volume-preserving CMC stability exactly in the time-symmetric setting for nonminimal surfaces. The two stability notions are now independent, the curvature inequalities hold under weaker variational stability assumptions

Differential Geometry.title: Veronese Classification of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics
Differential Geometry.summary: We prove that every linearly full, irreducible conformal minimal immersion of constant Gaussian curvature and finite isotropy order from the two-sphere into a complex hyperquadric comes from a member of a Veronese sequence. The result holds at every finite isotropy order, without an unramifiedness or additional Frenet-norm polynomiality assumption. Both the associated projective harmonic sequence and the target harmonic sequence are totally unramified as consequences. If the replacement depth is \(\ell\) and the holomorphic seed spans \(\mathbb{CP}^m\), the curvature is \(K=2/((2\ell+1)m-2\ell^2)\) in the Grassmannian normalization. Real Gram data characterize the admissible embeddings and give an algebraic converse. The proof uses holomorphic Pfaffian norm identities, degree estimates that retain all ramification divisors, and a valuation argument that identifies the retained lines with seed Frenet lines.

Differential Geometry.title: Rigidity of Constant-Curvature Minimal Two-Spheres in Complex Hyperquadrics at Isotropy Order $n-6$
Differential Geometry.summary: We classify linearly full, irreducible, totally unramified conformal minimal two-spheres of constant Gaussian curvature in the real Grassmannian $G(2,n;\mathbb R)$, or equivalently in the complex hyperquadric $Q_{n-2}$, whose finite isotropy order is $n-6$, where $n\geq7$. We remove the additional polynomiality assumption on a Frenet norm in the earlier classification of Li and Jiao. An exterior-product norm identity reduces the problem to the multiplicity of the irreducible polynomial $1+zw$; a further divisibility argument handles the boundary dimension $n=7$, including isotropy order one. The dimension $n$ is necessarily odd, and the immersion is congruent, after a conformal reparametrization, to the second member of a Veronese sequence with its prescribed real structure. Its curvature is $2/(5n-13)$ in the Grassmannian normalization. An explicit model in $Q_5$ illustrates the boundary case and its harmonic sequence.

Differential Geometry.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
Differential Geometry.summary: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.

Differential Geometry.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
Differential Geometry.summary: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

Differential Geometry.title: Nice bases for Lie algebras
Differential Geometry.summary: The concept of a nice basis for a Lie algebra was introduced to study the Ricci curvature on nilpotent Lie groups equipped with a left-invariant metric. Despite the many applications in differential geometry, for example in the construction of Einstein manifolds, very little is known about the existence and number of nice bases on a given Lie algebra. This paper studies this question for three classes of Lie algebras, namely direct sums, almost abelian ones and nilpotent Lie algebras associated to a graph. As an application we compute the number of nice bases for Lie algebras up to dimension $3$, and show that for a general Lie algebra the existence depends on the field over which it is defined. Moreover, for every natural number $n$ we give an indecomposable Lie algebra such that there exists exactly $n$ nice bases up to equivalence.
